title: 317 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 317 Dundas Street West to permit a six-storey, 48.35-metre addition in the parking area at the southeast corner of the Art Gallery of Ontario site, adding about 4,600 square metres of new gallery space. The Grange heritage building and Grange Park are not affected.

title: Parking Amendments - Conducting a new poll on Maclean Avenue
topics: parking;
brief: Councillor Bradford recommends City Council set aside the May-June 2023 parking poll on Maclean Avenue and direct a new poll, at the request of local residents. The original poll met the response threshold but fell short of 50 percent plus one in favour despite more yes than no votes, and one ballot was returned by a deceased individual.

title: Distillery Winter Village - Waiving of Parking Fees
topics: parking fees; parking charges; parking rates
brief: Deputy Mayor Malik recommends City Council ask the Toronto Parking Authority board to waive about $44,100 in lost pay-and-display parking revenue as part of the 2023 Distillery Winter Village. The event draws over 750,000 visitors a year and is described as Canada's premier holiday market; fee waivers were granted in prior years.

title: 8-18 Camden Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 8-18 Camden Street to permit a 19-storey mixed-use building with 191 homes and 308 square metres of ground-floor retail. The proposal is described as fitting within the existing and planned context.

title: By-law changes to reflect the new conditions after the King Street West, Queen Street West, The Queensway and Roncesvalles Avenue construction
topics: reconstruction; rebuilding
brief: Councillor Perks recommends City Council amend stopping and parking prohibitions on Roncesvalles Avenue to resolve discrepancies between by-laws and signage, following the imminent completion of the King Street West, Queen Street West, The Queensway and Roncesvalles Avenue intersection reconstruction.

title: 150 Sterling Road (Block 3B of 158 Sterling Road) - Zoning By-law Amendment Application (Removal of the Holding Symbol "H") - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve removing the holding symbol from the zoning for 150 Sterling Road (Block 3B of 158 Sterling Road), to permit a 14-storey mixed-use building with non-residential uses including a 36-space child care facility on the first and second floors. The report outlines the status of the conditions for removing the holding symbol.

title: Re-allocating dormant Section 37 funds within Ward 11
topics: community benefits;
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends City Council direct the Chief Planner to bring forward city-initiated zoning by-law amendments to reallocate dormant Section 37 funds in Ward 11 toward affordable housing. The funds come from developments approved between 1988 and 2013 and were never used for their original purposes, which are now complete, elsewhere, or impractical.

title: Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Regulations - 1245 Dupont Street
topics: traffic regulations, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize installing traffic control signals at the intersections of Dupont Street with Galleria Road/Private Access and with Radiator Street, plus related traffic regulations. The signals are conditions of approval for the Galleria redevelopment at 1245 Dupont Street, which will bring over 2,800 new homes plus retail, office and community uses. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Dufferin and Dupont Streets.

title: 209 Mavety Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment to permit a Community Health Centre at 209 Mavety Street through an interior retrofit and renovation of the existing city-owned building. In 2021 Council authorized a community space tenancy lease with Four Villages Community Health Centre, a not-for-profit serving Toronto West residents.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 5H to Exclude the Development Located at 1080-1088 Yonge Street
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve realigning Permit Parking Area 5H to exclude the development at 1080-1088 Yonge Street, responding to Council's direction to review the matter. Staff found the realignment feasible and have no objections; residents and visitors of the development would no longer be eligible for the area's permits. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Yonge Street.

title: On-Street Electric Vehicle Charging Station on O'Connor Drive - Parking Amendments (Non-Delegated Location)
topics: by-laws, parking, stations; bylaws
brief: Staff recommend City Council designate on-street electric vehicle charging station parking areas on the east side of O'Connor Drive, 73 metres north of St Clair Avenue East (2 spaces), for the exclusive use of electric vehicles, as part of a dual-pedestal charging station rollout. The location was reviewed and supported by the local councillor. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on the road.

title: Pay-and-Display Parking - Dufferin Street
topics: on-street parking, permit parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council approve installing on-street paid parking on the east side of Dufferin Street between Rogers Road and Eversfield Road, to offset parking lost from the closure of Municipal Car Park 670. Staff and the Toronto Parking Authority reviewed the segment for functionally safe and economically viable parking areas. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Dufferin Street.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - November 2023 (Non-Delegated)
topics: on-street parking, parking spaces; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, parking spots
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize installing on-street accessible parking spaces for persons with disabilities at the locations listed in the report's attachment. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on the subject streets.

title: 403 Keele Street and 48-50 Heintzman Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, zoning, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 403 Keele Street and 48-50 Heintzman Street to permit an 11-storey mixed-use building with 280 rental dwelling units and 265 square metres of commercial space at grade, plus one level of underground parking with 23 spaces. The proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy and an appropriate transition to the lower-scale Neighbourhoods along Heintzman Street.

title: 1404-1428 Yonge Street - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, on-street parking, parking machines; building, curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize closing the west sidewalk, the southbound and northbound bike lanes, and a 2.8-metre-wide portion of the southbound lane on Yonge Street near St Clair Avenue West for 35 months, from November 30, 2023 to October 31, 2026, to facilitate construction staging for YSC Development Corp's 50-storey condo at 1404-1428 Yonge Street. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Yonge Street.

title: 321 Davenport Road - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, street occupation permits; building, curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize temporarily closing the south sidewalk, parking lane, bicycle lane and eastbound lane on Davenport Road, between a point 82 metres west of Bedford Road and a point 30 metres further west, for 8 months from December 14, 2023 to July 31, 2024, to facilitate construction staging for a 9-storey condo at 321 Davenport Road. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Davenport Road.

title: Construction Staging Area - Lake Shore Boulevard West (955 Lake Shore Boulevard West)
topics: permits, site plan control; permit renewal, site plan approvals
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize closing a 3.5-metre-wide portion of the eastbound curb lane on Lake Shore Boulevard West, between Ontario Drive and a point 126 metres east, from December 18, 2023 to March 1, 2024, to facilitate EllisDon Civil's Infrastructure Ontario Ontario Place site servicing renewal project, including watermain and sanitary work under the Martin Goodman Trail. Council approval is needed for closures over 30 days on a major arterial.

title: 3524 Dundas Street West - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction; building
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize closing the north sidewalk and the north side westbound curb lane on Dundas Street West, between a point 128 metres east of Jane Street and a point 45.75 metres further east, for 9 months from December 31, 2023 to October 1, 2024, to facilitate construction staging for a 6-storey self-storage building at 3524 Dundas Street West. A temporary pedestrian walkway would be provided.

title: 2760 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, zoning, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 2760 Dundas Street West to permit a 6-storey mixed-use building with 28 dwelling units and 114 square metres of commercial space at grade, plus one level of underground parking with 16 spaces. The proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy and an appropriate scale for the site.

title: 90, 90A, 92 and 94 Isabella Street - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreements
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 90, 90A, 92 and 94 Isabella Street, including a pair of 1888-1889 semi-detached houses and an 1885 house, to allow construction of a new 69-storey building on the lands. The board is also asked to authorize heritage easement agreements.

title: 306-310 Gerrard Street East - Erection of a building on a Heritage Property Designated under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the erection of a new 10-storey (plus mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building at 306-310 Gerrard Street East, in the Cabbagetown South Heritage Conservation District. The proposal would replace three existing buildings and a surface parking lot; Council approval is required for the new building under the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 685 Lake Shore Boulevard East - Applications for Zoning By-law Amendment and Site Plan Control - Appeal Report
topics: site plan control, zoning; site plan approvals
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed zoning and site plan applications for 685 Lake Shore Boulevard East in the Port Lands' McCleary District, and to continue discussions with the applicant. The revised proposal has 38- and 43-storey residential towers with 899 condo units; the applicant appealed on July 10, 2023.

title: 15 Richmond Street East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed Official Plan and zoning amendment application for 15 Richmond Street East, and to continue discussions with the applicant. The proposal is a 71-storey mixed-use building with 565 homes that would retain the existing 21-storey building; the applicant appealed on August 9, 2023.

title: 396-398 Church Street, 73-77 McGill Street and 50 Gerrard Street East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal to oppose the appealed Official Plan and zoning amendment application for 396-398 Church Street, 73-77 McGill Street and 50 Gerrard Street East in its current form. The proposal is a 43-storey residential building with ground-floor retail and 463 homes; the applicant appealed on July 7, 2023 after Council did not decide within the Planning Act timeframe.

title: 141 Roehampton Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed zoning application for 141 Roehampton Avenue. The applicant revised the proposal from a 48-storey building with 614 homes to a 58-storey building with 809 homes, then appealed on May 24, 2023.

title: 219-221 Roxton Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed Official Plan and zoning amendment application for 219-221 Roxton Road, and to continue discussions with the applicant. The applicant revised the proposal from a 6-storey to a 12-storey mixed-use building with 33 homes, then appealed on June 1, 2023 after Council did not make a decision.

title: 276-294 Main Street - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: site plan control, zoning bylaws; site plan approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council enact a Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for 276-294 Main Street to permit dividing the site into four lots and transferring ownership into stratified parcels. The exemption implements the site-specific zoning and site plan approvals for the site, and the owner would register a Section 118 restriction under the Land Titles Act.

title: 1233-1243 Queen Street East and 77 Leslie Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments for 1233-1243 Queen Street East and 77 Leslie Street to permit a 9-storey mixed-use building with 142 rental homes and 385.8 square metres of retail and commercial space. The design includes a commemorative public space at Queen and Leslie celebrating the history of the former China Lily site.

title: 184 Chatham Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 184 Chatham Avenue to permit a 4-storey residential building, 12.3 metres tall, with 34 condo units. The proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy and fitting the surrounding context.

title: 410 Sherbourne Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning by-law amendment to permit a 42-storey mixed-use building with 473 dwelling units at 410 Sherbourne Street. The existing live music venue and four-storey office building would be demolished.

title: 383 and 387 Sherbourne Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, demolitions; application process
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the rental housing demolition application for 387 Sherbourne Street, allowing demolition of a 3-storey building with 44 rental units, to be replaced within a new 39-storey building of 346 homes. The adjacent 32-unit building at 383 Sherbourne Street would be extensively renovated and retained. The related zoning application was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, which issued a written decision.

title: 307 Sherbourne Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council amend the site-specific Zoning By-law 1192-2020 for 307 Sherbourne Street, following a 2020 Tribunal approval for a 15-storey mixed-use building, to permit a privately owned and operated student residence, increase the number of permitted dwelling units, reduce minimum parking requirements, and increase the maximum building height.

title: 90-94 Isabella Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 90-94 Isabella Street to permit a 69-storey residential building with 831 units. The site has two Part IV-designated heritage buildings; the front 10 metres of each would be retained in place and the rear portions demolished, and a rear row of townhouses is not heritage-designated.

title: 306-310 Gerrard Street East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments to re-designate 310 Gerrard Street East from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Areas and permit a 10-storey mixed-use building with office, retail and residential uses at 306-310 Gerrard Street East. The proposal includes 194 homes, including affordable rental units through the City's Open Door Program.

title: 1-7 Yonge Street, Phases 2 and 3 - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments for 1-7 Yonge Street, Phases 2 and 3, to permit adding 10 and 12 storeys to the previously approved development. The proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy and increases the number of affordable housing units in Phase 3.

title: 822-838 Richmond Street West Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments for 822-838 Richmond Street West to permit an 8-storey residential building with 26 rental homes, with a holding provision in place until the owner delivers updated servicing reports. The proposal is described as fitting the existing and planned context with an improved public realm.

title: 19-21 Ossington Avenue and 19 Rebecca Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 19-21 Ossington Avenue and 19 Rebecca Street to legalize an existing 16-space commercial surface parking lot. No physical changes to the existing building are proposed, and the proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy and the Growth Plan.

title: 600 King Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment  Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 600 King Street West to permit a 5-storey addition to an existing heritage-designated building for entirely non-residential uses, including a restaurant, private club and hotel. The proposal includes no vehicle parking and nine bicycle parking spaces.

title: 238 Ellerslie Avenue - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 23 197199 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee (North York Panel) will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued September 11, 2023 for 238 Ellerslie Avenue (file 23 197199 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order.

title: 100 Graydon Hall Drive - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 23 217431 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee (North York Panel) will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued October 24, 2023 for 100 Graydon Hall Drive (file 23 217431 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order.

title: 19 Charleswood Drive - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 23 209582 PRS 00 IV
topics: by-laws, compliance, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee (North York Panel) will hear the property owner's appeal of a property standards order issued October 2, 2023 for 19 Charleswood Drive (file 23 209582 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order.

title: Council Member Appointment to fill a Vacancy on the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board of Directors
topics: board members, public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Clerk recommends the Striking Committee consider members' preferences and recommend one Council Member to City Council to fill the vacancy on the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board left by Councillor Jon Burnside's resignation, for a term until December 31, 2024. City Council makes the final appointment.

title: Council Member Appointments to the City-School Boards Advisory Committee
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Clerk recommends the Striking Committee consider members' preferences and recommend four Council Members to City Council for appointment to the City-School Boards Advisory Committee, for terms until December 31, 2024. City Council makes the final appointments.

title: Birchmount Road and Chaldean Street/Glendower Circuit - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, road safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo
brief: Transportation Services reviewed the need for pedestrian crossing protection at Birchmount Road and Chaldean Street/Glendower Circuit and does not recommend a pedestrian crossover or traffic signals because the warrant criteria were not met. Staff recommend City Council not authorize the installation. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Birchmount Road.

title: 4674 Kingston Road - Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to Kingston Residences Inc.'s appealed zoning application for 4674 Kingston Road. The proposal is a 13-storey mixed-use building with 483 homes and a floor space index of 3.87; the owner appealed on July 28, 2023 after Council did not make a decision.

title: 1001 Ellesmere Road - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: part lot control, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: Staff recommend City Council enact a Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for part of 1001 Ellesmere Road to create 24 separately conveyable townhouse parcels. The lands are Block 3 of a subdivision registered June 12, 2019, which also created a 1,320 square metre public park on Block 5; earlier exemptions in the same subdivision created 45 townhouse lots.

title: 20 Stonehill Court - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for infill development at 20 Stonehill Court to permit a 29-storey residential building facing Warden Avenue and an 11-storey mixed-use building facing Finch Avenue East, while retaining the existing 13-storey rental apartment building at the centre of the site. The proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy and the Official Plan.

title: 150 Clonmore Drive - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve a zoning amendment for 150 Clonmore Drive to permit a 12-storey residential building with 290 homes, a gross floor area of 18,144 square metres, 162 vehicle parking spaces and 248 bicycle parking spaces. The proposal is described as consistent with provincial policy and the Growth Plan.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will review the Order Paper.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements will be made at the City Council meeting.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council will declare interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council receives the introduction of committee reports and new business from city officials, including reports from the Executive, Audit, Civic Appointments, and Economic and Community Development Committees.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from its regular meeting held November 8 and 9, 2023.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: Acquisition of Affordable Housing Development Project at 355 Coxwell Avenue
topics: affordable housing, land acquisition; affordable homes; housing projects, land acquisitions; park acquisition; parkland acquisition; parks acquisitions; property acquisition; property acquisitions
brief: The Executive Directors of the Housing Secretariat and Corporate Real Estate Management recommend City Council authorize negotiating the purchase of the vacant development site at 355 Coxwell Avenue for an affordable housing project, using the Development Charges Reserve Fund for Subsidized Housing. The project was approved for Open Door funding and incentives in 2021 and has a notice of approval conditions from City Planning.

title: Implementing Bill 109 - 2023 Annual Update
topics: legislation, urban planning; acts, city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: This is an information item: the 2023 annual update on implementing provincial Bill 109, the More Homes for Everyone Act, adopted by Council in December 2022. Work has focused on good city-building outcomes and protecting cost recovery for development review services, while revealing unintended consequences of the legislated review timelines. Council is asked to request the Minister consult the City before issuing related draft regulations.

title: Growing Space for Trees: Protecting and Enhancing the Tree Canopy While Supporting Infill Housing
topics: green standards, trees; ash trees, green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards
brief: Staff recommend City Council ask the Chief Planner, with Parks, Forestry and Recreation, to review Official Plan policies on protecting tree canopy and growing space for trees while supporting infill housing in low-rise neighbourhoods. Trees are described as critical to addressing the climate and biodiversity crisis, while infill housing risks reducing canopy and growing space.

title: Housing Action Plan: Zoning By-law Simplification and Modernization for Low-rise Residential Zones - Phase 1 Final Report
topics: by-laws, residential properties; bylaws, residential real estate
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council amend city-wide Zoning By-law 569-2013 to simplify and modernize low-rise residential zoning regulations, as phase 1 of the Housing Action Plan. The changes would remove barriers, ease administration and enable more housing toward the provincial target of 285,000 new homes over 10 years.

title: Supporting Purpose Built Rental Homes in Etobicoke North
topics: redevelopment, rental housing; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization, rental properties; rental units
brief: Councillor Crisanti recommends City Council ask the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing to enact a Minister's Zoning Order to permit the International Muslim Organization to redevelop 65 Rexdale Boulevard, its mosque site since 1994, with a new nine-storey rental building of about 220 units, a public park and a rebuilt mosque. Twenty to thirty percent of the units would be affordable.

title: Saving Iqbal Foods and Supporting Ontario’s Halal Food Supply Chain
topics: expropriations, official plan amendments, rezoning; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Councillors Robinson and Burnside recommend City Council ask the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing to enact an Enhanced Minister's Zoning Order to permit a grocery store at 100 Thorncliffe Park Drive, after Iqbal Foods' facility at 2 Thorncliffe Park Drive was expropriated for a Metrolinx maintenance facility. Iqbal Foods has served Thorncliffe and Flemingdon Park for over 30 years and supplies 80 percent of Ontario's halal food meeting the strictest religious requirements.

title: 699 and 707 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 699 and 707 Yonge Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for their cultural heritage value. The properties on the east side of Yonge Street south of Hayden Street contain a 3-storey building (summary truncated).

title: 119 Church Street, 127 Church Street, and 89 Queen Street East - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 119 Church Street, 127 Church Street and 89 Queen Street East under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for their cultural heritage value. The properties sit diagonally across from the Metropolitan United Church (1870-71).

title: Recommended Amendments to Zoning By-laws for Bars, Restaurants and Entertainment Venues as part of the Night Economy Review - Final Report
topics: economy, entertainment establishments, night, restaurants; cafeterias; dining; eating places; food premises, entertainment facilities
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council adopt zoning by-law amendments to modernize and clarify the rules for bars, restaurants and other entertainment venues, as part of the city's Night Economy Review. Related licensing framework reports went to the Economic and Community Development Committee on November 28, 2023.

title: 171 Lowther Avenue - Property Included on the City's Heritage Register - Consideration of Objection
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Chief Planner recommends that, after considering the property owner's objection under the Ontario Heritage Act, City Council continue to include 171 Lowther Avenue on the City's Heritage Register. The property is a two-and-a-half-storey Queen Anne Revival house built in 1901; Council first added it to the register on July 19, 2023.

title: Implementing Bill 23 - Update on Amendments to the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage preservation, legislation; acts, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: This is an information item: an update on the city's phased implementation of provincial Bill 23's amendments to the Ontario Heritage Act, in force since January 1, 2023, which introduced accelerated timelines for heritage listings and designations and new restrictions on the Heritage Register. Staff recommend reporting back in Q2 2024 on phase two implementation.

title: Amendments to Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 667: Rental Demolition and Conversion By-law
topics: by-laws, demolitions, rental housing; bylaws, rental properties; rental units
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council amend the rental demolition and conversion by-law (Chapter 667), responding to Auditor General recommendations on tenant access to affordable rental replacement housing based on financial need, and improving coordination with the building construction and demolition by-law and clarity for the public. Chapter 667 controls demolition or conversion of residential rental properties.

title: City Comments on the Province’s Proposal to Return 15 Parcels of Land to the Greenbelt and Update Greenbelt Act
topics: conservation, development controlled land; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening, greenbelts
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council support the Province's proposal to return 15 parcels totalling 2,995 hectares (7,400 acres) to the Greenbelt Plan Area, and support Bill 136 bringing the Greenbelt boundaries into the Greenbelt Act. The report frames Greenbelt protection with compact infill development as key to addressing biodiversity loss and climate change.

title: Amendment to Chapter 415, Development of Land of the Toronto Municipal Code - Toronto Green Standard
topics: green standards, municipal codes; green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council amend the Toronto Green Standard sections of the municipal code to clarify interpretation questions and ensure consistent application of the sunset clause for the Green Standard development charge refund program. The amendments improve readability without changing the program's substance.

title: Federal Rapid Housing Initiative - Program Update and Phase Three Implementation
topics: federal governments, housing; homes; residences
brief: The Executive Directors of the Housing Secretariat and Corporate Real Estate Management recommend actions to implement phase three of the federal Rapid Housing Initiative in Toronto, following Council's November 2023 adoption of the generational transformation of the housing system plan. The federal program has supported the City and Indigenous and non-profit partners in building affordable homes; confidential details are in an attachment.

title: Open Door Incentives to Support 856 Affordable Rental Homes
topics: affordable housing, subsidies and grants; affordable homes; housing projects, financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: The Executive Director, Housing Secretariat recommends City Council make affordable rental homes in the listed developments eligible for Open Door program incentives, including waivers of planning, building permit and parkland dedication fees and development charge exemptions, to support 856 affordable rental homes. The Open Door program supports the city's target of approving 65,000 rent-controlled homes by 2030, including 41,000 affordable rental homes.

title: Technical Amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013
topics: change, zoning bylaws; amendments; conversion; modification, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council enact technical amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013 to correct typographical errors, clarify wording and permissions, and adjust zoning and overlay map boundaries. The revisions keep with Council's original intentions and do not change the substance of the by-law.

title: 10-18 Abitibi Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: community councils, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse the Official Plan and zoning amendment applications for 10-18 Abitibi Avenue, which proposed a 50-storey mixed-use building with 534 homes and a floor space index of 16.2. The proposal is described as inconsistent with provincial policy and the Growth Plan. Staff also recommend opposing any appeal to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 34, 36, 40, 42, 46, 48, 52, 54, 58, 60, 64, 66, and 70 Montgomery Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the appealed proposal for a 24-storey mixed-use building with 306 homes and 525 square metres of ground-floor retail at 34-70 Montgomery Avenue, and to continue discussions with the applicant to address outstanding issues. The applicant appealed on June 23, 2023 after Council did not make a decision.

title: 55 Yeomans Road - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: demolitions, heritage conservation districts, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: Staff recommend City Council include the property at 55 Yeomans Road on the City's Heritage Register for its cultural heritage value. The property at Danby Avenue and Yeomans Road is a Modernist-style synagogue, the Beth David B'nai Israel Beth Am Synagogue, completed in 1959 to designs by architect Irving Grossman and artist Graham Coughtry.

title: 4800 Yonge Street - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, construction permits (right-of-way), street occupation permits; building, curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way), curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize the full closure of Bogert Avenue and its north sidewalk, between Yonge Street and a point 68 metres west, for 48 months from December 31, 2023 to December 31, 2027, to facilitate construction staging for Menkes' 49-storey mixed-use building at 4800 Yonge Street. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Yonge Street and Sheppard Avenue West.

title: Dufferin Street - Road Alteration
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, community councils, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, ttc
brief: Transportation Services, on behalf of the TTC, requests City Council approve altering Dufferin Street from Lawrence Avenue West to the south side of Apex Road (260 metres) to provide a queue-jump lane for through buses, also extending the southbound right-turn lane. The queue-jump lane would let 16 southbound buses per hour bypass general traffic and improve transit reliability.

title: Pedestrian Crossing Protection Studies - Bathurst Manor Neighbourhood Mobility Plan
topics: pedestrian crossovers, pedestrian infrastructure, pedestrians, traffic control systems; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, pedestrian network, pedestrianization, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Through the Bathurst Manor Neighbourhood Mobility Plan, Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize traffic control signals at Wilmington Avenue and Codsell Avenue and a pedestrian crossover at Wilson Heights Boulevard and Codsell Avenue. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on both streets.

title: Wilson Avenue and Maniza Road - Traffic Control Signals
topics: community councils, traffic control systems, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation Services reviewed the need for traffic control signals at Wilson Avenue and Maniza Road and does not recommend installation because the warrant criteria were not met. Staff recommend City Council not authorize the signals. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Wilson Avenue.

title: 2 - 12 Oakburn Crescent - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing, rentals, residential properties, residential tenants; rental properties; rental units, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve the rental housing demolition application for 2-12 Oakburn Crescent, allowing demolition of six low-rise rental buildings with 66 rental units. All 66 units have already been replaced in a new rental building at 105 Harrison Garden Boulevard as part of an earlier phase of the redevelopment. Tenant assistance measures are addressed in the report.

title: 5294-5304 and 5306 Yonge Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: community councils, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council approve Official Plan and zoning amendments for 5294-5304 and 5306 Yonge Street to develop a 43-storey mixed-use building with 395 homes and a gross floor area of 28,332.53 square metres. The application amends a previous approval for a 33-storey building by adding 10 storeys (29.74 metres); other elements remain materially the same.

title: Federation of Canadian Municipalities Advocacy Days - Municipal Priorities Ahead of Federal Budget 2024 - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: members of parliament, municipalities; boroughs; cities; counties; regional municipalities; towns, mp
brief: Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends City Council receive for information the Federation of Canadian Municipalities backgrounder 'New Research - Canada's Housing Challenge is also an Infrastructure Challenge'. FCM board members held over 100 meetings with MPs during November 21-24 Advocacy Days ahead of Budget 2024, focused on housing, homelessness and a new municipal growth framework.

title: Reimbursement of Cities Forum 2023 Conference Expenses, Torino, Italy - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: refund; reimbursement
brief: Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council approve reimbursing his travel expenses for attending the Cities Forum 2023 conference in Torino, Italy in March 2023 with his chief of staff, paid from his constituency office budget. A missed return flight required an extra flight and night's accommodation, pushing the total trip cost over $7,000 for both.

title: Authorization to Amend Section 37 Agreement on Timing of Obligations in Response to Committee of Adjustment Application Regarding 1141 Bloor Street West, 980 Dufferin Street, 90 Croatia Street - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends that if the Committee of Adjustment approves the variance for 1141 Bloor Street West, 980 Dufferin Street and 90 Croatia Street, Council require the owner to enter an amending Section 37 agreement. The 2021 Tribunal-approved redevelopment of the former school board lands includes affordable and market housing, a daycare, community space, a park, a public street and heritage conservation; the timing of the park and street conveyance was secured in the Section 37 agreement.

title: Last Chance to Help Small Businesses: Requesting the Federal Government Extend the Canada Emergency Business Account Deadline - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: small businesses;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council ask the federal government to extend the Canada Emergency Business Account repayment deadline to December 31, 2024, and forward the item to all Toronto-area MPs. Local businesses warn many must take loans to repay, adding financial pressure while still recovering from the pandemic.

title: Appointment of Public Member to the Toronto Film, Television and Digital Media Board - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by  Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: public appointments;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council appoint Sarah Farrell to the Toronto Film, Television and Digital Media Board for a term ending November 14, 2026. The industry contributes $2.6 billion in annual production volume and employs 35,000 Torontonians, and the board benefits from strong studio operator representation.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Bayview Village Participatory Budgeting Projects - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: budgets; budgets and accounts
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends City Council release Section 37 funds for Bayview Village participatory budgeting projects, adjusting Parks, Forestry and Recreation's capital budget and plan. Residents suggested over 70 project ideas in May 2023, which staff evaluated for cost and feasibility, and the community voted in fall 2023.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item MM11.34 - Opening City Hall - Regarding the Terms of Reference for the City-School Boards Advisory Committee - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: school boards, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, recommends City Council amend the City-School Boards Advisory Committee's terms of reference after consulting Toronto's French-language school boards: adding one trustee from each of the Conseil scolaire catholique MonAvenir and Conseil scolaire Viamonde, and reducing council members from four to two (truncated), removing the community council representation requirement. The change is urgent so the committee can meet in the new year.

title: Taking Action on the Declaration of Intimate Partner Violence as an Epidemic - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, recommends City Council ask the Chief People Officer to help develop a working group on the July 2023 declaration of gender-based and intimate partner violence as an epidemic in Toronto. The motion cites federal data that 44 percent of women aged 15 and older have reported intimate partner abuse, and that a woman is murdered by an intimate partner in Canada every six days.

title: Display of 988 Crisis Line Information Poster - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: community crisis response, emergency management; crisis management; disaster planning; disaster supply kits; emergency preparedness; emergency procedures; emergency supply kits; survival kits, crisis response
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council endorse the 988 national suicide and crisis hotline and display the 988 information poster in all city-owned buildings, including libraries, community centres and police stations. MP Todd Doherty asked the city to recognize and advertise the initiative.

title: Request for City Planning to Launch the Glencairn Subway Station Planning Study - by Councillor Michael Colle, seconded by Councillor Pasternak
topics: planning, subway stations;
brief: Councillor Michael Colle, seconded by Councillor Pasternak, recommends City Council direct the Chief Planner to issue the request for proposals for the Glencairn Subway Station Planning Study in Q1 2024. The Marlee Avenue corridor faces many new multi-residential applications, and the study would identify future social and community infrastructure needs amid growth constrained by provincial Bill 23.

title: Silent Nights and Peaceful Days - Providing relief to residents from Metrolinx’s Whistle Sounding at Manse Road Rail Crossing on the Lakeshore East Corridor - by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: railway crossings; grade crossings; level crossings; railway grade crossings
brief: Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council direct the City Manager to ask Metrolinx to work with city staff on quick safety fixes to stop train whistles at the Manse Road at-grade crossing on the Lakeshore East corridor. Metrolinx began sounding whistles on November 23 without warning residents, after its safety division deemed the crossing an unacceptable risk; residents find the whistles disruptive and alarming.

title: Securing the Future of Applegrove Community Complex - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, recommends City Council direct Corporate Real Estate Management to report back by Q2 2024 on alternative sites for the Applegrove Community Complex. The 7,911-square-foot community centre serving Greenwood-Coxwell since 1979 has been in lease overhold at the Duke of Connaught School since 2013, and 2020 Council direction on a permanent site stalled on cost and timelines.

title: Metrolinx Eglinton Crosstown West Extension - Elevated Guideway - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: light rail transit, transportation; lrt, transportation services
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends City Council ask Transportation Services and Transit Expansion to investigate reducing the setbacks between Eglinton Avenue West and the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension's elevated guideway, shifting it. The guideway would run along the north side of Eglinton West between portals east of Jane Street near Pearen Park and west of Scarlett Road, set back 10.6 metres from the curb east of Jane Street along Fergy Brown and Pearen Parks.

title: Confronting the Legacy of the Transatlantic Slave Trade: Renaming Civic Assets Bearing the Henry Dundas Name - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: facility naming, naming; park naming
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, recommends City Council direct the Yonge-Dundas Square Board, with Economic Development and Culture, to adopt the new name Sankofa Square selected by the Recognition Review Community Advisory Committee, and report back through the Executive Committee. Council voted in July 2021 to rename Dundas Street after a 2020 petition citing namesake Henry Dundas' role in delaying abolition of the trans-Atlantic slave trade.

title: 19 Forest Glen Crescent - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, hearings;
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends City Council authorize the City Solicitor to appeal and attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the Committee of Adjustment's decision on a new detached dwelling at 19 Forest Glen Crescent. The applicant sought variances on setbacks, driveway width, landscaping, lot coverage and canopy encroachment; staff raised concerns about the front yard setback and landscaping reductions.

title: Federal Housing Accelerator Fund - Supporting Generational Transformation of Toronto’s Housing System - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: funding, housing; financing, homes; residences
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council adopt recommendations to negotiate and execute agreements under the federal Housing Accelerator Fund, supporting the generational transformation of Toronto's housing system. The fund would bring new federal investment to increase housing supply, protect existing homes and improve housing stability.

title: Appointment of Councillor Parthi Kandavel to Various Committees and Boards - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends City Council appoint Councillor Parthi Kandavel, elected November 30, 2023 in the Ward 20 Scarborough Southwest by-election, to the Planning and Housing Committee until December 31, 2024 and to various boards. The Mayor issued a Mayoral Decision expanding the committee by one member rather than replacing anyone.

title: 300 Bloor Street West and 478 Huron Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: appeals, hearings;
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council authorize the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body in support of the appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's November 8, 2023 refusal of variances at 300 Bloor Street West and 478 Huron Street. The application sought more floor area, 16.5 metres more height and less amenity space per unit.

title: Conveyance of Parkland - 2150 and 2194 Lake Shore Boulevard West and 23 Park Lawn Road - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends City Council approve the conveyance of parkland for the phased mixed-use development at 2150 and 2194 Lake Shore Boulevard West and 23 Park Lawn Road, approved by Council in 2022 with about 7,500 homes, two parkland dedications, a new GO station, a library, a recreation centre, two child care centres and agency space. The owner would convey the parkland before condo registration or first occupancy of the second tower near the Phase 2 park.

title: Purchase Order Amendment on Contract with Midome Construction Services Limited for the New Streetcar Tracks on Adelaide Street - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: contracts, streetcars; street-cars
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council authorize amending the purchase order and contract with Midome Construction Services Limited for installing new streetcar tracks and associated infrastructure on Adelaide Street between York Street and Victoria Street. The work is part of the planned streetcar detour around Ontario Line Queen station construction.

title: Amendment to By-law 438-86 Regarding 325 Gerrard Street East (Regent Park Phases 4 and 5) - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council amend the zoning by-law amendment for Regent Park Phases 4 and 5 as set out in the motion's attachment, with no further public notice required under the Planning Act. Council adopted the original amendment in July 2023; as design of the first Toronto Community Housing building progressed, a modification to Map 3 became necessary.

title: Supporting Professional Women's Soccer in Toronto - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, recommends City Council express support for establishing a professional women's soccer league in Toronto and its commitment to gender equity in sport, and direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation to consult on next steps. Project 8 is leading the effort to launch the league; Toronto will also welcome a Professional Women's Hockey League team in 2024.

title: Naming of 39 Dundalk Drive as Domenica Place - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: street names; renaming; road names; street naming
brief: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, recommends City Council officially name the new 57-unit affordable and accessible modular housing residence at 39 Dundalk Drive in Scarborough Centre as Domenica Place, notwithstanding the property naming policy. The residence opened November 22, 2023 and is one of seven modular housing initiatives approved by Council.

title: 8 Adams Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: appeals, planning & development (sc);
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing to oppose the appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of variances at 8 Adams Drive, which sought to legalize 7 secondary suites in a single-detached dwelling's basement. The Scarborough panel refused the variances on October 18, 2023.

title: Road and Intersection Safety Review on Winona Drive at St. Clair Avenue West and Barrie Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: roads, safety; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), public safety
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow, recommends City Council ask Transportation Services, with Toronto Police as needed, to report back in Q1 2024 on traffic, cyclist and pedestrian safety at Winona Drive and St. Clair Avenue West, where a pedestrian died on December 7, 2023, and at Winona Drive and Barrie Avenue, where residents have raised concerns.

title: Appointment of City of Toronto Designate to ArtHubs Toronto Inc. Board of Directors - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: arts and culture organizations; art councils; art organizations; arts councils; arts groups; cultural organizations
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council appoint the General Manager, Economic Development and Culture, as the city's designate on the board of ArtHubs Toronto Inc. for two years ending December 31, 2025. ArtHubs is a new not-for-profit assuming operation of the community cultural hubs previously managed by Artscape, including Daniels Spectrum, Gibraltar Point, Wychwood Barns and Youngplace.

title: Balanced Approach to Distributing Legislative Meeting Materials - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: costs, council meetings, ecological footprint, environmental conditions, printing and distribution; circulation; copying; mailing list; photocopying; printing; subscriptions, environmental footprint; zero footprint cities; zerofootprint cities, environmental health; environmental quality; environmental sensitivity; state of the environment
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends City Council direct the City Clerk to survey councillors on their interest in receiving paper copies of legislative meeting materials and report back with findings, a proposal, budget implications and implementation options. The pandemic-era shift to digital-only materials has proven challenging for some members.

title: Recognizing the 100th Anniversary of East York - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: former municipalities;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow, recommends City Council recognize the former Borough of East York as an important founding member of the new city and ask the City Clerk to support commemorating the 100th anniversary of East York's founding in 1924. The Township of East York was incorporated January 1, 1924 with a population of 19,849.

title: 413 The Kingsway - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's October 26, 2023 refusal of a variance at 413 The Kingsway, which sought to legalize an addition atop an existing rear-yard cabana.

title: 8-26 Jopling Avenue South - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: boards of management; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, recommends City Council authorize the City Solicitor to appeal and attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the Committee of Adjustment's decision on 8-26 Jopling Avenue South. The applicant sought variances to the site-specific by-law permitting two towers of 27 and 33 storeys with up to 688 units.

title: Crisis Looms as Aging Booms: Creating a Path Forward to Age in Place - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: retirement homes; retirement housing
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, recommends City Council ask the federal government to develop a national strategy to support Naturally Occurring Retirement Communities and their programming, to help seniors age in place. Institutionalizing seniors removes them from support networks and is costly; in 2021 about 489 residential buildings in Toronto fit the NORC profile (truncated).

title: Refunding Rent Paid and Relieving Rent Owed by Flip Kitchen Vendors Previously at City-owned Site on 5200 Yonge Street in Response to Termination of Contract - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: vendors;
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, recommends City Council authorize writing off $27,621.78 in rent owed from January 1 to October 31, 2023 by Flip Kitchen vendors at the city-owned site at 5200 Yonge Street, and refunding rent paid. The pandemic-era food incubator for entrepreneurs from equity-seeking groups fell behind on rent from September 2023 and received an eviction notice in mid-November 2023.

title: Renaming the Stadium at Centennial Park - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: facility naming, facility naming, stadiums; park naming, park naming, sports stadiums
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council rename the stadium at Centennial Park as the 'Rob Ford Stadium', notwithstanding the city's naming policy. Rob Ford served on Council for nearly 15 years, including four years as Mayor, and the city has historically recognized former mayors with commemorative renamings such as Mel Lastman Square and June Rowlands Park.

title: Re-Opening Item EX2.1 on Re-establishing Council Advisory Bodies for 2022-2026 City Council Term to Amend the 2022-2026 Terms of Reference for the Toronto Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: committee meetings;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, recommends City Council amend the Toronto Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee's terms of reference so the committee meets 'at least' two times per year instead of 'up to' two times. As committee chair, she met with francophone community members who want the committee to have adequate time to advise on issues affecting francophones.

title: Welland Avenue - Parking That Blocks Toronto Transit Commission - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, parking prohibitions, stopping prohibitions; no parking, no stopping, ttc
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday, recommends City Council change parking rules on the west side of Welland Avenue between Inglewood Drive and Moore Avenue, because parked vehicles block TTC route 88 South Leaside buses from safely making the westbound left turn from Moore Avenue onto Welland Avenue. Transportation Services supports the change in consultation with the TTC.

title: Ensuring Safe and Accessible Pedestrian Routes in Construction Zones - Letter from Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee
topics: accessibility, construction, pedestrian infrastructure; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, building, pedestrian network
brief: The Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee recommends City Council ask Transportation Services to work with all constructors in the road right-of-way to ensure clear notification and signage, including the 311 phone number, so pedestrian routes in construction zones stay safe and accessible. The committee made the recommendations at its October 16, 2023 meeting.

title: Update: City Renewable Energy Programs
topics: energy, programs, residents; energy resources; energy use
brief: This is an information item: an update on the city's renewable energy programs, responding to Council direction on barriers to renewable energy deployment. Staff recommend Council direct continued work with Toronto Hydro to streamline the grid interconnection process for solar and storage projects, supporting the TransformTO target of 50 percent of community-wide energy from renewables.

title: Proposed Building Emissions Performance Reporting By-Law
topics: buildings, greenhouse effect, property (sc); greenhouse gas emissions
brief: Staff recommend City Council adopt a new Building Emissions Performance by-law, effective January 1, 2024. Existing buildings are Toronto's largest source of greenhouse gas emissions at about 58 percent of community-wide emissions, and the city's Net Zero Existing Buildings Strategy targets net zero by 2040 with emissions nearly halved by 2030 relative to 2008.

title: Expanding the Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program Eligibility Criteria to Include Registered Property Owners of Existing Residential Fourplexes
topics: flooding, residential properties, safety; floods, public safety, residential real estate
brief: The General Manager, Toronto Water recommends City Council expand the Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program to include registered owners of existing residential fourplexes, subject to the program's other eligibility criteria. The program is currently available only to owners of single-family, duplex or triplex properties.

title: Update and Action Plan on the Single-Use and Takeaway Items Reduction Strategy, including the Circular Food Innovators Fund
topics: businesses, commercial properties, water supply; commercial waste collection customers, office real estate; retail space, water delivery; water distribution; water hook-up; water installation; water service; water shut off; water shut-off; water turn off; water turn on
brief: Staff recommend City Council repeal the packaging by-law effective January 1, 2024 and adopt a new Single-Use and Takeaway Items By-law as Stage 2 of the reduction strategy. Retailers would have to confirm a customer needs a single-use food accessory item before distributing it, among other mandatory measures. The report also covers the Circular Food Innovators Fund.

title: Single-Space Meters - Various Locations
topics: business services industry, on-street parking, payment in lieu of parking; business services, cash-in-lieu of parking; payment-in-lieu of parking, curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council decommission all 176 on-street single-space parking meters across the city and delete the related entries in the parking by-laws. The proposal follows consultation with the Toronto Parking Authority on its experience with on-street single-space metered parking.

title: Reducing Bird Deaths by Turning off Lights during Migration
topics: birds, property owners, street lights; building owners; land owners; property ownership, chickens; dead birds; ducks; geese (wild); gulls; pigeons; seagulls; starlings; turkeys, street light covers; street lighting fixtures; streetlights
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends City Council direct the City Manager to resume turning off unnecessary lights on city property during bird migration seasons, a cost-saving practice that protects birds. Artificial light from buildings endangers migrating birds, which navigate at night by moon, star and sunset light, especially on foggy or rainy nights.

title: Eastbound F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Northbound Don Valley Parkway Closures - 2024 Toronto Triathlon Festival
topics: festivals and special events, highways, ramps (highways); community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, freeways; motorways; parkways, off ramps (highways); on ramps (highways)
brief: Transportation Services recommends City Council authorize closing the eastbound F.G. Gardiner Expressway from the Humber River to the Don Valley Parkway, including all ramps, and the northbound Don Valley Parkway from the Gardiner to Eglinton Avenue East, including all ramps, for the 2024 Toronto Triathlon Festival. The 2024 route is the same as in 2023.

title: Housing Numbers
topics: development, housing; developing land; development (land); land development, homes; residences
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday (Ward 2, Etobicoke Centre) submits an administrative inquiry about housing numbers, referring to the Chief Planner's February 2023 Development Pipeline 2022 report, which reported development activity from January 1, 2017 to June 30, 2022. The inquiry is made under the council procedure by-law for the December 13, 2023 Council meeting.

title: Renaming Dundas Street
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday (Ward 2, Etobicoke Centre) submits an administrative inquiry asking staff for the most recent assessment of the total cost of renaming Dundas Street, including costs to the city, the province, businesses and residents. The inquiry is made under the council procedure by-law for the December 13, 2023 Council meeting.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with Toronto Drydock Limited for Dry Docking Ship Repair Services for the Ongiara Vessel
topics: [water management equipment], employment & labour (sc), materials; commodities; goods
brief: This is an information item: Council is advised of a non-competitive contract with Toronto Drydock Limited for $5,350,656 for dry docking and ship repair services for the Ongiara ferry vessel, covering labour, equipment, materials and repairs. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with EllisDon Civil Limited to Repair the Temporary Dufferin Street Bridges over Metrolinx Rail Corridor
topics: bridge maintenance, construction, structures; building
brief: This is an information item: Council is advised of a non-competitive contract with EllisDon Civil Limited for $1,320,000 to repair damaged elements of the temporary Dufferin Street bridges over the Metrolinx rail corridor, south of Springhurst Avenue. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with BDA Inc. for the Roof Replacement at 291 Sherbourne Street
topics: damage, expropriations, property (sc); compulsory purchase; eminent domain
brief: This is an information item: Council is advised of a non-competitive purchase order with BDA Inc. for $2,075,000 to replace the roof at 291 Sherbourne Street, known as Robertson House, a city-owned shelter operated by Shelter, Support and Housing Administration. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with 1623052 Ontario Ltd. operating as CB Sales Canada for Purafil Scrubber Media Removal and Replacement of Chlorine Gas Scrubber at Island Water Treatment Plant
topics: charges, expropriations, taxes; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, levies
brief: This is an information item: Council is advised of a non-competitive contract with CB Sales Canada for Purafil scrubber media removal and replacement of the chlorine gas scrubber at the Island Water Treatment Plant, exceeding $500,000. Purchase orders include $181,670 awarded in 2018 and a $50,000 divisional order. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Largest Property Tax Debtors with Tax Arrears Greater than $500,000 as at June 30, 2023
topics: community & life (sc), properties (real estate), property tax rates; property; real estate
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports on the 24 properties with tax arrears of $500,000 or more as of June 30, 2023, including 20 owned by corporations and four by individuals. Council is asked to keep the confidential attachment with the debtor details confidential.

title: Parking Infractions Seamless Reporting
topics: parking, parking infractions, police services; blocked driveway; illegal parking; parking offences; parking violations; vehicle blocking driveway, police; policing
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie recommends City Council direct the Executive Director, Customer Experience, in consultation with the Toronto Police parking enforcement unit, to review and report on using 311 Toronto as an intake channel for parking infraction reports. The proposal would add a reporting feature to the existing 311 app for parking and bike infractions.

title: Update on Additional Costs Associated with Extraction of the Micro-Tunneling Boring Machine on Contract 20ECS-LU-01FP
topics: construction, contracts, fire and rescue services; building, fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council adopt confidential instructions to staff on options to recover costs from the emergency non-competitive contract to rescue the micro-tunneling boring machine on Contract 20ECS-LU-01FP near Old Mill Drive, and authorize public release of the recommendations at the City Solicitor's discretion.

title: Amendments to Toronto Municipal Code, Chapter 195, Purchasing, and Review of Open Contracting Global Principles and the Role of an Inspector General
topics: delegation of authority, materials, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, commodities; goods, signing authorities
brief: The Chief Procurement Officer recommends City Council amend the Purchasing By-law effective July 1, 2024, following the required five-year review of the by-law last reviewed in 2016 and enacted in 2017. The report also responds to Council's request on adopting the Open Contracting Global Principles and the role of an Inspector General.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate portions of properties - 32 to 50 Larwood Boulevard - Stage 1
topics: cyclists, expropriations, pedestrians; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, pedestrianization
brief: Staff recommend City Council authorize starting expropriation proceedings (Stage 1) for portions of 32 to 50 Larwood Boulevard, to install a multi-use trail improving pedestrian and cyclist safety on the east side of Brimley Road South from Barkdene Hills to Bluffers Park Road. Staff would then serve and publish the required notices.

title: Agreement with the University of Toronto for Voluntary Payments Relating to its Revenue-Producing Properties
topics: agreements, payment, residential properties; paying; payment information; payment methods; payment options; pre-authorized payment plans; pre-authorized plans; preauthorized payments, residential real estate, tenancy agreements
brief: The Controller recommends City Council authorize extending the existing agreement with the University of Toronto for voluntary payments on its revenue-producing properties, on substantially the same terms as the agreement approved by Council in 2013.

title: Councillors' Constituency Offices - Designation of Portions of Properties used as Municipal Capital Facilities
topics: education (sc), offices, properties (real estate); property; real estate
brief: The Controller recommends City Council pass by-laws to designate portions of three leased properties used as councillors' constituency offices as Municipal Capital Facilities, providing municipal and education tax exemptions. The agreements cover about 3,163 square feet of combined space, including 641B The Queensway (truncated).

title: 2900 Warden Avenue - Designation of a Portion of the Property used by the Toronto Public Library as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: leasing, property (sc), taxes; leases, levies
brief: The Controller recommends City Council pass a by-law to designate the Bridlewood Branch library space at 2900 Warden Avenue, about 19,425 square feet leased from Bridlewood Mall Management, as a Municipal Capital Facility, providing municipal and education tax exemptions.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with N. Barry Lyon Consultants for Multi-Tenant Housing Land Economics Study
topics: housing, planning & development (sc), residential properties; homes; residences, residential real estate
brief: The Chief Planner and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend City Council authorize a non-competitive agreement with N.
