title: New Housing Opportunities on the Danforth - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks City Council to direct staff to develop a pathway to redevelop 1117 Danforth as affordable supportive housing, working with the Housing Secretariat, City Planning, Houselink and Mainstay Community Housing. The motion builds on an April Planning and Housing Committee direction.

title: Amending Item TE34.11- 40 Raglan Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Final Report - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow asks City Council to amend its 2022 approval for 40 Raglan Avenue by removing the requirement for a Limiting Distance Agreement over 54 Raglan Avenue, which is not feasible because that property is neither adjacent to nor part of the development lands. The requirement has stalled development on the site.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 176-178 Front Street East and 33 Sherbourne Street to Anishnawbe Health Toronto - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: development, reserve funds; developing land; development (land); land development, reserves and reserve funds
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks City Council to direct $1,066,666 in Section 37 funds from the development at 176-178 Front Street East and 33 Sherbourne Street to Anishnawbe Health Toronto. The funding supports the Indigenous Community Hub at 425 Cherry Street in the West Don Lands.

title: Advancing Steeles Avenue Widening Archaeological Assessments - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: archaeological sites, environmental assessments, road reconstruction; archaeological digs, ea; ecological assessment; environmental assessment; environmental evaluation, road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: Councillor Jamaal Myers asks City Council to authorize Transportation Services to negotiate agreements with the Huron Wendat, Curve Lake and Mississaugas of the Credit First Nations for archaeological assessments needed for the Steeles Avenue widening. The project, jointly funded with York Region, is in detailed design with construction starting in 2025.

title: Amending Item CC45.21 - 717 Church Street and 85, 89, 93 and 97 Collier Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Further Directions Regarding Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks City Council to amend the Section 37 provisions for 717 Church Street and 85, 89, 93 and 97 Collier Street after the Ontario Land Tribunal approved the proposal. The changes ensure works along Collier Street are completed on time, with the owner agreeing to close the western portion of Collier Street to vehicles except emergency vehicles.

title: Supporting Sustainable Energy Storage in the Port Lands - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: energy; energy resources; energy use
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks City Council to endorse the potential use of City-owned lands for large-scale battery storage in the Port Lands, using infrastructure around the Hearn Generating Station. A battery facility could reduce running time at the Port Lands Energy Centre and support TransformTO goals, subject to due diligence.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item TE6.98 - 624 King Street West - CaféTO Curb Lane Café - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: zoning;
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks City Council to re-open and amend its July 2023 decision on the CafeTO curb lane cafe at 624 King Street West, to correct an error by enacting a no stopping zone on the south side of King Street West. Staff need the fix to bring the location into compliance.

title: 19 Branch Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: appeals, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards
brief: Councillor Amber Morley asks City Council to authorize the City Solicitor to appeal and oppose, at the Toronto Local Appeal Body, the Committee of Adjustment's approval of a triplex at 19 Branch Avenue. The application lacked a rental housing declaration, so the City has no confirmation that tenant assistance meets Official Plan policy.

title: Extension of the Alcohol in Parks Pilot - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: parks, parks permits, special occasion permits; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks City Council to extend the Alcohol in Parks pilot program, which ran from August 2 to October 9, 2023 in 27 parks, until March 31, 2024 or until Council considers staff's evaluation report. Residents have expressed appreciation for the pilot's responsible-drinking approach.

title: 196 Valley Road - Technical Amendment to By-laws 452-2022 and 453-2022 - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson asks City Council to make technical amendments to By-laws 452-2022 and 453-2022 for the three-storey townhouse development at 196 Valley Road. The amendments correct omissions, including allowing a front yard platform height of 1.41 metres instead of 1.2 metres.

title: Restore North York Civic Centre Hours of Operation - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: civic centres, hours of operation; business hours; holiday closures; hours; open hours; operating hours, ccs
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks City Council to request that Corporate Real Estate Management consider extending North York Civic Centre operating hours to include evenings and weekends in the 2024 budget submission. Many seniors rely on the Civic Centre's sheltered access to the library, transit and shops as a safe passageway.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2023.NY4.42 - Elvaston Drive - Community Safety Zone - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: community safety, school zone review, transportation; transportation services
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside asks City Council to re-open its May 2023 decision designating a Community Safety Zone on Elvaston Drive near Sloane Public School, to adjust the zone limits for enforceability. The amended zone would run between Sloane Avenue and a point 125 metres west of Halkin Crescent.

title: Last Chance to Urge Province to Build Cummer Station for the Future of North York - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: public transit, subway stations; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks City Council to request that the Province of Ontario fully fund the design and construction of Cummer Station as part of the Yonge North Subway Extension. The station would serve over 15,000 present and future residents within a 10-minute walk of Yonge Street and Cummer Avenue.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 and Section 42 Above 5 percent Cash-in-lieu Funds for Lighting Improvements to the Village of Yorkville Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks City Council to create a new capital sub-project for lighting improvements to the Village of Yorkville Park, at a cost of $560,000, funded by Section 37 and Section 42 cash-in-lieu funds. The park's aging lighting is no longer adequate for the heavily used gathering space.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to City Planning for a University Avenue Heritage Study, from the Development at 180-188 University Avenue - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: development, funding; developing land; development (land); land development, financing
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks City Council to release $57,751.47 in Section 37 funds to City Planning for a University Avenue heritage study. The funds were secured from the development at 180-188 University Avenue and allocated for studying the cultural heritage value of the 12 medians from College Street to Adelaide Street.

title: Rental Demolition Permits and Market Rentals - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks City Council to recognize the urgency of including purpose-built rental housing in large new residential developments and to reaffirm the right to return for renters displaced by demolition and redevelopment. The motion responds to a wave of applications to demolish aging rental buildings, often for condo towers.

title: Reimbursement of Cities Forum 2023 Conference Expenses, Torino, Italy - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: expenses, refund; reimbursement
brief: Councillor Nick Mantas asks City Council to authorize payment for his and his Chief of Staff's expenses attending the Cities Forum 2023 in Torino, Italy in March 2023. A missed return flight required an extra flight and night's accommodation, pushing costs over $7,000, which requires Council approval under the office budget policy.

title: 2639R Dundas Street West - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body- by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: appeals, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards
brief: Councillor Gord Perks asks City Council to authorize the City Solicitor to appeal and oppose, at the Toronto Local Appeal Body, the Committee of Adjustment's approval of a 4-unit townhouse block at 2639R Dundas Street West. City Planning staff had raised concerns, including that the townhouse block has no direct access to an existing street.

title: Amending TE3.9 - 276-294 Main Street and 144 Stephenson Avenue - formerly 286-294 Main Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Request for Directions - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: funding, parks, reserve funds; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing, reserves and reserve funds
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford asks City Council to amend its 2019 approval for 276-294 Main Street and 144 Stephenson Avenue. A final survey found 357.2 square metres of parkland can be conveyed rather than 365, so the remaining 7.8 square metres would be provided as cash in lieu.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Canada Ireland Foundation for ongoing renovations to the City-owned Building at 3 Eireann Quay - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: buildings, finance (sc), funding; financing
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks City Council to direct $500,000 in Section 37 funds to the Canada Ireland Foundation for ongoing renovations of the City-owned building at 3 Eireann Quay into a waterfront cultural and interpretive centre honouring Irish famine immigrants. The funds come from the development at 350 Queens Quay West.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Bentway Conservancy to Advance the Development of the Space South of Canoe Landing Park Under the Gardiner Expressway - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks City Council to create a new capital sub-project for the lands south of Canoe Landing Park, with a project cost of $798,970, advancing the Bentway's development of the space under the Gardiner Expressway. The funds come from Section 37 community benefits.

title: Establishing an Enforceable Enhanced Code of Conduct for Construction and Repair Companies Under Contract to the City of Toronto - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: behaviour standards, contracts; behavior standards; behaviour; code of conduct; codes of behaviour; codes of conduct; standards of behavior; standards of behaviour
brief: Councillor James Pasternak asks City Council to direct staff to develop an enforceable enhanced Code of Conduct for all companies doing construction, repair or maintenance work under City contract, and to report back. The motion responds to frustration with contractor project management such as unjustified lane closures and abandoned sites.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Mount Dennis Business Improvement Area, for the Installation of New, Energy-efficient, Decorative Lamp Standards at Various Locations - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: business improvement areas, energy efficiency, funding; alternative energy; electricity usage; energy use; sustainable energy, bia; business improvement associations, financing
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata asks City Council to release $26,886.71 in Section 37 funds to the Mount Dennis Business Improvement Area for new energy-efficient decorative lamp standards at various locations. The funds come from the development at 1391 Weston Road.

title: Learning from the Fire at 35 Vulcan Street
topics: fires, hazardous spills, pollution; accidental spills; chemical spills; environmental spills; illegal discharges; leaking oil tanks; liquid waste spills; spills; spills of hazardous material; toxic dumping; toxic spills, burning brush; burning garbage; burning leaves; outdoor fires, contamination
brief: Councillor Amber Morley recommends that City Council ask the Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks to publicly report the results of all sampling since the August 11, 2023 six-alarm fire at the Brenntag Canada chemical facility at 35 Vulcan Street, including any long-term risks to waterways, animals or people. Cleanup and monitoring are ongoing.

title: Citywide Approach to Dogs Off-Leash Areas
topics: Master Plans, dog off-leash areas, dogs; dog parks; dogs off leash parks; dogs off-leash parks; leash free areas; leash free dog walking areas; leash free parks; leash free zones; leash-free areas; leash-free dog walking areas; leash-free zones; off leash areas; off leash parks
brief: Councillor Chris Moise recommends that City Council direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation to review and update how the City plans, funds, builds and maintains dogs off-leash areas, based on best practices and integrated with the Facilities Master Plan. Toronto has an estimated 300,000 dogs, with more people and dogs sharing parkland.

title: Consumption-based Emissions Inventory and Cool Food Pledge Commitments
topics: climate, environment (sc), greenhouse effect; greenhouse gas emissions
brief: This item reports on a consumption-based emissions inventory, which estimates the greenhouse gas emissions tied to goods and services consumed by Toronto residents, from production through disposal. The report also covers the City's Cool Food Pledge commitments. Staff recommend that City Council direct further work on both the inventory and the pledge.

title: Update on the Net Zero Buildings Strategy and Implementation of Mandatory Emissions Performance Standards
topics: community development, greenhouse effect, high rise buildings; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, greenhouse gas emissions, tall buildings
brief: This is an information item: an update on the Net Zero Buildings Strategy and implementation of mandatory emissions performance standards. Existing buildings account for about 58 percent of Toronto's community-wide greenhouse gas emissions, and Council has set a net zero by 2040 target. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Transition of Toronto's Blue Bin Recycling Program to Extended Producer Responsibility
topics: labour relations, recycling containers, service delivery; collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, recycling bins
brief: Staff recommend that City Council support the decision not to bid on the request for proposals from Circular Materials and Reverse Logistics Group for Blue Box collection services after 2025. The report covers Toronto's role once responsibility for the Blue Bin program shifts to producers under extended producer responsibility on January 1, 2026.

title: On-Street Paid Parking Pilot - Mobile Only Zones
topics: parking authorities, parking fees, pilot projects; parking authority, parking charges; parking rates
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a pilot project of up to 12 months for mobile-only payment zones at on-street paid parking locations. Over 75 percent of Toronto Parking Authority transactions now go through the Green P App, which has 1.6 million subscribers, reducing use of pay-and-display machines.

title: Prioritization of Green Building Standards in Ontario Building Code
topics: building codes, green standards, planning; green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends that City Council reaffirm its support for moving green building standards from the site plan process into the Ontario Building Code, and ask the Province to expedite the transition. The standards cover construction of buildings and are key to the City's TransformTO net zero goals.

title: Cannabis Stores and Revenue Sharing
topics: public inquiries, revenue generation; judicial inquries, revenue tools
brief: Councillor James Pasternak has submitted an administrative inquiry seeking details of funds promised and received by the City from the Province of Ontario related to cannabis retail stores. Council decided on December 13, 2018 not to opt out of having cannabis stores in Toronto.

title: The Pink Floyd Exhibition at the Better Living Centre, Exhibition Place from August 18 to October 1, 2023
topics: discrimination, government (sc);
brief: Councillor James Pasternak has submitted an administrative inquiry seeking information about the Pink Floyd Exhibition held at the Better Living Centre at Exhibition Place from August 18 to October 1, 2023. The inquiry raises concerns about the exhibition's attention to Roger Waters given his public comments.

title: City Staff Use of Cameras During Online Virtual Meetings
topics: council meetings, public meetings;
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside has submitted an administrative inquiry asking about the City's policy on whether staff are required to have their cameras on during online virtual meetings. The inquiry asks the City Manager what the current policy is.

title: Toronto Public Health Backgrounder for 2024 Budget Preparation
topics: boards of health, funding, health (sc), public health, regulations; financing
brief: The Board of Health's Budget Committee recommends that the Board of Health ask the Province of Ontario for sufficient and sustainable funding for Toronto Public Health. The request cites inflationary pressures and the demands of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Update on the Confirmation Program for City Agencies, and Corporations
topics: [people in property], audits, security; auditors; auditors
brief: This is an information item: an update on the Confirmation Program, which helps the City's agencies and corporations implement baseline cyber security controls. Details on entities deviating from the program are in a confidential attachment. The Chief Information Security Officer recommends that City Council keep the attachment confidential.

title: Increase in Parking Violation Notice Penalty Amount on Municipal / Private Property
topics: parking, parking infractions, penalties; blocked driveway; illegal parking; parking offences; parking violations; vehicle blocking driveway
brief: Staff recommend that City Council increase the penalty for parking on municipal property without consent from $30 to $75. The change aligns penalty amounts with parking rates so drivers pay for parking rather than risking the lower fine, with implementation in December.

title: Status of Outstanding Payments in Lieu of Tax Amounts for Federal, Provincial and Municipal Properties and Proposed Delegation of Authority to Committee to Hear and Decide on Applications with respect to Payments in Lieu of Tax Amounts for Federal, Provincial and Municipal Properties
topics: [organizations in finance], accounts, payment; paying; payment information; payment methods; payment options; pre-authorized payment plans; pre-authorized plans; preauthorized payments
brief: The Controller reports on outstanding payments in lieu of taxes from federal, provincial and municipal properties as of August 31, 2023 for the 2022 taxation year. Payments in lieu of taxes are voluntary payments governments make to compensate the City for municipal services. Staff recommend that City Council delegate authority to the General Government Committee to hear and decide payment-in-lieu applications.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate a portion of the One Foot Reserve near Bantry Avenue - Stage 1
topics: land, pedestrian walkways, property (sc); footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways, property
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize starting expropriation proceedings for part of a one-foot reserve at the end of Bantry Avenue, for a pedestrian walkway from Montclair Avenue to Lower Village Gate. The walkway would provide access to St. Clair West subway station and the Cedarvale Ravine as part of a condominium development at 63-91 Montclair Avenue.

title: Declare Surplus of City Walkway Between 19 and 23 Lord Roberts Drive
topics: asset disposal, excess, pedestrian walkways; auctions; sale of surplus equipment; sale of surplus materials; surplus equipment disposal procedure; surplus materials disposal procedure, extra; overage; overflow; surplus, footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways
brief: Staff recommend that City Council declare the City walkway between 19 and 23 Lord Roberts Drive surplus, with the intended disposal being a permanent easement to Enbridge Gas Inc. Declaring the land surplus is a required step before the easement transfer, which would use delegated authority.

title: Amendment to Coca-Cola Coliseum Lease and Sublease
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements, leasing, tenants; leases, renters; tenancy agreements, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve amendments to the Coca-Cola Coliseum head lease with BPC Coliseum Inc. and the sublease with Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment. The 2005 head lease runs to 2052, and the sublease for the Toronto Marlies' home arena runs to June 30, 2025.

title: Amendment of Waterfront Property Management Agreement with Toronto Port Lands Company
topics: agreements, contracts, waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize an amendment to the 1995 property management agreement with the Toronto Port Lands Company, which manages City-owned industrial development properties acquired from the Toronto Harbour Commissioners. The agreement was last extended in 2017.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Sanscon Construction Ltd., for Construction Services for Watermain and Water Service Replacement on O'Connor Drive
topics: contracts, purchasing, taxes; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, levies
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a $5.5 million non-competitive contract with Sanscon Construction Ltd. to replace the 300-millimetre cast iron watermain on O'Connor Drive between Sandra Road and Bermondsey Road. The accelerated replacement is funded by Toronto Water.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with KPMG LLP for Committee of Adjustment Service Delivery Review
topics: committee meetings, contracts, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a $140,000 non-competitive contract with KPMG for a 20-week service delivery review of the Committee of Adjustment, ending April 1, 2024. The recommendation comes from the Chief Planner and the Chief Procurement Officer.

title: Award of Negotiated Request for Proposal Document Number 3703952212 for Management of Play, Pro Shops and Food and Beverage Services at Five City-Operated Golf Courses
topics: golf courses, proposals, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, bids; request for proposal; rfp, golf centers; golf centres; golf facilities; public golf
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize Parks, Forestry and Recreation to sign a management agreement for play, pro shops and food and beverage services at the City's five golf courses. The current contracts expire at the end of November 2023, and a new supplier is needed to continue services.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Blanket Contract Number 47022700 with Toromont Industries Ltd., for Supply and Delivery of Proprietary Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Specialized Services for Equipment Warranty and Non-Warranty Repair and Maintenance
topics: [parts of roads], contracts, equipment rentals;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council amend the non-competitive blanket contract with Toromont Industries Ltd. for Caterpillar equipment parts and specialized services. The amendment extends the term by five one-year periods, from five to ten years, and increases the contract value by $3,072,164 net of taxes.

title: 4195 and 4221 Dundas Street West and 556, 558, 560, 562 and 564 Prince Edward Drive North - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The applicant for 4195 and 4221 Dundas Street West and 556-564 Prince Edward Drive North appealed the Official Plan and zoning applications to the Ontario Land Tribunal in 2022. The revised proposal includes two 14-storey towers on a six-storey base, two nine-storey buildings and 19 townhouses, totalling 660 residential units. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor to oppose the applications at the Tribunal.

title: 2405-2411 and 2417 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The applicant for 2405-2411 and 2417 Lake Shore Boulevard West appealed the Official Plan, zoning and subdivision applications to the Ontario Land Tribunal. The proposal includes a 10-storey building, a 33-storey tower on an eight-storey base, and 471 residential units including 22 rental replacement units. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor to oppose the applications at the Tribunal.

title: 159 and 161-181 Mulock Avenue and 6 Lloyd Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after Council did not decide on the application within the Planning Act's timelines. The proposal is for two residential buildings with heights of 15 and 17 storeys, containing 535 dwelling units, one office building. Staff recommend that Council direct the City Solicitor to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the application.

title: 111 Plunkett Road - Part Lot Control Exemption - Decision Report - Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control; exceptions
brief: Staff recommend that City Council pass a Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for 111 Plunkett Road to create 42 separately sellable parcels, each containing one semi-detached home. The rest of the subdivision, including the public right-of-way, walkway and Phase 2 lands at 135 Plunkett Road, would stay unchanged.

title: 56, 58 and 60 Fieldway Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving a mixed-use development at 56, 58 and 60 Fieldway Road with four towers of 12, 25, 34 and 42 storeys, 1,297 dwelling units, and a 2,426-square-metre public park. The proposal includes 1,526 square metres of non-residential space and a floor space index of 6.2 times the lot area.

title: 5, 6 and 9 Jopling Avenue South - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving a 39-storey mixed-use building with 434 dwelling units and 250 square metres of ground-floor retail at 5, 7 and 9 Jopling Avenue South. The 26,990-square-metre development sits close to the Kipling Transit Hub in Etobicoke Centre.

title: Longbourne Drive between Willowridge Road and Redgrave Drive - Implementation of Permit Parking
topics: parking, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Councillor Vincent Crisanti recommends that City Council exempt the implementation of permit parking on Longbourne Drive, between Willowridge Road and Redgrave Drive, from the polling requirements in the Permit Parking by-law. No residential properties front the block, so the usual polling cannot be done.

title: Lake Shore Boulevard West - Parking Amendments
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services recommends that the parking be prohibited on the north side of Lake Shore Boulevard West, near the driveway exit of 3580 Lake Shore Boulevard West. The proposed amendment will deter parking at this location and will improve sightlines and vehicle movements by maintaining a clear passage for vehicles. City Council is asked to approve the parking by-law change.

title: 15 Canmotor Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving the demolition of a one-storey banquet hall at 15 Canmotor Avenue for a new two-storey medical office and cardiology clinic with surface parking. The plan provides 92 parking spaces on site plus 14 more within the Caven Street road allowance.

title: Emmett Avenue - Parking Amendment
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Transportation Services recommends that City Council prohibit standing at all times on the north side of Emmett Avenue between Jane Street and a point 45 metres west. The change is meant to deter parking there and improve visibility for vehicles exiting a laneway and eastbound traffic approaching it.

title: On-Street Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (Various Locations) - Parking Amendments (Non-Delegated Locations)
topics: on-street parking, parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend designating on-street parking areas for five electric vehicle charging stations at locations across the city (seven charging stations in total), as supported by local councillors. City Council is asked to approve the parking by-law change.

title: Albion Centre - Metrolinx Finch West Light Rail Transit - Traffic Control Signals Changes
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, light rail transit, pedestrians; lrt, pedestrianization, ttc
brief: Transportation Services recommends installing traffic control signals at Finch Avenue West and a point 300 metres west of Kipling Avenue. City Council is asked to approve the installation.

title: The West Mall and Waulron Street - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, pedestrians, transportation; pedestrianization, transportation services, ttc
brief: Transportation Services recommends that City Council approve traffic control signals at the intersection of The West Mall and Waulron Street, based on its assessment of pedestrian crossing protection needs. The signals are intended to improve safety for vulnerable road users.

title: 175-185 Eileen Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving 58 residential units in two back-to-back townhouse blocks at 175-185 Eileen Avenue, with a height of 12.4 metres and a floor space index of 2.2. The report also recommends classifying the site as a Class 4 Noise Area. The proposal is described as appropriate infill housing compatible with the surrounding area.

title: Wheel-Trans Service Model Update - Accessibility Feedback
topics: accessibility, accessibility standards, specialized paratransit services; accessibility legislation; aoda, accessible public transportation; accessible transit; accessible transit service; door to door service; special mobility services; wheel trans; wheel-trans; wheeltrans, barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible
brief: The Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee recommends that City Council ask the TTC Board to have the TTC's Chief Executive Officer consult the Advisory Committee on Accessible Transit and community organizations serving people with disabilities on the Wheel-Trans service changes. The recommendation follows a TTC presentation on Wheel-Trans service planning changes, the re-registration process and equity analysis.

title: ConnectTO Program Update: City Assets for Efficiency and Connectivity
topics: computer networks, electronic resources, infrastructure, internet; digital resources
brief: Staff report progress on ConnectTO, the City's program to bridge the digital divide, with a focus on expanding free public Wi-Fi and using City assets for connectivity. Staff recommend that City Council direct the Chief Technology Officer to consult the technology community, anti-poverty groups and groups with lived experience of the digital divide, including Indigenous, Black and racialized communities, on next steps.

title: Vacant Home Tax: Status Update
topics: property taxes; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: Staff report on the first year of the Vacant Home Tax, approved in December 2021, with learnings from other jurisdictions and recommended program changes. City Council is asked to approve changes to the tax, effective for vacancies in the 2023 taxation year, including amending the payment due date.

title: Small Business Property Tax Subclass Review
topics: [activities in finance], property taxes, small businesses; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: Staff recommend changes to the Small Business Property Tax Subclass, created in 2021. The changes would exclude land in the commercial tax class that has no building or structure on it from the definition of eligible property, and amend the criteria for inclusion in the subclass.

title: City of Toronto Reserve and Reserve Fund Balances as at June 30, 2023
topics: [rules in finance], budgets, capital budgets, finance (sc), financial reports, reserve funds; annual financial reports; financial statements, budgets and accounts, reserves and reserve funds
brief: The Interim Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports on the City's reserve and reserve fund balances at June 30, 2023, which cushion future capital needs, obligations and unforeseen costs. City Council is asked to consolidate the Doubtful Loan Guarantee Reserve with the Debt Servicing Reserve Fund.

title: Deferred Revenue Report at June 30, 2023
topics: budgets, finance (sc), operating budgets, revenue generation; budgets and accounts, revenue tools
brief: This is an information item: the Deferred Revenue Report at June 30, 2023 covers money the City has received but must set aside for specific future purposes, such as development charges collected with building permits. The Interim Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends that the Executive Committee receive the report for information.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Six Months Ended June 30, 2023
topics: operating budgets;
brief: The Interim Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports on operating spending for the six months ended June 30, 2023 and projections to year-end. The City continues to face significant COVID-19 financial impacts. City Council is asked to approve budget adjustments that have no impact on the City's net operating budget.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Six months Ended June 30, 2023
topics: capital budgets;
brief: The Interim Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports on City capital spending for the six months ended June 30, 2023 and projected year-end expenditures. City Council is asked to approve in-year budget adjustments to the 2023-2032 Adopted Capital Budget and Plan.

title: Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors Meeting September 5-15, 2023
topics: meetings;
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie reports on the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board and committee meetings held virtually from September 5 to 15, 2023, after wildfires forced the cancellation of the in-person Yellowknife event. The Federation adopted a motion supporting the Canadian Wildland Fire Prevention and Mitigation Strategy. Council is asked to receive the information.

title: Larry Grossman Forest Hill Memorial Arena Board of Management Governance Matters: Board Composition, Procedures By-Law, and Updates to Relationship Framework
topics: [activities in management], by-laws, governance, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards, bylaws, governance structure; municipal governance
brief: The City Manager recommends that City Council approve the Larry Grossman Forest Hill Memorial Arena Board's procedures by-law and increase the board's public members to eight, including an additional member from the Forest Hill Figure Skating Club. Council is also asked to let the City Manager make housekeeping amendments to the board's Relationship Framework.

title: Heron Park Outdoor Pool Late Night Swimming and Extended Hours
topics: outdoor pools, swimming pools; aquatic centres; bathing pavilions; pools; public pools, outdoor swimming pools
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie asks that City Council request the Mayor to consider funding late-night swimming at Heron Park Outdoor Pool at 292 Manse Road in the 2024 Parks, Forestry and Recreation budget, including the installation of lighting. The pool currently closes at 8 p.m., and the closest outdoor pool with night swimming is McGregor Park, about 35 minutes away by transit.

title: Transitioning Oversight of the Towing and Vehicle Storage Sector to the Province of Ontario
topics: garages, towing;
brief: The report outlines the Province's new authority over the towing and vehicle storage sectors under the Towing and Storage Safety and Enforcement Act, passed in June 2021, which shifts oversight from municipalities to Ontario. Staff recommend technical by-law amendments moving tow-related conditions from Chapter 545 to Chapter 915 as of January 1. Toronto is one of 20 municipalities that license the sector.

title: Transitioning the Vehicle-for-Hire Industry to Net Zero Emissions by 2030
topics: greenhouse effect, motor vehicles; greenhouse gas emissions, vehicles
brief: Staff recommend that City Council amend the licensing by-law to require net zero emissions for vehicles-for-hire starting January 1, 2030. The industry, covering taxicabs, limousines and private transportation companies like Uber and Lyft, accounts for 4 to 6 percent of the city's transportation emissions.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
topics: business improvement areas, public appointments; bia; business improvement associations
brief: Staff recommend that City Council appoint nominees to the Mount Pleasant Village and Rogers Road and The Eglinton Way Business Improvement Area boards of management, in line with the City's public appointments policy and the BIA provisions of the Municipal Code. The changes are made under Municipal Code Chapter 19, Business Improvement Areas.

title: Aligning Cultural Hotspot, Live Arts Mentor and Youth Cultural Incubators Stabilization Initiative Programs to the Community Grants Policy
topics: [activities in culture], subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: Staff recommend that City Council direct the General Manager, Economic Development and Culture to formally establish Cultural Hotspot as a grant program with four funding streams: Signature, SPARK, Ignite Ideation and Live Arts Mentor. The change aligns three arts initiatives serving vulnerable, equity-deserving artists and organizations with the City's Community Grants Policy.

title: Support for Toronto's Restaurants
topics: improvement, restaurants; cafeterias; dining; eating places; food premises, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: The General Manager, Economic Development and Culture recommends that City Council direct a review of the Winterlicious and Summerlicious programs so they more effectively and equitably support restaurants across Toronto. The recommendation follows two 2022 surveys of the city's restaurant and hospitality industry on pandemic recovery.

title: Why Manufacturing Is Essential To Toronto
topics: economic development, manufacturing industry; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: This is an information item: a presentation on the current status of Toronto's manufacturing sector, covering jobs, opportunities and competitiveness challenges. It highlights how manufacturing supports good jobs and contributes high economic multipliers to a diverse economy. No decision is attached.

title: Toronto’s Film Industry: Protecting a Valuable Asset
topics: entertainment, film and television industry; cinema industry; film and television cluster; film production; movie industry; television industry
brief: This is an information item: the Film Commissioner and Director of Entertainment Industries present an overview of Toronto's film industry, covering jobs, economic impact and cultural value, along with challenges including the SAG-AFTRA and WGA strikes and competition for studio space. No decision is attached.

title: Ombudsman Toronto Report: An Investigation into Toronto Community Housing Corporation's Tenant Human Rights Complaints Process

brief: This is an information item: the Ombudsman has tabled a report on its investigation into the Toronto Community Housing Corporation's tenant human rights complaints process, under the City of Toronto Act. The Ombudsman recommends that City Council receive the report for information.

topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The applicant appealed the planning application to the Ontario Land Tribunal after Council did not decide within the prescribed timelines. The City Solicitor is asking Council for directions on the Tribunal hearing; the legal recommendations are in a confidential attachment.

topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board

topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on heritage alterations to the designated property at 401 Yonge Street and a heritage easement agreement, and authorize their public release if adopted. The matter follows a March 2023 settlement of the Official Plan appeal for the lands.

title: Court Decision regarding the Decision to Provide Financial Support to the Legal Challenge against Quebec’s Bill 21
topics: legal matters; legal issues
brief: The City Solicitor reports on the July 13, 2023 Ontario Superior Court decision concerning Toronto's commitment of up to $100,000 to fund the legal challenge to Quebec's Bill 21 by the National Council of Canadian Muslims, the World Sikh Organization and the Canadian Civil Liberties Organization. The Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Property Standards Committee
topics: appointments;
brief: The Nominating Panel - Property Standards Committee will recommend seven candidates to City Council for appointment to the Property Standards Committee. The panel considered the item at its meeting on September 28, 2023.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Committee of Adjustment
topics: appointments;
brief: The Nominating Panel - Committee of Adjustment will recommend 35 candidates to City Council for appointment to the Committee of Adjustment. The panel considered the item at its meetings on September 14, 15 and 18, 2023.

title: Report on Former Mayor John Tory’s Conduct concerning a Personal Relationship
topics: integrity commissioners, mayors;
brief: The Integrity Commissioner recommends that City Council adopt findings that former Mayor John Tory violated Articles VIII and XV of the Code of Conduct for Members of Council concerning a personal relationship with a member of his political staff. Mr. Tory requested the investigation himself when announcing his resignation and accepts the findings.

title: Addressing Workplace Harassment and Discrimination
topics: harassment, integrity commissioners, workplaces; job sites; telework; work from home; worksites
brief: The Integrity Commissioner recommends that City Council ask the Province of Ontario to amend the City of Toronto Act to give municipalities effective tools to address workplace harassment and discrimination by Members of Council and local board members. Unlike other Ontario workers, councillors face no effective disciplinary measures.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Recommendations on Five Deferred Employment Area Conversion Requests - Final Report
topics: employment areas; employment districts; employment zones
brief: Staff recommend that City Council declare the Municipal Comprehensive Review concluded, with exceptions for 388 Carlaw Avenue and 10 Dickens Street and two remaining conversion requests. The report gives final recommendations on five deferred employment area conversion requests, including lands on Chesswood Drive, Queens Plate Drive, Islington Avenue, Evans Avenue and Finch Avenue West.

title: 1117 Queen Street West - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection

brief: Staff recommend that City Council designate 1117 Queen Street West under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act, using a revised Statement of Significance that responds to the property owner's objection. title: Support for a Canada-Wide Universal Student Nutrition Program

brief: Mayor Olivia Chow recommends that City Council join cities across Canada in calling on the federal government to implement a National School Food Program and fund it in Budget 2024. In Toronto, 28 percent of food bank clients are children and youth, and more children are going to school hungry.

title: Appointment of Members to the Toronto Film, Television and Digital Media Board

brief: City Council is asked to appoint 22 individuals to the Toronto Film, Television and Digital Media Board for the remainder of the current term of City Council for a term ending November 14, 2026. The nominees are named in a confidential attachment.

title: Appointment of Members to the Toronto Music Advisory Committee

brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to appoint the members of the public listed in a confidential attachment to the Toronto Music Advisory Committee, at pleasure of Council, for terms ending November 14, 2026. The appointments are for the remainder of the current term of City Council.

brief: The Civic Appointments Committee will interview candidates and recommend three candidates to City Council for appointment to the Toronto Zoo Board of Management for a term ending July 21, 2027. The nominees are named in a confidential attachment.

brief: City Council is asked to appoint 8 individuals to the Toronto Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee for a term ending November 14, 2026, or until their mandate is completed, whichever comes first. The nominees are named in a confidential attachment.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills

brief: This is a procedural item: Council introduces the general bills and the confirming bill that formally records the decisions of the meeting. This is the standard formal step used to give effect to Council's decisions at the end of a meeting.

title: Request to Consider Heritage Designation at 3100 Weston Road - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends City Council ask the Chief Planner to evaluate the property at 3100 Weston Road — already listed on the Heritage Register — for designation under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act, and report to the Toronto Preservation Board. The property includes the Carmine Stefano Community Centre (formerly Saint Basil-The-Great College School), the 1928 Rivermede house (the Gardiner family's summer home), the Marian Shrine of Gratitude, a parking lot, and soccer fields near the Humber River.

title: Granting Temporary Exemption to Mokaben Inc. and By The Way Café to components of Chapter 742 and Chapter 693 of the City of Toronto Municipal Code - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: exemptions, municipal codes; exceptions
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends City Council grant Mokaben Inc. and By The Way Café at 400 Bloor Street West a temporary exemption, from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2024, from any location and use restrictions on their existing sidewalk patio created by Chapter 742 and Chapter 693 of the Municipal Code. The patio has operated in the same location for many years, predating the City's sidewalk patio guidelines, and does not adversely affect pedestrian access.

title: Amending TE31.11 - 83-97 River Street and 2-4 Labatt Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Final Report - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: applications, demolitions, housing, rentals; application process, homes; residences
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, recommends City Council amend its March 2022 approval of the rental housing demolition at 83–97 River Street and 2–4 Labatt Avenue. All tenants have relocated and the units at 83, 85, 87, and 89 River Street are vacant; due to health and safety concerns, the applicant wants to demolish those four vacant units and a non-residential building at 2–4 Labatt Avenue ahead of the remaining three units.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item PH5.3 - Our Plan Toronto: Recommendations on Seventy Employment Area Conversion Requests and Chapter 7 Site and Area Specific Policy Review - Final Report - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: employment areas; employment districts; employment zones
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends City Council reopen its July 2023 adoption of Official Plan Amendment 653 on employment area conversion requests, to replace Attachment 3 to Motion 1 with the attached document and amend Part 7 of its decision. OPA 653 remains subject to approval and potential modification by the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2023.CC8.23 - 906 Yonge Street and 25 McMurrich Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends City Council reopen its July 2023 acceptance of a with-prejudice settlement of the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 906 Yonge Street and 25 McMurrich Street. Certain confidential recommendations regarding an application to alter on-site heritage resources were omitted by inadvertence, and further instruction is needed before the matter returns to the Tribunal on September 26, 2023.

title: Urgently Building More Affordable Homes
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Mayor Chow recommends City Council direct the City Manager, working with all City agencies, boards, corporations, and divisions, to assess preliminary cost estimates and create a plan, implementation framework, and timeline to urgently build more affordable homes amid an unprecedented housing crisis — with neighbours losing homes, refugees in shelters, seniors working past retirement, and young people leaving the city.

title: Updated Long-Term Financial Plan
topics: fees, financial reports, revenue generation; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, annual financial reports; financial statements, revenue tools
brief: The City Manager and the Interim Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommend City Council acknowledge the City's $46.5 billion combined operating and capital pressure over 10 years and commit to exploring and implementing solutions to the fiscal gap, and approve graduated Municipal Land Transfer Tax rates. An independent third-party-supported analysis presented in March 2023 produced the City's first 10-year consolidated operating and capital financial model, with pressures built up over decades.

title: 20 Broadoaks Drive and 11 Catford Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council adopt the confidential recommendations regarding the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the Official Plan and zoning applications for 20 Broadoaks Drive and 11 Catford Road — a 12-storey mixed-use building on Keele Street, two residential towers of 18 and 30 storeys on a six-storey base, and two four-storey townhouse blocks, with existing apartment buildings retained. Council is asked to authorize public release of the confidential recommendations if adopted.

title: Immediate Federal Government Support Required for Refugee Claimants in Toronto
brief: The City Manager and the Deputy City Manager for Community and Social Services recommend City Council request the federal government to fund and implement a regional response for refugee claimants in the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area, including full reimbursement of the City's costs. The City's shelter system is full; the number of refugee claimants in the shelter system has risen to 3,300, with almost 1,200 more supported outside the system, and the City projects up to 4,500 refugee claimants in the system by year-end — 50 percent of total shelter space.

title: Appointment of Interim Deputy City Manager, Corporate Services
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Manager recommends City Council appoint David Jollimore as Interim Deputy City Manager, Corporate Services, effective October 6 to November 5, 2023, and Patrick Matozzo as Interim Deputy City Manager, Corporate Services, for the period following. The appointments are urgent because the current Deputy City Manager, Josie Scioli, retires effective October 6, 2023, before the next Council meeting.
