topics: reserve funds, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, reserves and reserve funds
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, recommends City Council increase the 2023 Operating Budget by $150,000 gross ($0 net) to release Section 37 funds to the Toronto District School Board for Islington Junior Middle School's Greenspace Redevelopment Initiative. The funds were secured from the development at 1286–1294 Islington Avenue and 15–19 Cordova Avenue; the school's grounds are the only green space accessible to the entire community.

title: Accepting Donations for Shelter and Support for Refugees - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: emergency housing, refugees; emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless)
brief: This is a procedural item: Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council authorize the City Manager to accept financial and in-kind donations — including donations over $50,000 — for shelter and other support for refugees, refugee claimants, and asylum seekers, facilitating the generosity of Toronto residents and organizations.

title: Reopening and Amending Item 2023.TE5.8  - 500 Macpherson Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: Official Plans, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, recommends City Council reopen its June 2023 approval of the 500 Macpherson Avenue Official Plan and zoning amendments and replace the draft Zoning By-law Amendments attached as Attachments 6 and 7. Staff discovered that the schedules attached to the staff report contained draft by-laws for a different address; the report itself contained sufficient information for the public and Council to understand the proposal.

title: Creating a Pathway for the Beach Business Improvement Area to Install a Parkette on Queen Street East, west of Beech Avenue - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: business improvement areas, parks; bia; business improvement associations, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends City Council exempt a proposed curb lane public parklet on the north side of Queen Street East, west of Beech Avenue (fronting but not affiliated with 2232 Queen Street East), from platform requirements in Chapter 742 for the 2023 summer season. The Beach BIA requested the exemption so the parklet can be installed in time to provide seating for families and patrons during the busy summer season.

title: Reopening and Amending MM7.39 - Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 316 Bloor Street West - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: bike lanes, infrastructure; bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council reopen its June 2023 approval releasing Section 37 funds from the development at 316 Bloor Street West, to replace the words "neighbouring residents' association" with the word "community" and correct an error in the original motion.

title: Protecting the Science Centre to Support Thorncliffe and Flemingdon Park - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: life sciences sector, parks; biomedical and biotechnology cluster; biomedical industry; biotech; biotechnology industry; life-science sector; pharmaceutical industry, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, recommends City Council ask the City Manager to report to the Executive Committee in the third quarter of 2023 on the future of the Ontario Science Centre, including provincial lease requirements. The Province announced its intention to move the Science Centre to a smaller location at Ontario Place without consulting residents of Thorncliffe and Flemingdon Park, who rely on the Centre for employment and education opportunities.

title: Providing More Public Access to Fairbank Memorial Park During Trunk Sewer Construction Project - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: construction, parks, sewers; building, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, sewage systems; sewerage
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council ask the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to provide public access to the fenced baseball diamond in Fairbank Memorial Park during non-permitted periods, with signage on hours and dog rules. Public access to the park has been drastically reduced by construction of the Fairbank Silverthorn Storm Trunk Sewer, which runs until 2026, while the community is also still affected by the Metrolinx Crosstown project.

title: Expanding the Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program Eligibility Criteria to include Registered Owners of Existing Residential Fourplexes - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: basement flooding, residential properties; basement flood cleanup; basement flooding response, residential real estate
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow, recommends City Council ask the General Manager of Toronto Water to review the feasibility of expanding the Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program to include registered owners of existing residential fourplexes. The program currently provides up to $3,400 per eligible property for flood protection devices to owners of single-family homes, duplexes, and triplexes; Council recently permitted fourplexes to facilitate more low-rise housing.

title: Supporting Toronto’s Film and Television Production Industry in Response to Current Labour Disruptions - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Shelley Carroll
topics: film and television industry, labour disruptions; cinema industry; film and television cluster; film production; movie industry; television industry, labor disruptions; lockouts; strikes
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council direct the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to support Toronto's film and television production workers, creators, events, organizations, and businesses affected by the concurrent Writers Guild of America strike (from May 2) and Screen Actors Guild strike (from July 13), by collaborating with local unions and not-for-profit partners on worker supports.

title: Supporting the Development of Phase 2 of the Lawrence Heights Revitalization - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: redevelopment; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council support Phase 2 of the Lawrence Heights revitalization — a partnership between the City and Toronto Community Housing that includes a new community centre in Phase 2a — by authorizing the Executive Director of Toronto Building to waive fees for the rental housing demolition application at 3 and 5 Leila Lane and 31–109 Bagot Court (odd). The City has applied to the federal government for funding for the project.

title: Accommodating the 2023 Just for Laughs Street Festival - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: festivals and special events, road closures; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council direct the General Manager of Transportation Services to waive additional municipal fees related to temporary traffic adjustments for the Just for Laughs Street Festival, held September 21–25, 2023. The festival features music, stand-up comedy, and performance art with local and international artists.

title: Authority to enter into an Agreement with The Regional Municipality of York - Cost Share on the Steeles Avenue Grade Separation - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: agreements, grade separations, transportation; tenancy agreements, transportation services
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council authorize the General Manager of Transportation Services to negotiate and execute a cost-share agreement with the Regional Municipality of York for the Steeles Avenue East grade separation, being built by Metrolinx as part of the GO Expansion Program. The project is nearing completion, with substantial completion expected in July 2023, and the City will take ownership and maintenance of the municipal components.

title: Safety Improvements to Complete Streets, Ward 3 and Ward 4 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: improvement, safety; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), public safety
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends City Council amend traffic and parking regulations in Municipal Code Chapter 950 for safety improvements on Bloor Street West at South Kingsway/Mossom Road and The Kingsway, as part of the Bloor Street West Complete Street Extension. The improvements were developed through stakeholder and public consultation but were not included in the delegated authority Council approved earlier.

title: Installation of Two Commercial Loading Zones - Danforth Avenue - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: loading zones; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, recommends City Council approve two all-times commercial loading zones on the north side of Danforth Avenue — between 14 metres west of Carlaw Avenue and a point 15 metres further west, and a second location — providing six additional parking spots for commercial deliveries. Greektown on the Danforth businesses have had difficulty receiving deliveries due to limited curb space, and the motion is urgent ahead of summer.

title: Supporting the Development of Affordable Housing - Assistance to Brenyon Way's Project at 25 Sewells Road - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: affordable housing, development; affordable homes; housing projects, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This is a procedural item: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends City Council waive City fees and charges for tie-back and crane swing agreements for the Brenyon Way affordable housing project at 25 Sewells Road. The development proposes 318 units across two phases, approved through the City's Open Door Program, and the property abuts Wickson Trail Park.

title: Authority to Amend the 2023-2032 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation for Alexandra Park Improvements Body - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: budgets, improvement; budgets and accounts, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends City Council amend the 2023–2032 Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation by $145,000 gross ($0 debt) for Alexandra Park improvements, raising the total project cost from $1,000,000 to $1,145,000 with cash flow commitments in 2024. The funds come from Section 42 cash-in-lieu received from nearby developments.

title: 962 College Street - Liquor Licence Application - Fat Seoul Restaurant - Licence 2069404 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends City Council direct the City Clerk to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that issuing a liquor licence to Fat Seoul Restaurant at 962 College Street (indoor area) is not in the public interest unless certain conditions addressing community concerns — noise, litter, safety, and disturbances near residential units — are attached to the licence.

title: Securing Shelter and Support for Refugees - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: housing, refugees; homes; residences
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council direct the City Manager to immediately make temporary shelter available for at least 150 refugees, and then find locations for 100 more. Toronto's dedicated refugee shelter space and base shelter system are full; each night over 300 people are turned away, more than half of them refugees and refugee claimants, and upwards of 100 refugees wait and sleep outside the Streets to Homes Assessment and Referral Centre on any given evening.

title: Deadly Tanker Truck Crashes on Highway 401 - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: collisions, commercial vehicles, highways; automobile collisions; car accidents; car crashes; crashes; cycling accidents; road accidents; road fatalities; traffic accidents; traffic casualties; traffic fatalities; transit accidents, commercial motor vehicles, freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends City Council request the Province of Ontario to require tanker trucks hauling toxic and flammable materials to use Highway 407 instead of Highway 401 through Toronto. The motion follows a fatal June 20 crash near Pickering in which a fuel tanker rolled over, ruptured, and caught fire, killing two drivers. Highway 401 travels through 15 of Toronto's 25 wards.

title: 1192 Queen Street West -  Liquor Licence Application - Beaver Café T.B.K.A. Eleven Ninety-Two (Licence 2150657) - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: boulevard cafes, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants)
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council direct the City Clerk to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that issuing a liquor licence to Beaver Café T.B.K.A. Eleven Ninety-Two at 1192 Queen Street West (indoor area) is not in the public interest unless certain conditions addressing community concerns — noise, litter, safety, and disturbances near residential units — are attached to the licence.

title: 2 Cora Crescent - Request City Solicitor to appeal Committee of Adjustment decision to the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment, hearings; committee of adjustment
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council authorize the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's June 28 decision approving minor variances for 2 Cora Crescent (application A0349/21SC) to the Toronto Local Appeal Body, and to attend as a party to oppose it. The motion is urgent given the 20-day appeal period.

title: Supporting the Development of Supportive Housing - Assistance to Reena's Project at 165 Elm Ridge Drive - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council waive City fees and charges for real estate agreements — tie-back, crane swing, and construction staging — for Reena's supportive housing project at 165 Elm Ridge Drive. The development proposes 111 units, including 106 net new supportive housing units for people with developmental disabilities, approved through the City's Open Door Program.

title: Building Up Our Parks and Our Communities - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends City Council direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation and the Chief Financial Officer to hold funds allocated for capital improvements in Muirlands Park (PR 222) in trust until a suitable trustee organization can be selected, following the City's Social Development Strategy approach of fostering local participation in park design.

title: Interim Relocation of YMCA to St. Patrick's Market by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Alejandra Bravo
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council authorize the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management to increase the construction agreement with the YMCA of Greater Toronto for capital repair work at St. Patrick's Market, 238 Queen Street West, to support the interim relocation of the YMCA. The relocation is needed because redevelopment of 260 Adelaide Street West requires moving the Adelaide Fire Hall to Metro Hall, displacing the YMCA's ground-floor space there.

title: Request to Review the Nomination Requirements for Mayoral Candidates - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: by-elections; by elections; byelections
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas, recommends City Council ask the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing to review the nomination filing fee and number of endorsements required for mayoral candidates. The June 26, 2023 mayoral by-election ballot listed 102 candidates on a single page, causing confusion and voter frustration and possibly contributing to voting errors or deterring voters.

title: Summer Consultations, Happened so Fast! - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: summer;
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council ask the City Manager to ensure public consultations scheduled for summer 2023 — notably the Noise By-Law consultation — are held primarily in the fall of 2023, with all Councillors advised of the change by July 31, 2023, so interested residents have a genuine opportunity for input.

title: Acquiring Strategic New Parkland for Residents Moving into Dense Neighbourhood on the East Side of Yonge North Secondary Plan - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: parkland dedication;
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends City Council direct Parks, Forestry and Recreation and Corporate Real Estate Management, in consultation with the local Councillor, to identify parkland acquisition opportunities on the east side of the Yonge North Secondary Plan. Nearby parks will not be sufficient to serve the projected 24,000–25,000 residents in the development pipeline.

title: Authority to Enter Into Nominal Fee Licence Agreements with Four Existing Food Bank Operators at Six Parks, Forestry and Recreation Locations - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: food banks, recreation & tourism (sc); foodshare
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends City Council authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to negotiate and sign nominal fee licence agreements with four existing food bank operators at six Parks, Forestry and Recreation locations. Community spaces were made available at no cost during the COVID-19 pandemic for food security initiatives, and the need for accessible local space continues.

title: Allocate Section 37 Funds for City-owned site at 5200 Yonge Street to allow Scarborough Food Security Initiatives (Feed Scarborough) to Support Success of City-initiated Food Incubator Program - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: funding; financing
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, recommends City Council increase the 2023 Operating Budget by $60,000 gross ($0 net), funded by Section 37 funds from the development at 75 Canterbury Place, to allow Feed Scarborough to install necessities supporting the City-initiated food incubator program at the City-owned site at 5200 Yonge Street. The incubator gives entrepreneurs from equity-seeking groups a chance to establish food businesses.

title: 17 Courtsfield Crescent - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: hearings, municipal officials; city officials
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the appeal of a new detached dwelling proposal at 17 Courtsfield Crescent. The Committee of Adjustment refused the requested variances to lot coverage and floor space index on June 22, 2023, and City Planning staff found the proposal did not fit the neighbourhood context.

title: Prioritizing Non-Profit Housing in the Concept 2 Keys (C2K) Program - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: housing, non-profit organizations; homes; residences, non profit; nonprofit; not-for-profit organizations
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends City Council ask the Deputy City Manager for Infrastructure Services to provide a breakdown and analysis of non-profit and co-operative housing development applications in the Concept 2 Keys program and measures to remove barriers to their approval. Non-profit and co-op housing organizations face significant municipal and financial barriers to building affordable housing in Toronto's market.

title: Mount Dennis “Community for All Action Plan” - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: community development, community improvement plans; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends City Council direct the Deputy City Manager for Community and Social Services to engage with the Ward 5 Councillor, community organizations, residents, and businesses on a Mount Dennis Community for All Action Plan. The Eglinton LRT construction has brought development pressure and land speculation to the once-affordable neighbourhood, with new private developments expected to house some 20,000 new residents compared to one non-profit affordable housing proposal.

title: Making it Official: Establishing Danforth Avenue, between Main Street and Pharmacy Avenue, as Banglatown - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: community partners, naming;
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, recommends City Council ask the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture, in consultation with local Councillors' offices, to engage community organizations on designating Danforth Avenue between Main Street and Pharmacy Avenue as Banglatown. The area, home to Canada's largest Bangla community, welcomed Toronto's International Mother Language Monument in Dentonia Park in November 2021.

title: Authorization to Transfer Funds from Parks, Forestry and Recreation to Waterfront Toronto for the Legacy Art Project Toronto - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: arts and culture, funding, waterfronts; financing, lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council authorize a $75,000 transfer to Waterfront Toronto to repair and upgrade an existing accessibility ramp as part of the Legacy Art Project Toronto commemorating Terry Fox at 439 Queens Quay West. Council previously authorized a $340,907 Section 37 transfer to Waterfront Toronto for the project, a collaboration with the Legacy Art Project Toronto foundation backed by the Terry Fox family.

title: 1646 Queen Street East, Casa Di Giorgio - CaféTO Curb Lane Café - Waiving Platform Requirements - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: liquor sales licences, street occupation permits; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends City Council exempt the curb lane CaféTO patio at Casa Di Giorgio, 1646 Queen Street East, from platform requirements in Chapter 742 for the 2023 season. The restaurant participated in the program successfully in previous years; relief is needed because of upcoming sidewalk widening work on the north side of Queen Street East, and the matter is time sensitive.

title: Reimbursement of Cities Forum 2023 Conference Expenses, Torino, Italy - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: business travel (municipal), councillors, expenses, funding; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, corporate travel, financing
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council authorize payment of his and his Chief of Staff's expenses for attending the Cities Forum 2023 conference in Torino, Italy, in March 2023. A missed return flight required an additional flight and an extra night's accommodation, pushing the total above $7,000 and triggering the requirement for Council approval under the Constituency Services and Office Budget Policy.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to St. Clare's Multifaith Society for the Purchase of 1112 Ossington Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: funding; financing
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council authorize $800,000 from the Capital Revolving Reserve Fund for Affordable Housing to St. Clare's Multifaith Housing Society to acquire 1112 Ossington Avenue. The purchase would combine with the existing Monaco Place affordable housing project at 1120 Ossington Avenue, creating fully wheelchair-accessible amenity space — gathering space, a kitchen, and laundry facilities — plus on-site support staff space.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2023.CC7.14 - 100 Davenport Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council reopen item CC7.14, adopted June 14–15, 2023, which accepted a with-prejudice settlement of an Ontario Land Tribunal appeal concerning 100 Davenport Road. Certain amendments were omitted from the approval by inadvertence, and this is the first opportunity to add them, including a request that Transportation Services review the feasibility of amending Schedule B of the City's traffic by-laws.

title: 399 Jane Street - Liquor Licence Application - Gigli Café - Licence 2192032 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: boulevard cafes, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants)
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council direct the City Clerk to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that issuing a liquor licence to Gigli Café at 399 Jane Street (indoor and outdoor areas) is not in the public interest unless certain conditions addressing community concerns — noise, litter, safety, and disturbances near residential units — are attached to the licence.

title: Streetscape Design Gaps
topics: landscape design, urban design, urban form; civic improvements, landscape architecture; landscape projects, streetscapes; urban landscape
brief: This is a procedural item: the Infrastructure and Environment Committee directs the Chief Planner and the General Manager of Transportation Services, in consultation with Urban Forestry, to report back in the fourth quarter of 2023 on how the City should plan and achieve improved, connected, and harmonious streetscapes on streets converting to residential use, such as Dupont. Current streetscapes on such streets are described as inadequate for pedestrians and cyclists, with narrow or obstructed sidewalks and no street trees or seating, and no City department currently owns responsibility for them.

title: Planning for an E-Scooter Pilot
topics: accessibility, electric scooters, sidewalks; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, go peds; go-peds; motorized scooters; scooters
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends the Infrastructure and Environment Committee direct the General Manager of Transportation Services, in consultation with other divisions, agencies, and stakeholders including the Accessibility Advisory Committee, to develop a plan for an e-scooter pilot. Toronto chose not to join the province's 2020 e-scooter pilot over disability-community concerns about sidewalk riding and clutter, and e-scooters remain unlawful to operate in public space, though many are privately owned and used.

title: Two-Stroke Engine Small Equipment: Steps to Pursue a Ban
topics: climate, environment (sc), leaf blowers;
brief: The Executive Director of Environment and Climate recommends City Council choose an option to address two-stroke engine equipment — leaf blowers, lawnmowers, and other small engines — because of their adverse impact on air quality and human health. This report is the first of a two-step process: Council is asked to direct whether it wishes to pursue a ban on two-stroke engines in Toronto, with consultation and resourcing to follow. Option A includes the City phasing out gas-powered leaf blowers for municipal use.

title: Service Agreements Awarded and Executed by the Medical Officer of Health for 2023
topics: contracts, health, services; health coverage
brief: This is an information item: the Medical Officer of Health reports to City Council on the service contracts awarded and executed for 2023 under Council's delegation of authority. City Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Award of Negotiated Request for Proposal Doc 36872270278 to Enterprise Rent-A-Car Canada Company for Supply of Various Rental Vehicles
topics: city vehicles, proposals; bids; request for proposal; rfp, city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet
brief: This is a procedural item: the General Manager of Fleet Services and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend City Council authorize a two-year agreement with Enterprise Rent-A-Car Canada Company, from October 1, 2023 to September 30, 2025 with renewal options, for the non-exclusive on-demand supply and delivery of short-term rental vehicles for various City divisions. Enterprise was the highest-ranked supplier meeting the requirements.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with R Courier for the Provision of Courier Services for the Distribution and Transportation of Vaccine and Non-Medical Supplies for Toronto Public Health
topics: contracts, immunizations, public health; flu shots; shots; vaccinations; vaccines
brief: This is a procedural item: the Medical Officer of Health and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend City Council authorize a non-competitive ten-month agreement with R Courier, from June 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024, for $500,000 (net of HST), to provide courier services distributing vaccines and non-medical supplies from a central warehouse to fixed-site and mobile clinics across Toronto. The clinics provide COVID-19 vaccinations and School Immunization Program vaccines.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Kone Inc. for Escalator Maintenance and Repair Work at Union Station
topics: gross floor area, purchasing, stationary businesses; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, adult entertainment parlours; automobile body repair shops; bake shops; billiard halls; body rub parlours; car washes; coin-operated laundries; convenience stores; drug stores; handbill distributors; holistic centres; massage parlours; motor vehicle dealerships; non moving businesses; pawnbrokers; pet shops; public bath houses; public garages; salvage yards; second hand shops; sign painters; variety stores
brief: This is a procedural item: the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend City Council authorize a non-competitive purchase order of $43,588 (net of all taxes) to Kone Inc. for escalator maintenance and repair work at Union Station. The services were performed during the warranty period but determined not to be covered under the warranty, as the need was not preventable through routine maintenance.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Blanket Contract Number 47024284 with Canadian Red Cross Society
topics: accommodation providers, emergency housing, homelessness; accommodation services; bed and breakfasts; hotel rooms; hotels; lodging (short term); motels; resorts; student hostels; tourist accommodation; traveller accommodation, emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless)
brief: This is a procedural item: the General Manager of Shelter, Support and Housing Administration and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend City Council authorize amending the non-competitive blanket contract with the Canadian Red Cross Society for emergency services for Ukrainian arrivals needing emergency shelter. The Red Cross operates shelter services at a hotel site near the airport with a block of 70 rooms; as of June 16, 2023, 181 individuals from 68 households were on site.

title: Emergency Repairs to Raw Water Valves at F. J. Horgan Treatment Plant
topics: repairs, water, water treatment plants; filtration plants; water filtration plants; water treatment and supply plants; water treatment facilities
brief: This is an information item: the General Manager of Toronto Water and the Chief Procurement Officer advise City Council of an amendment to Purchase Order 6050742 with CIMA Canada Inc. (CIMA+), adding $530,503 for contract administration related to emergency repairs to raw water valves at the F.J. Horgan Treatment Plant, raising the purchase order value to $1,067,017. City Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Occupational Health and Safety Report: End of Year 2022
topics: annual reports, safety; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, public safety
brief: This is an information item: the Chief People Officer provides City Council with the end-of-year 2022 Occupational Health and Safety Report. Lost time injuries rose 25.4 percent in 2022 relative to 2021, primarily due to workplace COVID-19 exposures; recurrences fell 13.3 percent and medical aid injuries rose 1.5 percent. City Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 217, Records (Corporate)
topics: change, municipal codes, records; amendments; conversion; modification
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Clerk recommends City Council amend Municipal Code Chapter 217, Records (Corporate), to establish a process for deeming digitized copies as original records and enabling the disposition of source physical records.

title: 5230 Dundas Street West, 3825 Bloor Street West and 0 Beamish Drive - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [buildings by height], official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve a multi-phased development at 5230 Dundas Street West, 3825 Bloor Street West, and 0 Beamish Drive, with five buildings across four development blocks: two eight-storey mid-rises along Bloor Street West and towers of 25, 36, 41, 43, and 45 storeys. The proposal includes 2,387 residential units, 4,859 square metres of non-residential floor area, a J-shaped public road, and 1,900 square metres of public parkland. City Council is asked to approve the planning changes and draft plan of subdivision.

title: 408 Horner Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: construction, zoning bylaws; building, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve a two-storey addition containing six units at the rear of the existing two-storey triplex at 408 Horner Avenue. The proposal would demolish one existing rental unit and contain nine dwelling units in total (seven new and two retained rental units), five at-grade parking spaces, and a new rear yard amenity area. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: Driftwood Avenue - No Stopping
topics: stopping prohibitions, traffic management; no stopping, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Perruzza recommends City Council prohibit stopping at all times on both sides of Driftwood Avenue between Yewtree Boulevard and London Green Court, and rescind the existing all-times parking prohibition on the west side of Driftwood Avenue. Residents raised safety concerns near Venetian Crescent, where narrowed road markings, parked cars, and a busy bus route created dangerous conditions.

title: 315-327 Royal York Road and 27-39 Newcastle Street - Community Benefits and Class 4 Area Noise Classification - Request for Direction Report
topics: noise, report requests; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise
brief: City Planning recommends City Council allow the owner of 315–327 Royal York Road and 27–39 Newcastle Street to provide community benefits as an in-kind contribution under the Planning Act for the Transit Oriented Community development that includes integrated entrances and amenities for Mimico GO station. The zoning was approved through a Minister's Zoning Order on April 8, 2022. The recommended approach includes the design and construction of a pedestrian and cyclist bridge over Royal York Road.

title: Colonel Samuel Smith Park Drive - Parking Amendments
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Colonel Samuel Smith Park Drive. Transportation Services recommends City Council replace the all-times parking prohibition on the west side of Colonel Samuel Smith Park Drive, between Lake Shore Boulevard West and a point 49 metres south, with an all-times stopping prohibition to improve transit operations.

title: 240 Markland Drive - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, reconstruction; building, rebuilding
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Bloor Street West. Carttera Management is building a nine-storey rental apartment building at 240 Markland Drive. Transportation Services asks City Council to temporarily close the south sidewalk on Bloor Street West east of Markland Drive for 24 months, from August 1, 2023 to July 31, 2025, for construction staging.

title: 2801 Jane Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: apartment neighbourhoods, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve an 11-storey (35.4-metre) apartment building with 224 dwelling units, 19,230 square metres of gross floor area, and a one-level underground garage with 119 parking spaces at 2801 Jane Street. The existing 17-storey apartment building would be retained. City Council is asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 1001-1037 The Queensway - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, reconstruction; building, rebuilding
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit service on Islington Avenue. RioCan is building two mixed-use condominium buildings with ground-floor retail at 1001–1037 The Queensway (an 8- and 10-storey west building and a 10- and 17-storey east building). Transportation Services asks City Council to temporarily close the east sidewalk and part of the northbound curb lane on Dorchester Avenue from July 20, 2023 to May 31, 2025 for construction staging.

title: 555 Rexdale Boulevard (Non-Delegated) - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic control systems, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council approval is required because the TTC operates bus service on Rexdale Boulevard, Highway 27, and Queen's Plate Drive. Transportation Services asks City Council to authorize traffic control signals at Highway 27 and New Providence Trail/Nearctic Drive, and to rescind existing turn and through traffic prohibitions at Rexdale Boulevard and Queen's Plate Drive (west intersection).

title: 1860, 1860A, 1862, 1864, 1866, 1866A and 1868 Keele Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Planning recommends City Council approve a 19-storey mixed-use building with 245 dwelling units and 407 square metres of ground-floor retail at 1860–1868 Keele Street, with a total gross floor area of 17,667 square metres. The building is described as supportable intensification adjacent to the Keelesdale Light Rail Transit Station and Bus Terminal. City Council is asked to approve the zoning changes and rental housing demolition application.

title: 2023 Levy on Railway Roadways and Rights-of-Way and on Power Utility Transmission and Distribution Corridors
topics: development charges, railways; rail fares; railroads
brief: This is a procedural item: the Controller recommends City Council authorize the levy and collection of 2023 taxes on railway roadways and rights-of-way and on land used as transmission or distribution corridors owned by power utilities, totalling about $7.00 million in taxation revenue — a $6.49 million municipal share and a $0.51 million provincial education share. The 2023 levy decreased slightly from the 2022 total of $7.05 million due to reduced acreage subject to the levy.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Four Months Ended April 30, 2023
topics: operating budgets;
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports the operating variance for the four months ended April 30, 2023, with projections to year-end, and recommends City Council approve amendments to the 2023 Approved Operating Budget that have no impact on the City's net budget. The City continues to face added costs and revenue losses from the lasting impacts of COVID-19, and the 2023 budget was balanced on the expectation of continued federal and provincial support funding.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Four months Ended April 30, 2023
topics: capital budgets;
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports the City's capital spending for the four months ended April 30, 2023, with projected expenditures to December 31, 2023, and recommends City Council approve in-year budget adjustments to the 2023–2032 Adopted Capital Budget and Plan as detailed in the report's Appendix 4.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Twelve Months Ended December 31, 2022
topics: operating budgets;
brief: The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports the City's 2022 operating variance, with significant financial impacts from the lasting effects of COVID-19: the City budgeted $1.4 billion in federal and provincial COVID-19 support but received only $850.3 million. The recommendation is that City Council approve a one-time redirection of $300 million in 2022 budgeted Capital from Current funds and a one-time withdrawal of $95.3 million in COVID-19-related funding, due to the absence of further 2022 support funding.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Twelve months Ended December 31, 2022
topics: capital budgets;
brief: The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends City Council approve in-year adjustments to the 2022–2031 Capital Budget and Plan. The City's 2022 capital expenditure was $3.602 billion, or 64.4 percent of the $5.597 billion 2022 capital budget; tax-supported programs and agencies spent $2.524 billion, or 62.3 percent of their $4.051 billion approved capital budget. Council is also asked to direct $300 million in Capital from Current funding to the COVID-19 response.

title: Authorization to pursue designation as a Model City for the United Nations Environment Programme's Generation Restoration Project
topics: environment (sc);
brief: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie recommends City Council authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to submit an Expression of Interest for Toronto to become a Model City under the United Nations Environment Programme's Generation Restoration Project, and to negotiate and sign the appropriate agreements. Toronto is described as a recognized leader in ecological restoration, biodiversity planning, and urban forest and ravine management, alongside the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority.

title: Request for a Line of Credit Guarantee for Toronto Artscape Inc.
topics: credit, non-profit organizations; non profit; nonprofit; not-for-profit organizations, tax credit
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Carroll recommends City Council approve a line of credit guarantee in support of Toronto Artscape Inc. to its lender. Artscape is a not-for-profit developer managing 14 properties with 390 tenants in affordable housing and working spaces; expansion in 2017–2019 and COVID-19 shutdown disruptions left it facing cash flow and debt repayment challenges, and its board has adopted a restructuring plan.

title: Non-competitive Contract with Gensler Architecture & Design Canada Inc. for Architectural Services for the FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto Capital Project at BMO Field
topics: architecture;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Manager, the Chief Procurement Officer, and the Executive Director of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto Secretariat recommend City Council grant authority to negotiate and enter into a non-competitive contract of $4,168,561.70 (excluding taxes) with Gensler Architecture & Design Canada Inc. for architectural services for the FIFA World Cup 2026 capital project at BMO Field. A non-competitive contract is needed to meet FIFA's event timelines.

title: Request for Presentation from the Toronto Transit Commission on Changes to Wheel-Trans Service
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, specialized paratransit services; accessible public transportation; accessible transit; accessible transit service; door to door service; special mobility services; wheel trans; wheel-trans; wheeltrans, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Accessibility Advisory Committee recommends City Council ask the TTC Board to arrange a presentation to the committee's September 5, 2023 meeting on service planning changes being made to Wheel-Trans.

title: Graphic Image Delivery
topics: family planning, publications; birth control; contraception, brochures; catalogues; flyers; guides (publications); handbooks; information cards; newsletters; notices; posters; reports
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council direct the City Manager, in consultation with the City Solicitor, to report to the October 2023 Council meeting with a draft by-law regulating the unsolicited delivery of graphic images to residences. Residents are protesting being forced to view graphic anti-abortion flyers in their mailboxes without consent, which causes harm and distress, especially to young children and people who have had miscarriages or abortions.

title: Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Annual General Meeting and 2022 Audited Financial Statements
topics: seniors housing;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Board recommends City Council treat the portion of the Council meeting considering this report as the corporation's Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder, and receive the 2022 Annual Report, which summarizes performance during the organization's 2022 transition and progress on key initiatives for tenants, staff, and partners.

title: Toronto Port Lands Company Annual General Meeting and 2022 Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, financial reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Port Lands Company Board recommends City Council treat the portion of the Council meeting considering this report as the company's 2022 Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder, and receive the 2022 Annual Report and CreateTO's 2022 highlights report. The City is the sole shareholder; the last annual meeting was held July 19, 2022.

title: Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Annual General Meeting and 2022 Audited Financial Statements
topics: board members, budgets, community centres, financial reports, recreation centres, sports; annual financial reports; financial statements, board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, budgets and accounts, rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Board recommends City Council, as one of the facility's shareholders, adopt and authorize the City Manager to sign the resolutions of the shareholders, covering the appointment of the 2023 auditor, the 2022 financial statements, and the organization's operating results and outlook.

title: Toronto Building, Fleet Services and Paramedic Services - Employee Retention and Attraction, and Memoranda of Agreement with Local 79 and Local 416
topics: benefits, contracts, employees, employment & labour (sc), labour relations, paramedics, working conditions; collective agreements; employment contracts; workplace policies, collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, staff
brief: This is a procedural item: City staff recommend City Council ratify and approve the Memoranda of Agreement negotiated with CUPE Local 79 and TCEU Local 416 on employee retention and attraction in Toronto Building, Fleet Services, and Paramedic Services. The CUPE Local 79 agreement applies revised wage grades to sixteen bargaining unit classifications in the Toronto Building Division, retroactive to January 1, 2022.

title: Toronto Hydro Corporation Annual General Meeting and 2022 Audited Financial Statements
topics: hydro bills; electric bills; electricity bills; hydro accounts
brief: This is a procedural item: as sole shareholder of Toronto Hydro Corporation, City Council is asked to treat the portion of the meeting considering this report as the corporation's Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder and approve and adopt the attached shareholder resolution. Toronto Hydro Corporation wholly owns Toronto Hydro-Electric System Limited (electricity distribution) and Toronto Hydro Energy Services Inc. (street and expressway lighting), and pays the City dividends based on 60 percent of the prior year's net income.

title: Toronto Community Housing Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2022 Audited Consolidated Financial Statements
topics: social housing; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Community Housing Corporation recommends City Council treat the portion of the meeting considering this report as the corporation's Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder, receiving its 2022 Annual Report and audited consolidated financial statements — audited by KPMG LLP with an unqualified opinion — and appointing the 2023 auditor.

title: Lakeshore Arena Corporation 2022 Annual General Meeting and Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, financial reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural item: the Lakeshore Arena Corporation (operating as the Ford Performance Centre) Board recommends City Council treat the portion of the Council meeting considering this item as the corporation's 2022 Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder, and receive the Board-approved 2022 Annual Report and the 2022 audited statements.

title: Casa Loma Corporation 2022 Annual General Meeting and Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, financial reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural item: the Casa Loma Corporation Board recommends City Council treat the portion of the Council meeting considering this item as the corporation's 2022 Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder, and receive the 2022 Annual Report and the 2022 audited financial statements.

title: Build Toronto Inc. (Build Toronto) 2022 Annual General Meeting and Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, financial reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural item: the Build Toronto Board recommends City Council treat the portion of the Council meeting considering this report as the corporation's 2022 Annual General Meeting of the Shareholder, and receive Build Toronto's 2022 Annual Report and CreateTO's 2022 highlights report. Build Toronto was established by Council in 2008 and the City is its sole shareholder.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods - Beaches-East York Pilot Project: Status Update and Directions Report
topics: [housing by function], neighbourhoods; cultural neighbourhoods; ethnic neighbourhoods; neighborhoods
brief: The Deputy City Manager for Corporate Services and the Chief Planner recommend City Council direct that the City-owned property at 72 Amroth Avenue be allocated to the Beaches–East York Pilot Project for developing missing-middle housing solutions on City-owned, transit-oriented properties. The pilot, part of the Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods initiative, will develop a demonstration project in Ward 19 with the development industry and community consultation, informing how missing-middle projects can be built on other sites.

title: St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts Redevelopment
topics: redevelopment, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: The CreateTO Board recommends City Council adopt the St. Lawrence Centre for the Arts Design Competition jury's selection of Hariri Pontarini Architects, LMN Architects, Tawaw Architecture Collective, Smoke Architecture, and SLA as the winning submission for the reimagined St. Lawrence Centre. Council endorsed the building program for the new STLC in May 2022 following consultation with the performing arts and creative communities.

title: Toronto Water 2023 Capital Budget and 2024-2032 Capital Plan Adjustments
topics: capital budgets, water;
brief: This is a procedural item: the General Manager of Toronto Water recommends City Council authorize reallocating $18.185 million in cashflows and funding within Toronto Water's approved 2023 Capital Budget and 2024–2032 Capital Plan, to align forecasted project accelerations and deferrals. The adjustments have a zero-dollar impact on the budget and plan.

title: 2023 Heads and Beds Levy on Institutions
topics: institutional levies; heads and beds; institutional taxes
brief: This is a procedural item: the Controller recommends City Council authorize the 2023 Heads and Beds levy on colleges and universities, public hospitals, and correctional facilities, estimated at about $19.6 million at the maximum prescribed rate of $75 per full-time student, provincially rated bed, or resident place — a rate unchanged since 1987. Had the rate been indexed to inflation, it would be $170.64 and generate an additional $24.9 million.

title: Review of City of Toronto Guiding Principles for Executive Compensation Policies at City Agencies and Corporations
topics: nomination;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Manager recommends City Council approve updated Guiding Principles for the Development of Senior Executive Compensation Policies at City Agencies and Corporations, following an independent external review directed by Council in 2021. While the City is not the employer of agency and corporation executives, it supports transparent, rational, accountable, and fair executive compensation. Boards of listed agencies and corporations would be asked to adopt or amend their policies accordingly.

title: Changes to the Upper Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management
topics: appointments, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: This is a procedural item: the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends City Council appoint nominees to the Upper Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management, in accordance with the City's Public Appointments Policy and Municipal Code Chapter 19. The BIA spans two Community Council boundaries.

title: Alcohol in Parks Pilot Program
topics: parks, pilot projects; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends City Council approve a time-limited Alcohol in Parks pilot program from August 2 to October 9, 2023, allowing responsible personal consumption of alcohol in Toronto parks. The pilot design is based on public health guidance, public safety and operational considerations, and experiences from other Canadian jurisdictions, and will be evaluated for impacts on park visitors and surrounding communities.

title: Compliance Audit Application by Kevin Wiener for the Election Campaign Finances of Antonios Mantas
topics: [activities in government], [events in government], finance (sc);
brief: This is a procedural item: Kevin Wiener submitted a compliance audit application on June 29, 2023 for the election campaign finances of Antonios Mantas, candidate for City Councillor in Ward 22 Scarborough-Agincourt. The Election Compliance Audit Committee will consider the application.

brief: This is a procedural item: Kevin Wiener submitted a compliance audit application on June 29, 2023 for the election campaign finances of Lorenzo Berardinetti, candidate for City Councillor in Ward 20 Scarborough Southwest. The Election Compliance Audit Committee will consider the application.

topics: [activities in government], [events in government], finance (sc);
brief: This is a procedural item: Kevin Wiener submitted a compliance audit application on June 29, 2023 for the election campaign finances of Marco Valle, candidate for City Councillor in Ward 3 Etobicoke-Lakeshore. The Election Compliance Audit Committee will consider the application.

title: Compliance Audit Application by Kevin Wiener for the Election Campaign Finances of Sandeep Srivastava
topics: [activities in government], [events in government], finance (sc);
brief: This is a procedural item: Kevin Wiener submitted a compliance audit application on June 29, 2023 for the election campaign finances of Sandeep Srivastava, candidate for Mayor. The Election Compliance Audit Committee will consider the application.

title: Ombudsman Toronto Report: An Investigation into Toronto Community Housing Corporation's Tenant Human Rights Complaints Process
topics: complaints, human rights, ombudsman, report requests; ombudspersons
brief: This is a procedural item: the Ombudsman tables with City Council the investigation report, dated June 9, 2023, on Toronto Community Housing Corporation's Tenant Human Rights Complaints Process. The Ombudsman recommends City Council receive the report for information.

title: 1837-1845 Bayview Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning;
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council adopt the confidential recommendations regarding the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the zoning and site plan applications for a 25-storey mixed-use building at 1837–1845 Bayview Avenue, appealed in March 2022 after Council's failure to decide. The City Solicitor needs further directions ahead of a hearing scheduled October 17 to November 3, 2023. Council is asked to authorize public release of the confidential recommendations if adopted.

title: 83-95A Bloor Street West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Further Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council adopt the confidential recommendations regarding the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the zoning and site plan applications for a 79-storey mixed-use building with 1,118 residential units and 1,153 square metres of commercial space at 83–95A Bloor Street West. Council accepted a without-prejudice offer to settle in June 2023 and directed the City Solicitor to attend the Tribunal in support of the settlement. Council is asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 640 Lansdowne Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals, zoning bylaws; omb; ontario municipal board, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council adopt the confidential recommendations regarding the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the zoning application for 640 Lansdowne Avenue — a seven-storey mixed-use building by Magellan Community Charities with 256 long-term care beds, 57 affordable rental units, and ground-floor non-residential space, on lands under a long-term lease with the TTC and the City. Council approved the application in July 2022. Council is asked to authorize public release of the confidential recommendations if adopted.

title: 537-547 Eglinton Avenue East and 59 and 61 Hoyle Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Appeals - Request for Directions
topics: Official Plans, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council adopt the confidential recommendations regarding the Ontario Land Tribunal appeals of the refused zoning and Official Plan amendment applications for a 21-storey residential building at 537–547 Eglinton Avenue East and 59 and 61 Hoyle Avenue, and authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted. Council refused the applications in September and December 2021 and directed staff to oppose any appeal.

title: Legal Challenge to Bill 184 - Protecting Tenants and Strengthening Community Housing Act, 2020
topics: housing, social housing, tenants; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units, homes; residences, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: The City Solicitor recommends City Council adopt the confidential instructions to staff regarding the City's legal challenge to Bill 184, the Protecting Tenants and Strengthening Community Housing Act, 2020. The City issued a Notice of Application in Superior Court in March 2021 challenging amendments to the Residential Tenancies Act, and the parties have exchanged their application materials. The confidential information is subject to solicitor-client privilege.

title: Appointment of a Public Member as Chair of the Administrative Penalty Tribunal
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel – Administrative Penalty Tribunal considered the appointment of a Chair at its July 7, 2023 meeting and recommends City Council appoint a current member of the Administrative Penalty Tribunal as Chair, for a term tied to the member's existing term.

title: 200 University Avenue - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council enact a by-law designating the property at 200 University Avenue under the Ontario Heritage Act, with a revised Statement of Significance clarifying the earlier Council decision. The property owner, GWL Realty Advisors, objected to the March 2022 notice of intention to designate; the property sits on the southwest corner of Richmond Street West and University Avenue.

title: 789-793 Don Mills Road - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council affirm its May 2023 decision stating its intention to designate the property at 789–793 Don Mills Road under the Ontario Heritage Act, following an objection filed by the owner, 789 Don Mills Developments Inc. Known as Foresters House, the property sits on the east side of Don Mills Road just south of Eglinton Avenue East and contains a 22-storey office tower.

title: 15 Elm Street - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council affirm its May 10, 2023 decision stating its intention to designate the property at 15 Elm Street under the Ontario Heritage Act, following an objection to the notice of intention to designate filed on behalf of the property owner. The two-storey house-form building, completed before 1868 in the Georgian Revival style, is a rare surviving Confederation-era house on the south side of Elm Street between Yonge and Bay Streets. Council is asked to authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the designation by-law.

title: 409 Huron Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council state its intention to designate the property at 409 Huron Street under the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The Queen Anne Revival-style detached house, constructed in 1903 and designed by architect Frederick Henry Herbert, forms part of a Victorian streetscape in the Huron-Sussex neighbourhood.

title: 350 Bloor Street East - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council state its intention to designate the property at 350 Bloor Street East under the Ontario Heritage Act for its design, associative, and contextual cultural heritage value. The Modernist six-storey office building, at the northeast corner of Bloor Street East and the Mount Pleasant Road access ramp, is built into the upper portion of the Rosedale Ravine's south embankment.

title: Annual Report of the Toronto Lobbyist Registrar for the Year 2022
topics: annual reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: This is an information item: the Lobbyist Registrar recommends City Council receive the Annual Report of the Toronto Lobbyist Registrar for the year 2022 for information. No decision is attached.

title: 137 Bond Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council state its intention to designate the property at 137 Bond Street under the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. Constructed in 1855 on the TMU campus, the property — known as O'Keefe House — anchors the southeast corner of Bond and Gould Streets and represents an early period of development of the McGill estate, first the residence of lawyer William Mathers and Agnes Mathers.

title: 33 and 37 Maitland Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 33 and 37 Maitland Street under the Ontario Heritage Act for their cultural heritage value. The adjacent mid-block properties in the Church–Wellesley Village include the three-storey Biltmore Apartments at 33 Maitland Street, a brick Arts and Crafts-influenced building added to the Heritage Register on February 7, 2023.

title: 29 Basin Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council state its intention to designate the Sun Oil Company Building at 29 Basin Street under the Ontario Heritage Act for its design, historical, and contextual cultural heritage value. Completed in 1931 as a two-storey factory and warehouse designed by T.H. Mothersill, the property sits on the Port Lands' Ship Channel side of Basin Street.

title: Alterations to a Heritage Property and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement - 60 Mill Street
topics: agreements, easements, heritage designation; tenancy agreements
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council approve alterations and authorize an amendment of the Heritage Easement Agreement for the designated heritage property at 60 Mill Street, known as Rack House D. The alterations relate to a development application for a 31-storey hotel building that retains the existing Rack House D elevations as a podium, following an Ontario Land Tribunal decision.

title: Alterations to a Heritage Property and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement - 551 Mount Pleasant Road (Regent Theatre)
topics: agreements, easements, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation, tenancy agreements
brief: The Chief Planner recommends City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 551 Mount Pleasant Road — the three-storey Regent Theatre built in 1927 — under the Ontario Heritage Act in connection with a site plan application, substantially in accordance with plans dated January 30, 2023, and grant authority to enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement covering the theatre and its entrances at 549, 553, and 555 Mount Pleasant Road.

title: Demolition of a Heritage Attribute and a Structure to a Designated Property at 35 Kingsway Crescent
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation

brief: This is an information item: staff report to the Toronto Investment Board on the performance of the Sinking Fund and Long Term Fund for the first quarter of 2023, along with investment policy and plan compliance certificates and reports. The Board is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Presentations from Investment Managers
topics: investment, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards
brief: This is an information item: investment managers Connor, Clark, & Lunn and Leith Wheeler will present to the Toronto Investment Board on active fixed income. No decision is attached.

title: 55 Allanhurst Drive - Request for a Fence Exemption to the Toronto Municipal Code, Chapter 447
topics: exemptions, fences; division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council refuse the owner's request for a fence exemption at 55 Allanhurst Drive. The proposed front and side yard fence, plus an existing fence, would not meet the standards of the Fences by-law (Chapter 447). The community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: 148 The Kingsway - Request for a Fence Exemption to the Toronto Municipal Code, Chapter 447
topics: exemptions, fences; division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council refuse the owner's request for a fence exemption at 148 The Kingsway. The wood-panel fence sits within 2.4 metres of a driveway and obstructs the view of the boulevard and highway, in contravention of the Fences by-law (Chapter 447). The community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: 92 North Drive - Application to Remove Three City Trees
topics: city-owned trees, tree removal; city owned trees; public owned trees; publicly owned trees; trees on public property
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council deny a permit to remove three city-owned trees at 92 North Drive: two white spruce trees measuring 31 and 35 centimetres and a Norway spruce measuring 46 centimetres. The trees are healthy and maintainable, and the tree by-laws do not support removal for a proposed driveway with a second entrance.

title: 5 Verona Avenue - Application to Remove Two City Trees
topics: city-owned trees, tree removal; city owned trees; public owned trees; publicly owned trees; trees on public property
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council deny a permit to remove two city-owned Manitoba maple trees at 5 Verona Avenue, measuring 60 and 93 centimetres in diameter. The trees are maintainable and the tree by-laws do not support removal, even though they conflict with a planned new home and driveway.

title: 19 Disan Court - Application to Remove a Private Tree
topics: privately-owned trees, tree removal; private owned trees; private trees; privately owned trees; trees on private property
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council deny a permit to remove one privately owned tree at 19 Disan Court. The 44-centimetre Colorado blue spruce is healthy and maintainable, and the tree by-laws do not support its removal despite the owner's concerns about branches near the house and storm damage.

title: Introduction of By-laws
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Etobicoke York Community Council will introduce bills. No decision is attached.

title: Benrubin Drive - Investigation of Traffic Calming Measures
topics: road safety, traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Perruzza recommends that the Etobicoke York Community Council ask Transportation Services to review pedestrian and traffic safety on Benrubin Drive from Firenza Drive to Duncanwoods Drive and report back with findings and any proposed safety measures. Residents submitted a petition after observing speeding on the street.

title: Strathburn Boulevard and Melody Road - All-Way Stop Control
topics: stop signs, traffic control systems; all-way stop controls; technical warrants, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Councillor Perruzza recommends that the Etobicoke York Community Council authorize an all-way stop at Strathburn Boulevard and Melody Road. The intersection sits next to St. Simon Catholic School, where parents dropping off and picking up children create heavy morning and afternoon congestion and children cross with very limited visibility. Traffic counts came in below the formal warrants, but the councillor cites the proximity to the school and the dangerous conditions.

title: Lemonade for Love
topics: charities, fundraising; charitable organizations; charity, pledge forms
brief: This is an information item: Councillor Amber Morley recommends that the Etobicoke York Community Council receive a presentation from Lemonade for Love for information. The child-driven, parent-supported fundraiser began in 2014 as a lemonade stand in Etobicoke and now runs each June at Fairfield Park, having raised and reinvested over $150,000 for children with special needs through the Captain Xavier Fund at Silver Creek Preschool.

title: Grandville Avenue - Parking Amendments
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council change parking on Grandville Avenue between Lambton Avenue and the street's south limit to the east side only, ending the alternate-side arrangement. The change responds to a resident petition submitted through the ward councillor's office. The community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Kane Avenue at Dunraven Drive and Aileen Avenue - Temporary Stop Signs
topics: stop signs, temporary signs, traffic management; all-way stop controls; technical warrants, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
