brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend temporary traffic changes around Kane Avenue, Dunraven Drive and Aileen Avenue while the Fairbank Silverthorn Basement Flooding Protection Project closes Silverthorn Avenue and Scott Road at Dunraven Drive until July 2024. Kane Avenue, normally one-way, would temporarily become two-way between Dunraven Drive and Kersdale Avenue, with two additional temporary stop signs on the northbound approach to keep traffic flowing. The community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Orpington Crescent and Masseygrove Crescent (east intersection) and Orpington Crescent and Orpington Crescent (east intersection) - Compulsory Stop Control
topics: traffic control systems, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council approve stop controls for northbound and southbound traffic on Orpington Crescent at the east intersection with Masseygrove Crescent, remove the existing westbound stop control there, and add a stop for northbound traffic at the east intersection of Orpington Crescent with itself. The changes would clarify right-of-way and improve safety. The community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.
address: Toronto Ontario Orpington Masseygrove; Toronto Ontario Orpington Orpington

title: Government Road and Mill Cove/Thorndale Crescent - Stop Control
topics: road safety, stop signs; all-way stop controls; technical warrants
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council approve a compulsory stop control for eastbound traffic on Government Road at Mill Cove/Thorndale Crescent. Transportation Services assessed the intersection and found the stop would improve safety for all road users. The community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Edgemore Drive and Humbervale Boulevard - All-Way Stop Control
topics: traffic control systems, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council approve all-way stop control at the intersection of Edgemore Drive and Humbervale Boulevard. Transportation Services assessed the intersection and found the all-way stop would improve safety for all road users. The community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Easthampton Drive and Greyswood Court - Stop Control
topics: traffic control systems, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council approve a compulsory stop control for westbound traffic on Greyswood Court at Easthampton Drive. Transportation Services assessed the intersection and found the stop would improve safety for all road users. The community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: 555 Rexdale Boulevard (Delegated) - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic control systems, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council authorize traffic control signals at Rexdale Boulevard and Glorious Song Way plus five future public road intersections within the Woodbine Lands at 555 Rexdale Boulevard, and a stop control for northbound traffic on Sunny's Halo Trail at Rexdale Boulevard. Staff also seek turn prohibitions at the private driveway at 500 Rexdale Boulevard to improve safety for all road users. The community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Woodstream Drive - Parking Amendments and Heavy Truck Prohibition
topics: heavy truck prohibitions, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that the Etobicoke York Community Council prohibit parking at all times on both sides of Woodstream Drive between Rexdale Boulevard and Humberwood Boulevard, and impose a heavy truck prohibition on that stretch at all times. The changes would improve vehicle movement, visibility and safety for road and park users. The community council has delegated authority to decide this matter finally.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the George Bell Arena Board
topics: appointments, public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Clerk recommends that the Etobicoke York Community Council appoint Omolola Abiola and Dale Fallon to the George Bell Arena Board. The appointments would be at pleasure of Council, for terms ending June 19, 2027.

title: Melissa Chang - Appeal DDRT2022-04
topics: animal services, by-laws, dogs; animal control; animal protection; animal shelters; animal welfare; humane society; injured animals; lost pets; missing animals; missing pets; sick animals; stray animals; stray pets, bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the dangerous dog appeal tribunal will hear Melissa Chang's appeal of a dangerous dog order issued January 13, 2022 (file DDRT2022-04). The tribunal can uphold, change, or cancel the order, which sets the city's requirements for the dog's owner.

title: Veronika Taratine - Appeal DDRT2023-19
topics: animal bites, animal services, by-laws, dogs; animal control; animal protection; animal shelters; animal welfare; humane society; injured animals; lost pets; missing animals; missing pets; sick animals; stray animals; stray pets, bylaws, dog bites
brief: This is a procedural item: the dangerous dog appeal tribunal will hear Veronika Taratine's appeal of a dangerous dog order issued January 17, 2023 (file DDRT2023-19). The tribunal can uphold, change, or cancel the order, which sets the city's requirements for the dog's owner.

title: 880-882 and 888 Eastern Avenue and 74-80 Knox Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a zoning change to permit a 12-storey mixed-use building with 180 homes at 880-882 and 888 Eastern Avenue and 74-80 Knox Avenue. Staff describe the proposal as an appropriate built form that fits the existing and planned context of the surrounding area.

title: 500 Macpherson Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an official plan and zoning change to permit an eight-storey residential building with 152 homes at 500 Macpherson Avenue, at the northeast corner of Macpherson Avenue and Kendal Avenue. The proposal includes 103 vehicle and 153 bicycle parking spaces.

title: 24-26 Imperial Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a zoning change to permit a nine-storey residential building with 30 homes at 24-26 Imperial Street. The building would total 4,000 square metres of floor area with eight parking spaces in a single-level underground garage.

title: 555 Davenport Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an official plan and zoning change to permit an eight-storey residential building with 143 homes at 555 Davenport Road, at the southeast corner of Davenport Road and Kendal Avenue. The proposal includes 98 vehicle and 143 bicycle parking spaces.

title: 124 Bedford Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report  - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: This is a planning approval item: staff recommend that City Council approve a zoning change for 124 Bedford Road. The change would permit an office use to occupy the entire house-form building.

title: Report Back on Metrolinx's Ontario Line Construction within the Toronto and East York District
topics: contracts, regional transportation agencies; commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies
brief: This is an information item: staff report back with details requested by the Subcommittee on Metrolinx's Ontario Line construction in the Toronto and East York district, including awarded contract costs, the consortium companies, federal funding, and provincial plans for community benefits. The Ontario Line will run about 15.6 kilometres with 15 stations, connecting to the Eglinton Crosstown LRT, Lines 1 and 2, and the GO network. The Community Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: 374-390 Dupont Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a planning approval item: staff recommend that City Council approve an official plan and zoning change for 374-390 Dupont Street. The change would permit a 12-storey mixed-use building with 256 homes and 1,000 square metres of non-residential floor area.

title: 100 College Street - Revising Heritage Designation Status
topics: heritage designation, post-secondary education; college education; graduate studies; higher education; post-graduate studies; postgraduate studies; postsecondary education; university applications; university education
brief: Councillor Saxe recommends that City Council decline to designate or list 100 College Street (the University of Toronto's Banting Institute) under the Ontario Heritage Act. Council first signalled its intention to designate the property in August 2020, but consideration was deferred pending a rezoning application or the University of Toronto Secondary Plan. When a zoning application arrives, Council is asked to have the Chief Planner secure the commitments in President Gertler's May 3, 2023 letter instead.

title: 40 kilometres per hour Speed Limit on Major Arterial Roads
topics: major arterial roads, speed limits;
brief: Six councillors (Perks, Bravo, Saxe, Matlow, Moise and Fletcher) recommend that City Council lower the speed limit to 40 km/h on all major arterial roads in Wards 4, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14 that are currently above 40 km/h, except Lake Shore Boulevard. Many arterials in these wards are already 40 km/h near schools or under the 2016 Road Safety Plan; the motion aims to improve safety and make limits consistent.

title: 31-37 Gladstone Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a zoning change to permit a six-storey residential building with 28 homes at 31-37 Gladstone Avenue. Staff describe it as a contextually appropriate mid-rise that transitions to the lower-scale neighbourhoods to the north and east. The report also recommends a Holding symbol on the site, liftable once servicing matters are resolved.

title: Traffic Control Signals - Dufferin Street and Croatia Street
topics: traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize traffic control signals at the intersection of Dufferin Street and Croatia Street. The signals are required as a condition of approval for the development at 1141 Bloor Street West, 980 Dufferin Street and 90 Croatia Street, and Transportation Services confirms the technical justification is met. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Dufferin Street.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 8B to Exclude the Development Located at 485 Logan Avenue
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a revised map of Permit Parking Area 8B that excludes the development at 485 Logan Avenue, at the direction of the Toronto and East York Community Council. If approved, residents and visitors of that address would no longer be able to take part in the area's permit parking program. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Logan Avenue.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 5E to Exclude the Development Located at 208 Bloor Street West
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a revised map of Permit Parking Area 5E that excludes the development at 208 Bloor Street West, at the direction of the Toronto and East York Community Council. If approved, residents and visitors of that address would no longer be able to take part in the area's permit parking program. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Bloor Street West.

title: Port Lands Flood Protection and Enabling Infrastructure - Construction Staging Time Extension
topics: construction permits (right-of-way), construction waste; broken concrete, curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way)
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize the temporary full closure of Commissioners Street, from Cherry Street to 120 metres east of Don Roadway, from June 1 to October 31, 2023, for the Port Lands Flood Protection and Enabling Infrastructure project. The project, led by Waterfront Toronto, the City, the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority and the Toronto Port Lands Company, creates two new outlets for the Don River to protect the Lower Don Lands from flooding. TTC service on Commissioners Street has been rerouted along Villiers Street and Saulter Street South, so Council approval is required.

title: 6-16 Wellesley Street West and 5-7 St. Nicholas Street - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: construction permits (right-of-way), construction waste; broken concrete, curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way)
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize continued closure of the north sidewalk and a 2.3-metre-wide portion of the westbound curb lane and cycle track on Wellesley Street West, between Bistro Lane and St. Nicholas Street, for construction staging of a 55-storey residential development at 6-16 Wellesley Street West and 5-7 St. Nicholas Street. A temporary pedestrian walkway would be provided within the closed portion. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Wellesley Street West.

title: 1660 Bloor Street West - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction permits (right-of-way), construction waste; broken concrete, curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way)
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize temporary closures around 1660 Bloor Street West, at the northwest corner of Bloor Street West and Indian Road, for construction staging of a 13-storey residential building by Mattamy (Bloor) Limited. The north sidewalk and part of the westbound curb lane on Bloor Street West, and the west sidewalk and part of the southbound curb lane on Indian Road, would close from June 15, 2023 to November 30, 2025, with pedestrian movement maintained. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Bloor Street West.

title: 1-15 Delisle Avenue and 1496-1510 Yonge Street - Public Art Plan
topics: public art, residential properties, rezoning, site plan control; outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate, site plan approvals
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the public art plan for 1-15 Delisle Avenue and 1496-1510 Yonge Street. The plan sets out how the owner will commission public art in the privately owned, publicly accessible area of the site, covering the art vision, objectives, locations, artist research and shortlist, and the selection process under the Section 37 agreement.

title: 35, 41, 95 High Park Avenue, 66, 102-116 Pacific Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Removal of Holding Symbol ("H") - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council remove the Holding symbol from zoning for 35, 41 and 95 High Park Avenue and 66 and 102-116 Pacific Avenue. The underlying by-law permits demolition of 20 townhouses and construction of three buildings of 35, 11 and 30 storeys with 366, 103 and 294 homes, while four existing buildings with 968 homes in total remain on site. The hold required certain conditions to be fulfilled before development.

title: 353-355 Adelaide Street West, 46 Charlotte Street and 16 Oxley Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: zoning;
brief: A 50-storey mixed-use building with 293 homes and retail and office space was proposed at 353-355 Adelaide Street West and 46 Charlotte Street, with a 12-storey extension at 16 Oxley Street, incorporating a six-storey heritage building; a new owner bought the site in July 2022. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the current zoning amendment appeal while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 33 and 39 Davies Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse a zoning amendment to permit an office tower at 33 and 39 Davies Avenue, revised in January 2023 to 15 storeys within an Employment Area east of the Don Valley, north of Queen Street East. Staff find the built form inappropriate for the low- and mid-rise employment area next to Neighbourhoods and Joel Weeks Park and not in conformity with the Official Plan. Council is also asked to authorize the City Solicitor to defend the refusal before the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 15-19 Bloor Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: commercial properties, mixed use areas, multi-unit dwellings, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, office real estate; retail space, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council refuse an official plan and zoning amendment to permit a 94-storey mixed-use tower with 1,262 homes and retail space at 15-19 Bloor Street West. Staff find the tall building cannot be appropriately accommodated on the site and that the proposal does not conform with the Official Plan, the Downtown Secondary Plan, or the Tall Building Design Guidelines. Council is also asked to authorize the City Solicitor to defend the refusal before the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: Guildwood Parkway and Rowatson Road - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: community councils, pedestrian crossovers, pedestrian walkways, traffic control systems; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize traffic control signals at the intersection of Guildwood Parkway and Rowatson Road (including the private access there). Transportation Services assessed the crossing between Prince Philip Boulevard and Rowatson Road and found the signals would improve safety for pedestrians and other vulnerable road users. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Guildwood Parkway.

title: 3585 and 3595 St. Clair Avenue East, 636 to 646 and 641 to 663 Danforth Road, and 411 and 415 Kennedy Road - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment, Draft Plan of Subdivision - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments, part lot control, planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A series of development applications for lands at 3585 and 3595 St. Clair Avenue East, 636 to 663 Danforth Road, and 411 and 415 Kennedy Road, including an official plan amendment, rezoning and a draft plan of subdivision, were appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the current appeal while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 100 Eglinton Square - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning Amendment  Application - Appeal Report
topics: Secondary Plans, community councils, official plan amendments, planning tribunals, zoning bylaws; omb; ontario municipal board, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 35-storey mixed-use building with 296 homes, plus retail and office space, was proposed at 100 Eglinton Square in April 2022, and the applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in September 2022 after Council missed the legislated decision deadline. City Planning staff do not support the application in its current form. Staff recommend that Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition while continuing to discuss a resolution with the applicant.

title: 3250 Markham Rd and 568 Passmore Avenue - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning approvals, zoning; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve zoning changes to allow three single-storey multi-tenant industrial buildings at 3250 Markham Road and 568 Passmore Avenue. The three buildings would hold 18 commercial-industrial units totalling about 34,473 square metres, with 319 parking spaces and 68 loading spaces.

title: 1680 Brimley Road - Official Plan Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, community councils, official plan amendments; application process
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve an Official Plan amendment for 1680 Brimley Road exempting the lands from Policy 6.3 of the Scarborough Centre Secondary Plan. The change would bring the parkland dedication rate for the site into line with the Official Plan policies in force when the first above-grade building permit is issued.

title: 3070 Ellesmere Road - Application to Lift Holding Provision - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, community councils, planning; application process
brief: Staff recommend that City Council lift the Holding provision on the lands at 3070 Ellesmere Road. The hold, added through site-specific Zoning By-law 1421-2007, blocked development until the Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks issued a Certificate of Approval for the site's methane venting system. The Chief Planner, in consultation with Solid Waste Services, is now satisfied the requirement has been met.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will review the Order Paper, which sets out the business before the meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements will be made at the City Council meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions. No decision is attached.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council will declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act before the meeting proceeds. No decision is attached.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: committee reports and new business from city officials are introduced, including reports from the Executive Committee, Board of Health, Civic Appointments Committee, Economic and Community Development Committee, General Government Committee, and Infrastructure and Environment Committee. No decision is attached.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from the regular meeting held on May 10, 11 and 12, 2023. Confirming the minutes formally adopts the record of that meeting.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting opens with the call to order, O Canada, and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: City Comments on the Proposed Provincial Planning Statement
topics: [organizations in planning and development], provincial governments;
brief: The Chief Planner recommends that City Council express its concern to the Minister of Municipal Affairs about the general direction of the draft Provincial Planning Statement, introduced April 6, 2023 as part of Bill 97. The draft statement would replace the Provincial Policy Statement and the Growth Plan for the Greater Golden Horseshoe, representing fundamental changes in how growth planning is carried out in the province and by the City of Toronto.

title: Our Plan Toronto: Recommendations on Forty-Five Employment Area Conversion Requests - Final Report
topics: employment areas, zoning bylaws; employment districts; employment zones, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Chief Planner recommends that City Council adopt Official Plan Amendment 644, which decides on forty-five requests to convert employment lands to other uses. Employment areas hold over 21,600 establishments and 390,000 jobs (27% of city jobs), produce about 27% of the city's estimated $195.7 billion 2021 GDP, and contribute about 12% of property taxes. Council is also asked to authorize seeking the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing's approval of the amendment.

title: 1871 and 1879-1885 Weston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate 1871 and 1879-1885 Weston Road under the Ontario Heritage Act. The 1947 Modern Gothic church at 1871 Weston Road, designed by architect Francis Bruce Brown for the Weston Park Baptist Church, has served the Weston community for over 115 years at the southeast corner of Weston Road and Lawrence Avenue West.

title: 1123 Leslie Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate 1123 Leslie Street under the Ontario Heritage Act. The 1962 building was the Canadian headquarters of the William Wrigley Jr. Company, housing its offices and gum manufacturing plant until the factory closed in March 2016. It sits on the east side of Leslie Street opposite Wilket Creek Park.

title: 1117 Queen Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate 1117 Queen Street West under the Ontario Heritage Act. Council first stated this intention on August 15, 2022, but the designation by-law was not passed within the 120-day window (extended to April 18, 2023), so the notice was deemed withdrawn. This report restarts the designation process.

title: Creation of a Woodbine Special Sign District
topics: regulations, signs; signage
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve creating a Woodbine Special Sign District under the Sign By-law (Chapter 694), allowing and regulating first-party electronic signs in the area. The by-law lets members of the public apply to change sign district designations for a specific property or area; the city currently has seven special sign districts alongside nine standard ones.

title: 586 Eglinton Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment and Site Plan Control Applications - Appeal Report
topics: community councils, site plan control, zoning bylaws; site plan approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 32-storey building with 249 homes, ground-floor retail and office space was proposed at 586 Eglinton Avenue East in September 2021, and the applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in November 2022 after Council missed the decision deadlines. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the zoning amendment.

title: 774, 776, 778, 780 and 782 Marlee Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-Law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, community councils, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 12-storey residential building with 301 homes was proposed at 774 to 782 Marlee Avenue in December 2021, and the applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in October 2022 after Council missed the 120-day decision deadline. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal hearing to oppose the application in its current form while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 128, 130 and 132 Gorman Park Road and 795, 797, 799 Sheppard Avenue West Application to Lift the Holding Provisions (H) - Decision Report - Approval
topics: land use designations, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council lift the Holding provision on zoning for 128, 130 and 132 Gorman Park Road and 795, 797 and 799 Sheppard Avenue West. The underlying by-law permits a nine-storey mixed-use building with 170 homes, and the hold, which required an acceptable sanitary system solution to be built and operational, can now be removed.

title: 5830 Bathurst Street - Application under Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act, 2002 - Decision Report - Approval
topics: burial permits, funerals, legislation; acts, memorial services
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a three-storey addition to the existing three-storey mausoleum at Westminster Cemetery, 5830 Bathurst Street, as in the public interest under the Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act. The addition, with six parking spaces, is part of a seven-phase master plan that would add six new mausoleums, an administration and funeral visitation centre, and new roads, parking, and pedestrian and cycling connections.

title: 817 Mount Pleasant Road - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: churches, community councils, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff recommend that City Council add 817 Mount Pleasant Road to the City's Heritage Register. The property, St. Peter's Estonian Lutheran Church, is a Mid-Century Modernist church designed by Estonian-Canadian architect Michael Bach and completed in 1955, and it meets the provincial criteria for cultural heritage value.

title: Avenue Road - Parking Amendments
topics: community councils, parking, transportation; transportation services
brief: Staff recommend that City Council change parking rules on the west side of Avenue Road, north of Brooke Avenue: reducing pay-and-display hours and adding three short-term parking spaces limited to 10 minutes during weekday morning and afternoon periods. The spaces would support pick-up and drop-off at the daycare at 1920 Avenue Road, though they remain open to anyone for short stays. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Avenue Road.

title: 5051-5061 Yonge Street - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: A mixed-use tower at 5051 to 5061 Yonge Street, revised in October 2022 to 39 storeys with 365 homes above two floors of non-residential uses, was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in January 2023 after Council missed the 120-day deadline. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal to oppose the application in its current form while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 2500 Don Mills Road - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: community councils, zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Thirty- and 39-storey mixed-use buildings with 823 homes and ground-floor commercial space were proposed at 2500 Don Mills Road in April 2022, and the applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in February 2023 after Council missed the 120-day deadline. Staff recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Tribunal hearing to oppose the applications in their current form while continuing talks with the applicant.

title: Exploring a Community Assets Dashboard - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: databases, information and communication technology; ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to have the City Manager, in consultation with other divisions, review the feasibility of a community assets dashboard. The dashboard would draw on data the city already holds to create community-based, data-driven insights, supporting open government principles of transparency, participation, accountability and accessibility.

title: Request to Implement an Adequate Temperature By-law - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: by-laws, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems; air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems, bylaws
brief: Councillors Shelley Carroll and Amber Morley ask City Council to direct the Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards to report to the Planning and Housing Committee by the fourth quarter of 2023 on an adequate temperature by-law for landlords. The city already requires landlords to heat units to at least 21 degrees Celsius from September 15 to June 1 and to keep air-conditioned units at no more than 26 degrees from June 2 to September 14; with climate change driving more extreme heat, many tenants face very high indoor temperatures. The report would examine requiring landlords to provide adequate cooling.

title: Developing a Framework for the Installation of  Outdoor Working Stations - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: local government structure; city council structure; committee structure; council committee structure; council structure; council-committee structure; governance structure
brief: Councillors James Pasternak and Shelley Carroll ask City Council to have the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture and the General Manager of Transportation Services report back on a framework to pilot free-to-use outdoor working stations equipped with WiFi and solar lighting. The idea is inspired by Montreal's 2020 Cabine de Castelnau pilot, which drew nearly 30,000 users in 2021 and grew to 40 spaces in 2022.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2023.CC5.23, regarding 1648-1670 Avenue Road and 405-407 Brookdale Avenue - Conveyance of Ravine Buffer - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Jaye Robinson
topics: ravine protection, ravines; ravine bylaws; ravine protection bylaws, ravine protection areas
brief: Councillors Mike Colle and Jaye Robinson ask City Council to reopen and amend its earlier decision on 1648 to 1670 Avenue Road and 405 to 407 Brookdale Avenue over the timing of a ravine buffer conveyance. As approved, the owner must convey a 10-metre naturalized ravine buffer, per Toronto and Region Conservation Authority policy, before the Ontario Land Tribunal issues its final order implementing the settlement. That timing is not viable or practical because an existing building with tenanted units will still be on the lands when the order issues.

title: Governance Review of Yonge-Dundas Square - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: governance, squares; civic squares; public squares, governance structure; municipal governance
brief: Councillors Chris Moise and Shelley Carroll ask City Council to direct the City Manager to review the governance and operations model for Yonge-Dundas Square and report back. The review would consider options including publicly operating the square in the same manner as Nathan Phillips Square. The square, established in 2001, draws millions of visitors a year as a downtown gathering place.

title: Patio Approval for 17 St Nicholas Street (Bar Volo) - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: boulevard cafes; boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants)
brief: Councillors Chris Moise and Brad Bradford ask City Council to direct the General Manager of Transportation Services, with staff from Economic Development and Culture, Municipal Licensing and Standards, and Toronto Fire, to report to the June 22, 2023 Toronto and East York Community Council meeting on a solution letting Bar Volo at 17 St Nicholas Street install a CaféTO patio. The business, denied this year despite taking part in previous years, faces a time-sensitive decision.

title: Improvements to the Modular Housing at 175 Cummer Avenue - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: Councillors Lily Cheng and Jamaal Myers ask City Council to require that the request for proposals to select a non-profit operator for the modular housing at 175 Cummer Avenue address the main concerns of nearby seniors. The motion notes the green space in front of Willowdale Manor is cherished by its senior residents, yet the site plan places the 59-unit building in the middle of it, and the project still awaits an Ontario Land Tribunal hearing.

title: Securing Emergency Shelter for Refugees - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: emergency housing, refugees; emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless)
brief: Councillors Josh Matlow and Jamaal Myers ask City Council to direct the General Manager of Shelter, Support and Housing Administration to work with the Ethiopian Association of Greater Toronto and other refugee settlement and advocacy organizations to provide shelter to refugee claimants. The motion responds to the city's decision to stop admitting refugee claimants to the core shelter system and a lack of federal funding, leaving large groups of refugees unhoused and at risk of relocation to Montreal.

title: CaféTO Exemption - 1068 Yonge, Rebel House - Waiving requirement regulating interference with delivery vehicle parking zones - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: street occupation permits; curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: Councillors Dianne Saxe and James Pasternak ask City Council to exempt the curb lane café at 1068 Yonge Street (The Rebel House) from the sidewalk café by-law's delivery vehicle parking zone rule. The café would overlap a delivery loading zone, but staff found the impact would not be excessive since the adjacent Paul Hahn lane serves as the primary delivery route for area businesses.

title: 65 Front St West - Temporary Outdoor Patio During "Union Summer" Event - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: street occupation permits; curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: Councillors Ausma Malik and Alejandra Bravo ask City Council to exempt the outdoor patio at 65 Front Street West (Union Chicken) from the 10-metre extended liquor licence adjacency rule for the Union Summer event outside Union Station. The patio has long been part of the event, but a change in the application process left its location outside the 10-metre limit.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 1-25 Defries Street to the Transportation Services Division for the design and construction of a new sidewalk - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: funding; financing
brief: Councillors Chris Moise and Shelley Carroll recommend that City Council increase the Transportation Services 2023-2032 capital budget by $350,000 on a one-time basis, fully funded by Section 37 community benefits from the 1-25 Defries Street development. The money would design and build public realm improvements including a new sidewalk on the west side of Bayview Avenue between Old Brewery Lane and Labatt Avenue, with a raised crossing and marked crosswalks; the design requires acquiring 99.17 square metres of private property at 576 Bayview Avenue.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 316 Bloor Street West - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: development, funding; developing land; development (land); land development, financing
brief: Councillors Dianne Saxe and Chris Moise recommend that City Council increase the Transportation Services 2023-2032 capital budget by $1,750,000, fully funded by Section 37 community benefits from the 316 Bloor Street West development, for on-street bikeway construction on Bloor Street West. The Bloor cycle tracks, made permanent in 2017 after a pilot, are a backbone of the city's cycling infrastructure and climate commitments.

title: Authority to Install Curb Lane CaféTO Patios for Small Businesses on Queen Street East - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: boulevard cafes, small businesses; boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants)
brief: Councillors Brad Bradford and Gary Crawford ask City Council to exempt the curb lane café patios at 1966 Queen Street East (Bud's Coffee Bar and Chowpatty Culture) from parts of the sidewalk café by-law so they can be installed. The two small businesses were denied because of utility locates (manhole covers) where the patios would sit, even though both successfully took part in CaféTO in prior years.

title: Appointment of Interim Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: appointments, municipal officials; city officials
brief: This is a procedural item: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie and Councillor Gary Crawford recommend that City Council appoint Stephen Conforti as Interim Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer, including as interim statutory treasurer. The appointment is urgent because the position becomes vacant on July 5, 2023.

title: 892 Queen Street West - CaféTO Curb Lane Café - Waiving Intersection Setback Requirement in Municipal Code Chapter 742 - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: boulevard cafes; boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants)
brief: Councillors Ausma Malik and Alejandra Bravo ask City Council to exempt the curb lane café at 892 Queen Street West (Le Swan) from the 15-metre intersection setback in the sidewalk café by-law. The café would sit 12.9 metres from the Crawford Street intersection, and Transportation staff have confirmed the reduced setback would not compromise safety.

title: Patio Approval for 161 Danforth Ave (Sidebar) - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: street occupation permits; curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher and Ausma Malik ask City Council to exempt the curb lane café at 161 Danforth Avenue (Sidebar) from the extended liquor licence adjacency rule. The patio sits about 12 metres from the restaurant, just beyond the 10-metre limit for serving liquor in the extended café area; Sidebar has taken part in CaféTO since 2020.

title: Authorization to Release of Section 37 funds for the Colonel Danforth Park Off Leash Area Expansion Project - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie and Councillor Paul Ainslie recommend that City Council amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital budget to create a Colonel Danforth Park Off Leash Area Expansion sub-project costing $140,000 in 2023. The project is fully funded by Section 37 community benefits and is urgent because bidding has closed and delaying past the summer could raise prices.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 1 Bloor Street West to St. Clare’s MultiFaith Housing for the construction of a new theatre and rehearsal space at 877 Yonge Street
topics: boulevard cafes, restaurants; boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants), cafeterias; dining; eating places; food premises
brief: Councillors Dianne Saxe and Josh Matlow recommend that City Council increase the 2023 operating budget by $1,250,000 gross ($0 net), fully funded by Section 37 community benefits from the 1 Bloor Street West-area developments, for St. Clare's MultiFaith Housing to build a new theatre and rehearsal space at 877 Yonge Street. Nightwood Theatre and Tapestry Opera will lease the city-owned building's sub-basement, which needs major renovation to become a wheelchair-accessible community theatre, rehearsal studio and offices shared with other performing arts groups.

title: 1122 Queen Street West - CaféTO Curb Lane Café - Waiving Permit Parking Requirement in Municipal Code Chapter 742 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: parking, restaurants; cafeterias; dining; eating places; food premises
brief: Councillors Alejandra Bravo and Ausma Malik ask City Council to exempt the curb lane café at 1122 Queen Street West (Hello 123) on Lisgar Street from the sidewalk café by-law's permit parking requirement. CaféTO staff found a solution keeping the adjacent alternate-side parking unaffected, so the café can proceed.

title: 77-83 Mutual Street - Extension of Part Lot Control Exemption - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillors Chris Moise and Dianne Saxe recommend that City Council extend the Part Lot Control exemption for 77 to 83 Mutual Street by two years from the expiry of By-law 668-2021. The site, approved for a 36-storey mixed-use building in 2016, needs the exemption to create five conveyable lots.

title: Request to Accept In-kind Donation of New Playground at Dixon Park - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: donation, playground equipment; bequest; toy drive, park equipment; play apparatus; play equipment; play structures
brief: Councillors Vincent Crisanti and Frances Nunziata recommend that City Council authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept an in-kind donation of up to $250,000 in playground and related equipment from KaBOOM!, Inc. for a new playground at Dixon Park. KaBOOM!, a U.S.-based charity active in Canada, has previously partnered with the city on playground builds including Glendorgan Park in 2019.

title: 29 De Marco Boulevard - Request for City Solicitor to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillors Frances Nunziata and Vincent Crisanti recommend that City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the applications for 29 De Marco Boulevard. The Committee of Adjustment refused the owner's applications on April 27, 2023 for a consent to sever the property into two undersized residential lots and minor variances for two proposed dwellings, and the owner appealed on May 17, 2023.

title: Fringe Festival Lane Closure - by Councillor Diane Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: festivals and special events, road closures; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Councillors Diane Saxe and Chris Moise recommend that City Council approve closing Barbara Barrett Lane, between David French Lane and Brunswick Avenue, to vehicles from July 3 to July 18, 2023 for the Toronto Fringe Festival. The festival marks its 35th year with 102 shows at 17 venues from July 5 to 16, and has returned over $6.5 million in box office revenue to artists over three decades.

title: Advancing Truth, Reconciliation and Justice: Supporting Indigenous Housing Partners Right to Self-Determination - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: First Nations; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie and Councillor Shelley Carroll ask City Council to direct the General Manager of Shelter, Support and Housing Administration and the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat to allocate at least 20 percent of all city grant funding under the federal Reaching Home program to Indigenous housing partners. The motion builds on the Meeting in the Middle engagement strategy launched in 2018 with Indigenous leaders to address Indigenous homelessness and support Indigenous organizations' right to self-determination.

title: Appointment of a Toronto Lobbyist Registrar - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appointments, lobbying; lobbyist registrars; lobbyist registry; lobbyists
brief: This is a procedural item: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie and Councillor Mike Colle recommend that City Council appoint the candidate named in a confidential attachment as the city's Lobbyist Registrar. The current registrar, Cristina De Caprio, had her term extended to September 6, 2023, and a selection panel chaired by Councillor Colle has recommended a successor.

title: Proclamation of July 1, 2023 as Chinese Railroad Workers Day - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: congratulatory messages, public holidays; bank holidays; holidays; holidays (public), letter of greeting; proclamations; scrolls
brief: Councillors Ausma Malik and Alejandra Bravo ask City Council to proclaim July 1, 2023 as Chinese Railroad Workers Day. The date marks 100 years since the Chinese Immigration Act of 1923, which banned virtually all Chinese immigration for 24 years after the railway was built largely through the labour of 17,000 men from Guangdong, China. The motion recognizes the separation of families and the hostility Chinese Canadians faced under the exclusion.

title: Requesting Federal Government Support for the City's Climate Goals - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: energy, environmental conditions; energy resources; energy use, environmental health; environmental quality; environmental sensitivity; state of the environment
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher and Alejandra Bravo ask City Council to request that the Government of Canada issue Clean Electricity Regulations prohibiting any increase in gas-fired generating capacity at the Portlands Energy Centre, effective immediately. The motion follows Council's May 2023 objection to more fossil fuel burning in Toronto and the province's move to increase emissions at the Portlands plant while claiming municipal consent is not required.

title: Mitigating Disruption of Betty Sutherland Trail Closure - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: nature trails; interpretive trails; urban wilderness trails
brief: Councillors Shelley Carroll and Jon Burnside ask City Council to request that the provincial Ministry of Transportation, with city divisions, investigate alternatives to the closure of the Betty Sutherland Trail at the Highway 401 crossing. The trail, closed since March 2023 for provincial highway work between Avenue Road and Warden Avenue, will stay shut until winter 2025, severing one of North York's most-used recreational trails with no detour for cyclists or pedestrians.

title: Exploring Toronto as a Charter City - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: policy development; policy making
brief: Councillors Jamaal Myers and Jennifer McKelvie ask City Council to direct the City Manager to report by the end of 2023 with a proposal, including options and budget implications, to inform the public on recognizing and enshrining the City of Toronto's authorities. The motion argues Council should be empowered to enact the policy changes residents elected it to deliver.

title: Authority to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 2490-2514 Yonge Street for the 20 Castlefield Avenue Phase 1 Activation Project - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Jaye Robinson
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillors Mike Colle and Jaye Robinson ask City Council to amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital budget to create a 20 Castlefield Park Phase 1 Activation sub-project, funded by Section 37 community benefits from the 2490 to 2514 Yonge Street development. The lands at 20 Castlefield Avenue were transferred from the Toronto Parking Authority in February 2023 for parkland use; full park construction cannot start until the developer vacates a licensed staging area in 2025 to 2026, so early activation would meet community needs sooner.

title: Reconfiguration and Additional Improvements to the Modular Housing at 175 Cummer Avenue - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: emergency housing, housing; emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless), homes; residences
brief: Councillors Lily Cheng and James Pasternak ask City Council to have the Chief Planner report to the July 19 to 21, 2023 council meeting on the feasibility of reconfiguring the modular supportive housing proposed for 175 Cummer Avenue, including adding one to two more units. The modular units sit in storage in Owen Sound at $77,000 a month while the project awaits an Ontario Land Tribunal hearing, and the motion notes that over 600 seniors living at Cummer Lodge and Willowdale Manor on the same property were not properly consulted.

title: Relocation of Proposed Modular Housing and Designation of 175 Cummer Avenue Green Space as Parkland - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: Councillors Lily Cheng and Nick Mantas ask City Council to have the Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management, the Chief Planner and the Housing Secretariat explore options to relocate the 59 modular housing units proposed for 175 Cummer Avenue, and to designate the site's green space as parkland. The property holds Cummer Lodge, a long-term care home for almost 400 seniors, and Willowdale Manor, housing 256 elderly residents who are mostly low-income and have limited English; the motion notes these seniors, living about 20 metres from the proposed building, were never consulted.

title: 3104 Dundas Street West - Liquor Licence Application - Jayne's Gourmet - Licence 2149250 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillors Gord Perks and Alejandra Bravo recommend that City Council tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor licence for Jayne's Gourmet at 3104 Dundas Street West (licence 2149250), covering indoor and outdoor areas, is not in the public interest unless conditions are attached. The premises sit close to homes, and the community has raised concerns about noise, litter, safety and other disturbances to residents.

title: Staying on Top of Sinkholes: Coordinating Toronto Transit Commission and Toronto Water Preventative Inspections - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: potholes, road safety, water efficiency; pot holes; sink holes; sinkholes, water conservation; water efficient plants; watersaver programs
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher and Ausma Malik ask City Council to direct the City Manager and the Deputy City Manager of Infrastructure and Development Services to work with the TTC's chief executive and Toronto Water's general manager on a proactive inspection schedule for sewers along streetcar lines. The motion follows a recent sinkhole at Queen Street and De Grassi Street, one of several large sinkholes along streetcar lines that preventative sewer inspections could help avoid.

title: Authority for a Limiting Distance Agreement between 4330 Dufferin Street and 4340 Dufferin Street - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: delegation of authority; signing authorities
brief: Councillors James Pasternak and Jamaal Myers ask City Council to authorize the Chief Building Official to enter into a Limiting Distance Agreement with the owner of 4340 Dufferin Street. The agreement would let the city build a solar carport on its lands at 4330 Dufferin Street as part of a retrofit of Emergency Services Headquarters, expected to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 65 percent and energy use by 55 percent.

title: Graphic Image Delivery - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: privacy, publications; brochures; catalogues; flyers; guides (publications); handbooks; information cards; newsletters; notices; posters; reports
brief: Councillors Dianne Saxe and Paula Fletcher ask City Council to direct the City Manager, with the City Solicitor, to report to the October 11 to 13, 2023 council meeting with a draft by-law regulating the unsolicited delivery of graphic images to homes. Residents have protested being forced to view graphic anti-abortion flyers left in mailboxes, which cause distress especially to children and people who have had miscarriages or abortions; London, Ontario and Calgary have adopted by-laws requiring such flyers to be enclosed.

title: Improving CaféTO - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: boulevard cafes; boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants)
brief: Councillors Paula Fletcher and Alejandra Bravo ask City Council to direct the City Manager to review the CaféTO program by the end of 2023 and report to the Executive Committee. The review would seek improvements so permits are issued well in advance of installation dates and communication improves, after local businesses hit problems in May that staff addressed with a temporary fix of installing technically approved locations while permits were still under review.

title: Critical Measures to Restore Ecology and Preserve the History and Culture of Hanlan’s Point Beach and Surrounding Area - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: ecology, history;
brief: Councillors Ausma Malik and Jennifer McKelvie ask City Council to have Parks, Forestry and Recreation expand the clothing-optional beach at Hanlan's Point on city-operated lands between Toronto Island Airport and Gibraltar Point. The motion follows Council's May 2023 adoption of an item recognizing the 2SLGBTQ+ community's history at Hanlan's Point, noting the southern part of the beach lacks adequate markers identifying it as a community hub. Staff reviewed proposals and advised which can proceed now and which need further review.

title: Exploring Municipal Options to Create a Pedestrian and Cycling Connection Between Antler Street and Lappin Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: cycling, pedestrians, transportation (sc); bicycling, pedestrianization
brief: Councillors Alejandra Bravo and Paula Fletcher ask City Council to endorse, in principle, an east-west pedestrian and cycling connection between Antler Street and Lappin Avenue across the rail corridor, and to have staff explore municipal tools and partnerships to create it. Metrolinx had included the connection in its Davenport Diamond public realm plan in 2016 but later dropped it, while Wallace-Emerson residents still rank it a community priority.

title: Ensuring Fairness in Water Billing, Metering and Customer Service - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: billing, water, water billing; water accounts; water bills; water charges
brief: Councillors Jamaal Myers and Vincent Crisanti recommend that City Council raise the income threshold in the definition of Low Income Person under the water and sewage services and utility bill by-law (Chapter 849) from $50,000 or less to $55,000 or less in household income. The change follows up on Council's 2012 response to the Ombudsman's investigation into water billing, metering and customer service.

title: Bright Night in the Boroughs: Bring Nuit Blanche Back to Etobicoke, North York and Scarborough in 2024 - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: arts and culture;
brief: Councillors James Pasternak and Lily Cheng ask City Council to direct the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to report to the November 28, 2023 Economic and Community Development Committee on a plan to include the inner suburbs in Nuit Blanche exhibition areas on an annual basis, starting in 2024. Nuit Blanche has run since 2006 with over 1,600 installations generating more than $443 million for the city, but exhibitions have focused on the downtown core while North York, Scarborough and Etobicoke have suitable, transit-accessible locations.

title: Advancing University Park - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie and Councillor Dianne Saxe ask City Council to authorize the City Manager to negotiate with the Matthews Foundation and the Michael Young Family Foundation to receive a donation fully funding the start of a Municipal Class Environmental Assessment and preliminary design for University Park. The project would convert the southbound section of Queen's Park Crescent, from Hoskin Avenue to College Street, into parkland with pedestrian space and a cycle track, creating 45 acres of connected parkland around the Ontario Legislature and the University of Toronto campus.

title: Making Sense of 311 Reporting - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: [activities in information and communication], non emergency municipal services; 3-1-1; 311; 311 calls; non-emergency city services
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, asks City Council to direct the Executive Director of the Customer Experience Division, with the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation, to expand 311 support to include the operations and maintenance of parks and facilities. The motion aims to close gaps where residents cannot report common issues, such as graffiti on a park sign or bench, through 311.

title: Redirecting the Proceeds of the Sale of a Residual Portion of City-owned land at 276 Lauder Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: sale (action); selling; vending
brief: Councillors Alejandra Bravo and Ausma Malik ask City Council to waive the policy governing proceeds from surplus city land in the case of 276 Lauder Avenue. In 1984 the owner, believing they owned a municipally owned parcel behind the property, built a double garage there with the then-Borough of York's knowledge and approval; officials never told the owner the land had been acquired by the Borough in a 1974 tax sale, and the mistake only surfaced when the property was listed for sale 38 years later. The motion would redirect the proceeds of selling that residual parcel.

title: Pickleball Play in Toronto
topics: city-operated sports facilities, recreation centres, sports; rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers
brief: Staff report on the fast-growing sport of pickleball: the city has expanded outdoor courts from one to 165 over five years and added more than 30 new outdoor courts, with future opportunities including pickleball on underutilized flat surfaces. Council is asked to amend the 2023 capital budget and 2024-2032 capital plan so three new planned lit tennis court complexes in the South, East and North districts include new pickleball courts.

title: Reimbursement for Emergency Electrical Work for the Llama and Capybara Building in High Park
topics: assets, attractions, refund, zoos; cultural attractions; places of interest; tourist attractions; tourist sites, reimbursement
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize amending the construction and license agreement with the Friends of High Park Zoo to transfer up to an additional $31,530 from the City to the Friends. The Friends, a registered charity working with the city, carried out emergency electrical work in the new llama and capybara building in High Park in time for the 2022-2023 winter season, and this reimburses that work under the Parks capital asset management program.

title: Cycling Network Plan - 2023 Cycling Infrastructure Installation - Third Quarter Updates
topics: bicycles, bike paths, bikeway networks; bicycle facilities; bicycle routes; bike routes; bikeway routes; bikeways; cycling routes; shared roadways; signed routes, bicycle paths; bicycle trails; bike trails; cycling paths; cycling trails; off-road paths (cycling), bikes
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize installation of several bikeway projects under the Cycling Network Plan, for which design and consultation are complete. The proposed near-term installations include uni-directional cycle tracks on Bloor Street from Runnymede Road to Resurrection Road and a contra-flow bike lane on Gladstone Avenue from Dundas Street to Peel Avenue, among others.

title: Landfill Gas to Renewable Natural Gas Project and Future Potential Renewable Energy Opportunities at the Green Lane Landfill
topics: landfills, natural gas, renewable energy, solid waste; commercial waste; municipal solid waste; refuse, dumps; garbage dumps; landfill areas; landfill facilities; landfill sites, green energy; green power
brief: This is an information item: staff update City Council on the renewable natural gas project being implemented at the Green Lane Landfill, where Solid Waste Management Services has been exploring energy from landfill gas and biogas since 2015. Council is asked to authorize the General Manager to negotiate and enter into any agreements, including non-competitive procurements, needed for the project and future renewable energy opportunities at the landfill.

title: Long-Term Residual Waste Management Options for the City of Toronto
topics: agreements, garbage, waste management infrastructure; food containers (waste); household garbage; plastic bags (waste); polystyrene (waste); residual solid waste; residual waste; styrofoam (waste); trash, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve the Residual Waste Management Work Plan for planning Toronto's long-term garbage disposal. Landfill space in Ontario, including the city's Green Lane Landfill, is expected to reach capacity around 2034/2035, and building new waste disposal infrastructure can take more than 10 years. The work plan supports the city's long-term waste strategy goals of zero waste and a circular economy.

title: Military Trail Road Reconstruction
topics: road reconstruction; road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Paul Ainslie of Ward 24 Scarborough-Guildwood asks Transportation Services staff for information on road construction delays on Military Trail, which was closed to traffic in both directions between Ellesmere Road and Highcastle Road on September 1. He raises concerns about staff oversight and the prolonged closure's inconvenience to the community, asking whether this reflects a wider pattern with road repairs.

title: 2023 Student Nutrition Program Service Subsidies
topics: health, nutrition, students; diet; dieting; healthy eating, health coverage
brief: The Medical Officer of Health recommends that City Council authorize the transfer of 2023 student nutrition program subsidies to the Angel Foundation for Learning ($4,543,500) and the Toronto Foundation for Student Success ($13,094,900). Student nutrition programs provide meals and snacks, mainly in schools, so children and youth at risk of poor nutrition get safe, adequate and culturally appropriate food; research links school meals to better focus, higher marks and healthier habits.

title: Expanding Access to Dental and Oral Health Services for Torontonians
topics: [activities in health], dental services, health, health promotion; dental care; dental screening; dental work; dentistry; dentists; oral health, health coverage
brief: The Medical Officer of Health reports on Toronto Public Health's dental and oral health work, focused on the city's most vulnerable residents, and plans to expand service by building new city-run dental clinics, renovating existing ones, and growing partnerships with community organizations, hospitals and academic institutions. Council is asked to authorize the Medical Officer of Health to enter into agreements, on an ongoing basis, with community health centres, Aboriginal health access centres, hospitals, health care agencies and academic institutions to deliver mandated dental and oral health services.

title: Report Back on Facilities Management - Custodial Services
topics: facilities;
brief: This is an information item: staff report back on Corporate Real Estate Management's custodial services, including the cleaning approach for return-to-work under the ModernTO desk and space sharing plan, historical and current staffing, and the use of contracted cleaning services. Council requested the report at its May 2023 meeting. Council is asked to receive it for information.

title: ModernTO: 610 Bay Street and 130 Elizabeth Street - Results of Request for Expression of Interest
brief: CreateTO's Board recommends that City Council approve the shortlist of preferred proponents, named in a confidential attachment, for the redevelopment of the former Toronto Coach Terminal and Annex Building at 610 Bay Street and 130 Elizabeth Street. Council is also asked to authorize CreateTO to issue a Request for Proposals. The shortlist follows a Request for Expression of Interest issued November 24, 2022 under the ModernTO program.

title: Nominal License Agreement with FoodShare Toronto #10739 for Non-Exclusive Use of Dragon Alley Community Gardens at 9 Bonar Place
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize a five-year, non-exclusive nominal license agreement with FoodShare Toronto for part of the city-owned lands at 9 Bonar Place, to operate the Dragon Alley Community Gardens. The Toronto Parking Authority operates the site as municipal parking facility Carpark 241.

title: Expropriation of Permanent and Temporary Easements in the Properties known as 19, 21, 23, 25 and 27 Halford Avenue - Stage 2
topics: expropriations, retaining walls; compulsory purchase; eminent domain
brief: Staff recommend that City Council, as approving authority under the Expropriations Act, consider the Ontario Land Tribunal's report and approve the expropriation of permanent and temporary easements from the properties at 19, 21, 23, 25 and 27 Halford Avenue. The easements are needed to remove the current retaining wall, build a new one, and carry out related works. Council authorized starting the expropriation in October 2021; this is Stage 2.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate a Part of 165 The Queensway, for Road Safety Enhancements - Stage 1
topics: expropriations, road construction, road safety; compulsory purchase; eminent domain
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize the start of expropriation proceedings for about 40 square metres of the property at 165 The Queensway, for road safety enhancements as part of The Queensway Complete Street project. This is Stage 1 of the expropriation process: if adopted, staff may serve and publish the Notice of Application for Approval to Expropriate while continuing to negotiate a purchase.

title: Authority to Enter into a Construction Management Agreement with Toronto Community Housing Corporation and to Transfer Funds for the Construction of St. James Town Open Space and Public Realm
topics: agreements, construction, parks and open space areas; building, green spaces; open spaces, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize the City to enter into a construction management agreement with Toronto Community Housing Corporation and transfer up to $4.722 million for building the St. James Town Open Space and Public Realm. Construction would be managed by TCHC with the City, starting in 2024 and running to about 2027. The project, on TCHC-owned land, includes a large open space and a shared walking and cycling corridor.

title: Award of Negotiable Request for Proposal Document Number 2915353397 for the Provision of a Program Registration and Recreation Facilities/Space Booking System
topics: agreements, external services, facility booking; book a room; booking centre; booking space; civic centre public space booking; elevator postings; event booking; event space booking; facilities booking; facilities rental; facility rental; hall booking; meeting room booking; promotional space booking; rental space; room booking; room rates; room rental; space booking, consultants; consulting services; professional services, tenancy agreements
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize an agreement for a new program registration and recreation facilities and space booking system to replace CLASS, the enterprise system supplied by Active Network LLC that the city has used since 1999 for program registration, facility booking and cashiering. CLASS has reached the end of its useful life. The contract follows Negotiated Request for Proposal document 2915353397, and the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation and the Chief Technology Officer would execute the agreement.

title: Administrative Penalty Tribunal Chair's 2022 Annual Report
topics: annual reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: This is an information item: the Director of Court Services presents the 2022 annual report from the Chair of the Administrative Penalty Tribunal. The Tribunal's 25 hearing officers, appointed by Council, provide an independent second review of parking violation disputes, with authority to affirm, vary or cancel a screening officer's decision. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Negotiated Request for Proposals (nRFP) Doc3518771019 for the Provision of Administrative and Underwriting Services for Employee Benefit Programs
topics: benefits, programs, proposals; bids; request for proposal; rfp
brief: Staff recommend that City Council authorize an agreement with Green Shield Canada for administration and underwriting of the City's employee benefit plans, covering extended health care and dental benefits and a wellness portal (Categories A and E). The contract, for the City, Public Health, agencies and corporations under the city's umbrella, and Toronto Police Service and Toronto Transit Commission benefits administration, follows Negotiated Request for Proposal Doc3518771019.

title: 2022 Write-off of Uncollectible Property Taxes and Accounts Receivable
topics: accounts receivable, property taxes; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: This is an information item: staff report on accounts receivable written off as uncollectible in 2022 under the Controller's delegated authority, including property taxes owing, invoiced services, and Provincial Offences Act fines. Council is asked to deem uncollectible and approve the write-off of unpaid property taxes on 18 accounts, covering 107 receivables totalling $75,853 from taxation years 1995 to 2022, since they no longer appear on the assessment roll and cannot be collected.

title: Grant of Easement to Cloverdale Mall Inc. (Cloverdale) for Airspace Surrounding a Bridge Owned by Cloverdale, over The East Mall
topics: easements;
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve a permanent easement for Cloverdale Mall Inc. covering the airspace around its existing bridge over The East Mall. A July 27, 2021 court decision confirmed that Cloverdale already holds an implied easement of necessity over that airspace; this item would register the easement on negotiated terms.

title: 4500 Jane Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve zoning changes at 4500 Jane Street to permit two six-storey mid-rise buildings fronting Gosford Boulevard while keeping the existing 14-storey rental apartment building. Staff describe the infill as a compatible, sensitive addition to the Apartment Neighbourhood, with generous setbacks allowing a double row of trees along Gosford Boulevard and Milo Park Gate.

title: Federation of Canadian Municipalities Annual Conference and Trade Show May 25 - May 28
topics: [organizations in government], conferences, conventions; conference travel, trade shows
brief: This is an information item: Councillor Ainslie thanks the city's FCM Conference Liaison Table, naming staff including Josie Scioli, Aretha Phillips, Karen Jones and Caphan Lieu, plus volunteers, for preparing and managing the Federation of Canadian Municipalities annual conference and trade show held May 25 to 28, 2023. Toronto hosted 1,500 municipal leaders from across the country. Council is asked to receive the conference review for information.

title: Open Data Centralized Platform and Compliance Standards
topics: information, metadata;
