brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie recommends that City Council ask the City Manager to work with the deputy city managers and the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer to develop a centralized open data platform and compliance standards. The city's open data sets are currently published across different platforms, making them hard for residents to find and use; a single user-friendly, accessible platform with clear metadata would increase the value of the open data program.

title: Amendment to Toronto Fire Services’ 2023 Approved Capital Budget for the Next Generation 9-1-1 capital project and Amendment to Blanket Contract 47023903
topics: capital budgets, contracts, fire and rescue services, projects; fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue
brief: Staff recommend that City Council increase Toronto Fire Services' 2023 approved capital budget and cash flow for the Next Generation 9-1-1 capital project by $1.4 million gross, fully funded by a Province of Ontario grant with no impact on the city's debt. Council is also asked to authorize amending the September 1, 2021 contract with Combat Networks Inc. to supply, deliver and install the equipment upgrading the 9-1-1 telephony system to a Next Generation 9-1-1 platform.

title: CreateTO 2022 Financial Results
topics: [organizations in government], financial reports, properties (real estate); annual financial reports; financial statements, property; real estate
brief: CreateTO's Board recommends that City Council receive the CreateTO 2022 Highlights Report for information and approve the 2022 audited financial statements. CreateTO is the city's real estate agency, managing the real estate portfolio and developing city lands to advance Council's housing, sustainability, economic development, cultural and community health goals.

title: City of Toronto Investment Report for the Year 2022
topics: investment, reserve funds; reserves and reserve funds
brief: This is an information item: the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer reports on the performance of the city's investment funds for 2022, the general market update and benchmark performance, and the city's investment policy and procedures. The General Fund, holding working capital and reserves, had a book return of 0.9 percent and generated $92 million in 2022. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Update on Metrolinx Subways Program - Second Quarter 2023
topics: subway stations, urban transit systems; local transit authorities; municipal transit authorities; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; transit agencies; transit operating agencies
brief: This is an information item: staff update City Council on the Province of Ontario's Metrolinx-delivered Subways Program in the second quarter of 2023, covering the Ontario Line, Scarborough Subway Extension, Eglinton Crosstown West Extension and Yonge North Subway Extension, including procurement, design, construction and engagement milestones. Staff recommend that Council ask the Province to fund all associated costs of delivering Cummer Station as part of the Yonge North Subway Extension.

title: SmartTrack Stations Program - Provincial Funding Update
topics: funding, intergovernmental relations, provincial governments, rail transportation, transportation infrastructure, urban transit systems; federal-municipal relations; governmental relations; inter-governmental relations; intergovernmental cooperation; provincial-municipal relations, financing, local transit authorities; municipal transit authorities; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, railway transport; railway transportation, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: This is an information item: staff update City Council on provincial funding for the SmartTrack Stations Program, which together with Metrolinx's GO Expansion will turn heavy rail infrastructure into an urban rapid transit network. In March 2023 Council directed the City Manager to negotiate with the Province to pay all amounts above the original $1.463 billion program budget. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Next Generation 9-1-1 Agreements
topics: agreements, emergency services, technology acquisition; 9-1-1; 911; 911 calls; emergency assistance; emergency response, information technology acquisitions; it acquisitions, tenancy agreements
brief: The City Manager recommends that City Council authorize the City Manager to enter into a Next Generation 9-1-1 Authority Service Agreement with Bell Canada, as required by the CRTC. The technology delivering 9-1-1 emergency calls across Canada is changing from analog networks to internet-protocol-based services under a 2017 CRTC mandate, and this agreement enables the modernization.

title: Temporary Signs By-law Review
topics: by-laws, signs; bylaws, signage
brief: Staff recommend that City Council modernize the Temporary Signs By-law (Chapter 693), which covers signs not permanently installed or affixed to the ground or a structure. The amendments would improve enforcement, respond to new sign types in Toronto, and make the by-law more readable, including placement rules requiring A-frame and portable signs on public property to be placed curbside. Election signs, third-party signs, posters and signs under Chapter 694 were not part of the review.

title: Willowdale Business Improvement Area - Name Change
topics: boards of management, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: Staff recommend that City Council approve renaming the Willowdale Business Improvement Area to the Yonge North York Business Improvement Area, and amend Municipal Code Chapter 19 accordingly. The BIA's Board of Management voted to support the name change, which was also endorsed by the general membership at its January 31, 2023 annual general meeting.

title: Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care Agreement Implementation in Toronto - Update
topics: child care, early childhood education; childcare, early education; ece; kindergartens; pre-school education; preschool education; preschool learning
brief: This is an information item: staff update City Council on implementation of the Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care agreement signed by Ontario and Canada on March 27, 2022, covering April 1, 2022 to May 1, 2023 and the anticipated impacts on Toronto families and child care operators. Staff recommend that Council advocate to the Province to increase Toronto's allocation of child care spaces to meet the Child Care Growth Strategy targets and improve access to affordable, high-quality care.

title: Leveraging Post-Secondary Institutions for a Stronger Workforce - Follow-up
topics: labour force; labor force; workforce
brief: This is an information item: the Chief People Officer reports back on implementing revised omnibus agreements with post-secondary institutions, securing agreements with more institutions and advancing student placement opportunities aligned with city needs and course requirements, ahead of September 2023 student intakes. The Economic and Community Development Committee is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Toronto Action Plan to Confront Anti-Black Racism: Year Four Update
topics: racial discrimination; anti-racism; racism
brief: This is an information item: staff report on year four of the Toronto Action Plan to Confront Anti-Black Racism, noting investments to understand and combat anti-Black racism in city policies and structures, alongside competency and awareness building across the city, while flagging that pandemic impacts have increased the need. Staff recommend that Council direct a review of the first five years' outcomes and the development of a new 10-year action plan.

title: 4, 6, 8 and 10 Beamish Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals, zoning, zoning bylaws; omb; ontario municipal board, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks further instructions from City Council on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the development application at 4, 6, 8 and 10 Beamish Drive. Council is asked to adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and to authorize their public release if adopted.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the CreateTO Board
topics: nomination, public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel - Corporations recommends that City Council appoint candidates to the CreateTO Board, including Ron Carinci as Chair, at pleasure of Council, for terms ending June 16, 2027. The panel interviewed candidates and is recommending two appointments.

title: Appointment of Public Member to the Toronto Hydro Board
topics: nomination, public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel - Corporations recommends that City Council appoint Nicole Martin to the Toronto Hydro Board, at pleasure of Council, for a term ending June 16, 2025. The panel interviewed candidates and is recommending one appointment.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Community Housing Corporation Board of Directors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel - Corporations recommends that City Council appoint seven public members to the Toronto Community Housing Corporation Board of Directors, at pleasure of Council, for terms ending June 16, 2025. One of the seven public members or one of the three tenant directors would be recommended for appointment as Chair.

title: Appointment of Tenant Directors to the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Board of Directors
topics: nomination, public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel - Corporations recommends that City Council appoint two tenant directors to the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Board of Directors. The appointments would be at pleasure of Council, for terms ending June 16, 2025.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Board
topics: nomination;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel - Corporations recommends that City Council appoint candidates to the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Board. The appointments would be at pleasure of Council, for terms ending July 22, 2025, continuing until successors are appointed.

title: Appointment of Deputy City Manager, Infrastructure Services
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Manager recommends that City Council appoint the candidate named in a confidential attachment as Deputy City Manager for the City of Toronto. The appointment would take effect June 16, 2023, subject to the candidate's written acceptance of the employment terms.

title: 18 Portland Street, 1-9 Niagara Street - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Demolition of a Designated Property - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, official plan amendments;
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential instructions on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 18 Portland Street and 1-9 Niagara Street, covering an official plan amendment, zoning amendment and demolition of a designated property. The hearing starts July 24, 2023 for 10 days, and the item cannot be deferred as it is urgent. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the instructions if adopted.

title: University of Toronto St. George Campus Secondary Plan - Official Plan Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: Secondary Plans, official plan amendments;
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the University of Toronto St. George Campus Secondary Plan. The university applied in September 2016 to replace its 1997 secondary plan with an updated framework to manage change and guide development; staff recommended the new plan as Official Plan Amendment 582. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: King-Spadina Secondary Plan - City-initiated Official Plan Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: Secondary Plans, official plan amendments, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the King-Spadina Secondary Plan. Council adopted Official Plan Amendment 486 in January 2020, and it was appealed by 46 appellants; a 12-day hearing is scheduled to start in August after an earlier 26-day hearing was adjourned. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 3401 Dufferin Street and 1 Yorkdale Road - Official Plan Amendment and Dufferin Street Secondary Plan - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: Secondary Plans, official plan amendments;
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for the Yorkdale Shopping Centre site at 3401 Dufferin Street and 1 Yorkdale Road, where Oxford Properties Group proposed a long-term, phased mixed-use development over 30 years and beyond. The plan adds new streets, parks, residential, commercial, office and hotel uses while the shopping centre stays in operation. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: Appointment of Deputy City Manager, Development and Growth
topics: appointments, managers;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Manager recommends that City Council appoint the candidate named in a confidential attachment as Deputy City Manager for the City of Toronto. The appointment would take effect August 14, 2023, subject to the candidate's written acceptance of the employment terms.

title: 2010-2050 Yonge Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 2010 to 2050 Yonge Street, where a 14-storey mixed-use building with 164 homes, ground-floor retail, office uses and a second-floor childcare centre was proposed. The applicant appealed in February 2022 and submitted a revised proposal in April 2023 under Tribunal timelines. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 1911 and 1921 Eglinton Avenue East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 1911 and 1921 Eglinton Avenue East. Samuel Sarick Limited appealed Official Plan Amendment 231, which redesignated the lands as General Employment Areas while the appellant sought a Mixed Use Areas designation; in June 2022 Council accepted a without-prejudice settlement offer. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 1466-1500 Bayview Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 1466 to 1500 Bayview Avenue, where an eight-storey mixed-use building with 153 homes and retail at grade was proposed after a December 2021 revision from a nine-storey plan. A portion of the site was proposed to be conveyed to the city for public use. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 351 to 365 Royal York Road- Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 351 to 365 Royal York Road, where an 11-storey residential building was proposed. The applicant appealed in June 2022 and the hearing runs July 10 to 14, 2023, with a with-prejudice settlement offer on the table, making this the last council meeting for directions before the hearing. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 320 McCowan Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 320 McCowan Road, where the owner proposes demolishing a four-storey above-grade parking structure to build two residential towers of 27 and 31 storeys (88 and 102 metres) on a shared six-storey podium. The applicant appealed in April 2022 after Council failed to decide. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 100 Davenport Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 100 Davenport Road, where a 19-storey mixed-use building with 42 homes was proposed. The applicant appealed in July 2022 after Council missed the 120-day deadline, and a with-prejudice settlement offer expires at the end of the council meeting starting June 14, 2023, making the matter urgent. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 83-95A Bloor Street West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 83-95A Bloor Street West, where a 79-storey mixed-use building with 1,118 homes and commercial uses was proposed. The applicant appealed in July 2022 and the hearing is scheduled for September 18, 2023, with witness statements due in July, making the matter urgent. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 15 Charles Street East and 16 Isabella Street - Zoning Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals, rezoning; omb; ontario municipal board, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 15 Charles Street East and 16 Isabella Street, where a 54-storey mixed-use building with a six-storey base was proposed. The applicant appealed in May 2022 and hearings are set for October 2023, making the matter urgent. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 1-3 Concorde Gate and 10-12 Concorde Place - Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Appeal - Request for Directions
topics: zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 1-3 Concorde Gate and 10-12 Concorde Place, where five residential buildings with nine towers of 40 to 52 storeys were proposed. The applicant appealed Council's failure to decide in January 2022 and made a with-prejudice settlement offer in March 2023 that Council did not accept. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: 1-11 Bloor Street West and 768-784 Yonge Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning tribunals, zoning bylaws; omb; ontario municipal board, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential recommendations on the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal for 1-11 Bloor Street West and 768-784 Yonge Street, where the applicant seeks to raise the maximum height by nine storeys to 94 storeys (338.3 metres). The Ontario Municipal Board had approved 85 storeys for the site in 2017. Council is also asked to authorize public release of the recommendations if adopted.

title: Ombudsman Toronto Report: An Investigation into Toronto Community Housing Corporation's Tenant Human Rights Complaints Process
topics: complaints, human rights, ombudsman, report requests; ombudspersons
brief: This is an information item: the Ombudsman tables its investigation report, dated June 9, 2023, into the Toronto Community Housing Corporation's tenant human rights complaints process, under Section 170(2) of the City of Toronto Act, 2006. The Ombudsman recommends that City Council receive the report for information.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Transit Commission Board
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, public appointments; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the Civic Appointments Committee will interview candidates and recommend two public members for City Council to appoint to the Toronto Transit Commission Board. The City Clerk recommends the appointments be at pleasure of Council for terms ending June 16, 2027.

title: Appointment of Members to the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee
topics: advisory committees, public appointments; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups
brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that City Council appoint 14 community members, named in a confidential attachment, to the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee. The appointments would be at pleasure of Council for terms ending November 14, 2026, or until the committee's mandate is completed.

title: Appointment of Members to the Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer (2SLGBTQ+) Council Advisory Committee

brief: This is a procedural item: staff recommend that City Council appoint 13 individuals, named in a confidential attachment, to the Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer (2SLGBTQ+) Council Advisory Committee. The appointments would be at pleasure of Council for terms ending November 14, 2026, or until the committee's mandate is completed.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will introduce General Bills and Confirming Bills, which formally enact the decisions made at the meeting. No separate decision is attached.

title: Award of Ariba Document Number 3973032085 to PTR Paving Inc. for the General Maintenance Repairs to Roads and Sidewalks including Guide Rail Repairs at Various Locations in the City of Toronto, North York District for Transportation Services
topics: quotations; bids; quotes; request for quotation; rfq
brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel award the contract for general maintenance repairs to roads and sidewalks, including guide rail repairs at various locations in the North York district, to PTR Paving Inc. Three bids were received; PTR's bid of $5,090,440 excluding HST was the lowest, and the award value includes contingency.

title: Award of Ariba Document Number 3952713027 to IL Duca Contracting Inc. for Road Resurfacing, Street Road Reconstruction, Watermain Replacement and Sidewalk Construction at Various Locations for Engineering & Construction Services
topics: quotations; bids; quotes; request for quotation; rfq
brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Procurement Officer recommends that the Bid Award Panel award the contract for road resurfacing, street reconstruction, watermain replacement and sidewalk construction at various locations to IL Duca Contracting Inc. topics: infrastructure, traffic, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, transportation services
brief: Councillor Mike Colle recommends the General Manager of Transportation Services review the feasibility of removing the southbound on-ramp from Lawrence Avenue West to the Allen Road and report back to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee in the fourth quarter of 2023. Traffic at Lawrence and the Allen regularly backs up onto side streets, creating safety concerns for cyclists, motorists and pedestrians, and the lands around Lawrence West station are slated for development.

title: E-scooter Pilot Program
topics: climate, electric scooters, environmental projects, pilot projects; go peds; go-peds; motorized scooters; scooters
brief: The Infrastructure and Environment Committee is asked to have the General Manager of Transportation Services and the Executive Director of Environment and Climate report back at the October 25, 2023 committee meeting with a framework for an e-scooter pilot project, for possible inclusion in an active transportation network. The province began a five-year e-scooter pilot in January 2020 that municipalities could join, but Toronto chose not to participate, which members of the public say has put the city at a disadvantage.

brief: The Director of Urban Forestry recommends Etobicoke York Community Council deny a permit to remove a City-owned 86-centimetre sugar maple at 150 Hillside Avenue. title: 14, 18, 24 and 26 Jopling Avenue South - Residential Demolition Application
topics: demolitions;
brief: The Deputy Chief Building Official asks Etobicoke York Community Council, which has final decision authority, to refuse or grant demolition of four vacant one-storey frame dwellings at 14, 18, 24 and 26 Jopling Avenue South (applications 23 104812, 23 104821, 23 104828 and 23 104831 DEM 00 DM). Staff recommend refusing the applications because there is no building permit application to replace the buildings on the site.

title: Introduction of By-laws
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: Etobicoke York Community Council will introduce bills. This is the formal step of enacting by-laws.

title: No Stopping on Muir Avenue
topics: stopping prohibitions; no stopping
brief: Councillor Perruzza recommends Etobicoke York Community Council prohibit stopping at all times on both sides of Muir Avenue between Knox Avenue and Islington Avenue. Residents raised safety concerns near Islington Avenue, where recent Vision Zero markings narrowed the roadway and cars parking near the intersection have created a dangerous situation.

title: Removal of a Director from the Weston Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management
topics: boards of management, business improvement areas, removal; bia; business improvement associations, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: The General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends Etobicoke York Community Council remove Naveed Mukhtar from the Weston Village Business Improvement Area Board of Management. Community Council has delegated authority to appoint and remove directors of Business Improvement Areas within its geographic boundaries.

title: Snow Plough Damage To Sod Along Sidewalks and Other Landscape Features within the Road Right of Way
topics: sidewalk snow ploughs; ploughs; sidewalk plows; sidewalk snow plows
brief: This is an information item: Transportation Services reports to Etobicoke York Community Council on snow plough damage to sod and other landscape features in the road right-of-way after the 2022-23 winter, including the extent of the damage, the responsibilities of the City, the snow-clearing contractor and residents, and progress on spring repairs. Staff recommend the report simply be received for information.

title: Hertford Avenue - Introduction of Overnight On-Street Permit Parking
topics: on-street parking, permit parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation Services recommends Etobicoke York Community Council introduce overnight on-street permit parking on Hertford Avenue between Bicknell Avenue and the western end of Hertford Avenue, from 12:01 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. daily on the even side, on a street-name basis. Residents requested it to meet their long-term parking needs.

title: Gilpin Avenue - Introduction of Overnight On-Street Permit Parking
topics: on-street parking, permit parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation Services recommends Etobicoke York Community Council introduce overnight on-street permit parking on Gilpin Avenue between Keele Street and Bicknell Avenue, from 12:01 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. daily on the even side, on a street-name basis. Residents requested it to meet their long-term parking needs.

title: Chalkfarm Drive - Parking Amendments
topics: parking;
brief: Transportation Services recommends Etobicoke York Community Council amend the parking rules on Chalkfarm Drive near Chalkfarm Public School: prohibit stopping from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, on the east side between Gravenhurst Avenue and Heavitree Drive/Neames Crescent; rescind the existing school bus loading zone; and prohibit northbound U-turns near the school. The changes would create short-term parking for parents accompanying students and improve safety and reduce congestion.

title: Woodstream Drive - Parking Amendments and Heavy Truck Prohibition
topics: heavy truck prohibitions, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Transportation Services recommends Etobicoke York Community Council, which has final decision authority, prohibit parking at all times on both sides of Woodstream Drive between Rexdale Boulevard and Humberwood Boulevard, and ban heavy trucks there at all times. The measures are meant to keep a clear passage and improve visibility and safety for all road users and park users.

title: John Spence - Appeal DDRT2023-11
topics: animal bites, animal licences, by-laws, dogs; animal licenses; animal registration; cat licences; cat licenses; cat registration; dog licences; dog licenses; dog tags; pet identification tags; pet licences; pet licenses; pet microchips; pet registration; pet tags, bylaws, dog bites
brief: This is a procedural item: the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal will hear the appeal (DDRT2023-11) by John Spence of a dangerous dog order issued October 9, 2022. The tribunal can confirm, change or cancel the order.

title: Kiano Vafaeian - Appeal DDRT2023-13
topics: animal bites, animal licences, by-laws, dogs; animal licenses; animal registration; cat licences; cat licenses; cat registration; dog licences; dog licenses; dog tags; pet identification tags; pet licences; pet licenses; pet microchips; pet registration; pet tags, bylaws, dog bites
brief: This is a procedural item: the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal will hear the appeal (DDRT2023-13) by Kiano Vafaeian of a dangerous dog order issued September 27, 2022. The tribunal can confirm, change or cancel the order.

title: Jason Lemos and Marina Serzhan - Appeal DDRT2023-12
topics: animal bites, animal licences, by-laws, dogs; animal licenses; animal registration; cat licences; cat licenses; cat registration; dog licences; dog licenses; dog tags; pet identification tags; pet licences; pet licenses; pet microchips; pet registration; pet tags, bylaws, dog bites
brief: This is a procedural item: the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal will hear the appeal (DDRT2023-12) by Jason Lemos and Marina Serzhan of a dangerous dog order issued November 19, 2022. The tribunal can confirm, change or cancel the order.

title: 182-184 Spadina Avenue - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is asked to approve rezoning 182-184 Spadina Avenue to permit a hotel with a ground-floor restaurant and 250 hotel suites. The design has a one-storey-plus-mezzanine base with a 14-storey component fronting Spadina Avenue at 41.4 metres and a 15-storey component fronting Cameron Street at up to 44.4 metres. Two levels of underground parking would provide 34 vehicle spaces and 8 bicycle spaces. The Division recommends Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site.

title: 101 - 105 Spadina Avenue and 363 Adelaide Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is asked to approve rezoning the southern portion of 101-105 Spadina Avenue and 363 Adelaide Street West to permit a 39-storey mixed-use building. The site is subject to a proposed land transaction with the City that would reconfigure the parcels to enable the development and create a 1,000-square-metre City park on the northern portion fronting Spadina Avenue and Adelaide Street West. The Division recommends Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site.

title: Parking Amendments to Support CaféTO on College Street between Dovercourt Road to Ossington Avenue
topics: parking prohibitions; no parking
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends parking regulation changes on College Street between Dovercourt Road and Ossington Avenue to support the CafeTO program. The changes shift the daycare pick-up and drop-off area for the local West End YMCA from the north side of College Street to the east side of Dovercourt Road, making room for curb lane cafes while keeping the drop-off area. This includes rescinding the 10-minute maximum parking on the north side of College Street east of Dovercourt Road on weekday mornings. The local BIA and the West End YMCA were consulted.

title: Update on Metrolinx's Ontario Line Construction within the Toronto and East York District
topics: advisory committees; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups
brief: This is an information item: the report updates Toronto and East York Community Council on Metrolinx's Ontario Line construction within the district. It covers the current status of the project, construction timelines, mitigation plans, and community engagement milestones for the planned subway line connecting Exhibition Place in the west to the Ontario Science Centre. No decision is attached to this item.

title: 39-53 Fraser Avenue, 8-42 Pardee Avenue and 135 Liberty Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is asked to approve rezoning 39-53 Fraser Avenue, 8-42 Pardee Avenue, and 135 Liberty Street to permit two non-residential buildings: a 10-storey building fronting Fraser Avenue and an 11-storey building fronting Pardee Avenue, retaining the existing heritage buildings on the site. The buildings would contain 29,417 square metres of office space and 1,340 square metres of retail at grade, with three levels of underground parking for 67 vehicles and 178 bicycles. The Division recommends Council amend Zoning By-law 438-86 for the site.

title: Exclusion of 462 Eastern Avenue from Permit Parking
brief: City Council is asked to amend Schedule B of the Permit Parking chapter to exclude the development at 462 Eastern Avenue, including 150 Logan Avenue and any other addresses for the development. The development contains 307 residential units with 323 parking spaces and 361 bicycle parking spaces, which staff found adequate to meet residents' parking demand. Excluding the development means its residents cannot obtain on-street permit parking.

title: Summer Closure of a portion of Bellair Street for CaféTO
brief: City Council is asked to temporarily close Bellair Street from Cumberland Street to Yorkville Avenue to vehicle traffic from May 15 to October 15, 2023 and again from May 15 to October 15, 2024, to allow curb lane cafes under the CafeTO program. The street has been closed for CafeTO in 2020, 2021, and 2022, and eligible eating establishments would operate under Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 742. Bellair Street is a one-way local road with no TTC service.

title: Pedestrian Safety on Avenue Road, Bloor Street to St. Clair Avenue West
brief: City Council is asked to reduce the speed limit on Avenue Road between Bloor Street and St. Clair Avenue West from 50 to 40 kilometres an hour, following six years of requests from the Avenue Road Safety Coalition over speeding, street racing, and reckless driving. The 2.1-kilometre stretch is already a Community Safety Zone but has seen multiple collisions causing death or serious injury. Council is also asked to request the Toronto Police Services Board to seek enhanced speed enforcement from the Toronto Police Service on this stretch.

title: 152-164 Bathurst Street and 621-627 Richmond Street West - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is asked to approve redeveloping 152-164 Bathurst Street and 621-627 Richmond Street West with an 18-storey mixed-use building, retaining the heritage building at 621 Richmond Street West and 164 Bathurst Street and demolishing the remaining buildings. The project includes ground-floor commercial uses, 217 residential condominium units, 64 vehicle parking spaces, and 224 bicycle spaces. The report also asks Council to approve the Rental Housing Demolition application under Chapter 667 of the Municipal Code. The Division recommends Council amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site.

title: Traffic Control Signals - Bloor Street West and Pauline Avenue/Collegiate Road
topics: traffic control systems; traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: City Council is asked to authorize traffic control signals at the intersection of Bloor Street West and Pauline Avenue/Collegiate Road, and to remove the existing pedestrian crossover on Bloor Street just east of Pauline Avenue. The change is a condition of approval for the developments at 1141 Bloor Street West, 980 Dufferin Street, and 90 Croatia Street; Collegiate Road is a new public road being built on the south side of Bloor Street West. Transportation Services supports the signals. Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Bloor Street West.

title: On-Street Parking Review - Parliament Street
topics: on-street parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: This is an information item: Toronto and East York Community Council asked Transportation Services to study free on-street parking at several locations on Parliament Street for mosques. The report finds the requests cannot be supported at this time but will be considered in the broader City-wide Parking Strategy study underway this year, with a final report expected at City Council in the second quarter of 2024. The Director recommends City Council receive the report for information.

title: Construction Staging Area - Toronto Transit Commission Easier Access Program - Donlands Station (Phase 4)
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction; building, ttc
brief: City Council is asked to authorize a construction staging area for the TTC's Easier Access and Second Exit work at Donlands Station, on the southwest corner of Donlands Avenue and Strathmore Boulevard. The station is being modernized with an at-grade and a below-grade elevator plus a second entrance on the east side of Dewhurst Boulevard south of Strathmore. The request closes the north sidewalk and a 2.0-metre portion of the westbound curb lane on Strathmore Boulevard between Donlands Avenue and a point 25 metres west, from May 1 to September 30, 2023. Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Donlands Avenue.

title: 571 Dundas Street West - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction; building
brief: City Council is asked to authorize a construction staging area for Tridel Corporation and Toronto Community Housing Corporation's 15-storey affordable rental building at 571 Dundas Street West, which includes retail and community uses and a two-level underground garage shared with an adjoining 14-storey condominium. The request closes a 2.9-metre-wide portion of the east sidewalk on Denison Avenue between Grange Avenue and Dundas Street West from January 1, 2023 to March 1, 2025, and rescinds the existing all-times no-parking prohibition there. Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Dundas Street West.

title: Intersection Safety Review - Broadview Avenue and Torrens Avenue
topics: intersections, road safety;
brief: This is an information item: Toronto and East York Community Council directed Transportation Services to review safety and operational concerns at the intersection of Broadview Avenue and Torrens Avenue, including the possibility of upgrading the existing pedestrian crossover to traffic control signals. The report summarizes the assessments and improvements proposed or undertaken. The Director recommends City Council receive the report for information.

title: Intersection Safety Review - Broadview Avenue and Mortimer Avenue/Pottery Road
topics: intersections, road safety;
brief: This is an information item: Toronto and East York Community Council directed Transportation Services to review safety and operational concerns at the intersection of Broadview Avenue and Mortimer Avenue/Pottery Road. The report summarizes the assessments and improvements proposed or undertaken by Transportation Services. The Director recommends City Council receive the report for information.

title: Intersection Safety Review - Broadview Avenue and Chester Hill Road
topics: intersections;
brief: City Council is asked to rescind the existing prohibited pedestrian crossing on Broadview Avenue at Chester Hill Road, between the south curb line of Chester Hill Road and a point 30.5 metres north of its north street line. Toronto and East York Community Council had directed Transportation Services to review safety and operational concerns at the intersection, and this report covers the assessments and improvements proposed or undertaken. Council approval is required because the TTC operates on Broadview Avenue. The Director recommends Council rescind the crossing prohibition.

title: Status Report on the Gerrard-Carlaw North Transit Oriented Community
topics: housing, public transit; homes; residences, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: This is an information item: the report updates Toronto East York Community Council on the Gerrard-Carlaw North Transit Oriented Community, where Infrastructure Ontario has partnered with Choice REIT. The proposal at 425-471 Carlaw Avenue includes a mixed-use podium with three towers of 30, 35, and 40 storeys, tied to the Ontario Line's Gerrard-Carlaw station. It includes preliminary planning comments, outstanding issues, and feedback from the City's and Infrastructure Ontario's public engagement. The report is recommended for receipt for information.

title: 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 Charles Street West; 11, 13 Irwin Avenue; 10 Isabella Street, 145 St. Luke Lane and 750 and 756 Yonge Street - Inclusion of 11 Properties on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is asked to include 11 properties on the City's Heritage Register for their cultural heritage value and interest. The properties are 5, 7, 9, 11, and 13 Charles Street West; 11 and 13 Irwin Avenue; and 10 Isabella Street, all in the Toronto Centre area. The Senior Manager of Heritage Planning recommends the inclusions in accordance with the listing statements prepared for each property.

title: 72-78 Berkeley Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council is asked to approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 72-78 Berkeley Street, in connection with the development of the site, and to authorize entering into a heritage easement agreement. The properties contain a row of four attached Bay-and-Gable house-form buildings completed together in 1883, designated under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act. The Senior Manager of Heritage Planning recommends Council consent to the alterations, with conditions, under Section 33 of the Act.

title: 164 Bathurst Street - Alterations to a Heritage Property and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage designation;
brief: City Council is asked to approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 164 Bathurst Street, at the southwest corner of Bathurst Street and Richmond Street West, and to authorize a heritage easement agreement. The property dates to about 1875 and is a notable surviving nineteenth-century mixed-use commercial building with Italianate influences. The alterations would allow an 18-storey mixed-use residential building to be constructed, and the Senior Manager of Heritage Planning recommends Council approve the changes under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 63 Old Forest Hill Road - Alterations and Demolition of Heritage Attributes to a Designated Heritage Property
topics: demolitions, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council is asked to approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 63 Old Forest Hill Road, the Dorothy (McLaughlin) Tait House, a 1934 Arts and Crafts residence designed by architect Douglas E. Kertland. The changes would allow a contemporary three-storey rear addition. The Senior Manager of Heritage Planning recommends Council approve the alterations under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and the demolition of some heritage attributes under Section 34(1)1.

title: 127 Strachan Avenue - Alterations and Demolition of a Heritage Attribute to a Designated Property and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: City Council is asked to approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 127 Strachan Avenue, and to authorize a heritage easement agreement for the property. The report also asks Council to approve demolishing one heritage attribute: the single-storey rear wing identified in the designation by-law. The changes are tied to an Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment application for 109-127 Strachan Avenue for a new 13-storey mixed-use building that retains and alters the designated building. The Senior Manager of Heritage Planning recommends Council approve the alterations under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and the demolition of the rear wing.

title: 41 - 53 Fraser Avenue, 135 Liberty Street and 42 Pardee Avenue - Alterations to Designated Properties, Demolition of a Building on a Designated Property and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement - Approval Report
topics: demolitions, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council is asked to approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 41 and 47 Fraser Avenue and 135 Liberty Street, and to authorize heritage easement agreements, in connection with a zoning application that would add two buildings of 10 and 11 storeys above the heritage buildings. The report also asks Council to approve demolishing the former power house building at 42 Pardee Avenue, which is designated under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act. The Senior Manager of Heritage Planning recommends Council approve the alterations under Section 33 of the Act and the demolition.

title: 2721 Danforth Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment, and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Appeal Report
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant is appealing the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for 2721 Danforth Avenue, which propose two towers of 35 and 55 storeys, plus a Draft Plan of Subdivision application to divide the land into four blocks. The applicant appealed after Council did not decide in time. The Division recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the applications in their current form while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 109-127 Strachan Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant is appealing the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for 109-127 Strachan Avenue after Council did not decide in time. Since the appeal, the applicant has worked with City staff on a revised proposal for a 13-storey mixed-use building at 43.5 metres, with a Case Management Conference held February 9, 2023 and the next set for May 26, 2023. The Division recommends City Council authorize the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in support of the revised proposal, subject to the report's recommendations.

title: 1366 Yonge Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council is asked to refuse the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment application for a 41-storey mixed-use building with 489 dwelling units at 1366 Yonge Street. Planning staff found the proposal does not conform with the Official Plan or the Yonge-St. Clair Secondary Plan, has not shown how a tall building can be accommodated on the site, and does not meet the intent of the Tall Building Design Guidelines. The Division recommends Council refuse the application and authorize the City Solicitor to defend the refusal at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 21-31 Sherbourne Street North - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is asked to enact a Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for 21-33 Sherbourne Street North to allow five residential lots to be created as parcels of tied land within a common elements condominium, which includes a below-grade parking garage, access stairwells, and servicing elements. The exemption implements the site-specific zoning and site plan approvals, and the owner would register a restriction under the Land Titles Act so no part of the lands can be conveyed or mortgaged separately. The Division recommends Council enact the by-law.

title: 241 Church Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Removal of Holding Symbol ("H") - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is asked to remove the holding symbol from the site-specific zoning by-law for 241 Church Street, which permits a 53-storey mixed-use building with ground-floor commercial uses and residential units totalling 36,550 square metres. The holding symbol requires certain conditions to be fulfilled before development proceeds, and staff have reviewed the submitted materials and are satisfied the conditions are met. The Division recommends Council amend Zoning By-law 1017-2022 to remove the holding symbol so the project can proceed.

title: 25 St. Mary Street - Official Plan Amendment,  Zoning Amendment, and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, official plan amendments, planning & development (sc), zoning;
brief: City Council is asked to approve redeveloping 25 St. Mary Street by demolishing the existing 24-storey rental apartment building with 259 rental units and building two mixed-use towers of 59 and 54 storeys. The proposal includes a minimum of 259 replacement rental units, 1,024 new residential units, 310 square metres of ground-floor retail, a 730-square-metre child care facility, and a 500-square-metre parkland dedication. The Division recommends Council amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site.

title: 49 Ontario Street and 72-94 Berkeley Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council is asked to approve a zoning amendment for 49 Ontario Street and 72-94 Berkeley Street to permit three buildings of 11, 39, and 44 storeys with 1,094 dwelling units, 1,099 square metres of retail, and 15,206 square metres of office space. The proposal retains the existing heritage rowhouses, adds an east-west mid-block connection, and includes a 581-square-metre public park. The Division recommends Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site.

title: 2039-2049 Yonge Street and 40-50 Tullis Drive - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is asked to approve an Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment for 2039-2049 Yonge Street and 40-50 Tullis Drive to permit an 11-storey mixed-use building fronting Yonge Street and seven three-storey residential townhouses fronting Tullis Drive. The two parts would be connected by a single-storey service area with a one-level underground parking garage. The Division reviewed the application and recommends approval.

title: 208 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is asked to approve rezoning 208 Bloor Street West to permit a 34-storey mixed-use building with 142 dwelling units and 440 square metres of non-residential gross floor area. The Division reviewed the application and recommends approval. Council is asked to amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site.

title: Pedestrian Crossing Protection - Orton Park Road and Botany Hill Road/Slan Avenue
topics: pedestrian crossovers, traffic management, transportation; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, transportation services
brief: City Council is asked to authorize installing a pedestrian crossover at the intersection of Orton Park Road and Botany Hill Road/Slan Avenue. Transportation Services assessed the location and recommends the crossover to give vulnerable road users a safer way to cross the intersection. Council approval is required because the TTC operates a transit service on Orton Park Road. The Director recommends Council authorize the installation.

title: 4630 Kingston Road - Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant is appealing the Zoning By-law Amendment application for a 13-storey mixed-use building at 4630 Kingston Road, with 417 residential units and 273.1 square metres of retail. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on August 23, 2022 after Council missed the Planning Act deadline. City Planning does not support the application in its current form, citing unresolved issues around the mix of uses and servicing. The Division recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the tribunal in opposition while continuing discussions.

title: 2993 to 3011 Sheppard Avenue East and 1800 to 1814 Pharmacy Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment - Final Report
topics: official plan amendments, planning, zoning;
brief: City Council is asked to approve a 22-storey mixed-use building at 2993 to 3011 Sheppard Avenue East and 1800 to 1814 Pharmacy Avenue, with 410 residential units and ground-floor commercial retail on Sheppard Avenue East and Pharmacy Avenue. The proposal redesignates the lands from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Areas and establishes a site and area specific policy requiring at least 1,500 square metres of non-residential uses in any future redevelopment. The Division recommends Council amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will review the Order Paper for the May 10, 2023 meeting. The Order Paper sets out the business Council will consider. No decision is attached to this item.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions, and announcements will be made at the May 10, 2023 City Council meeting. These are ceremonial or informational moments in the meeting's agenda. No decision is attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions at the May 10, 2023 meeting. Filing petitions is a standard procedural step in the Council agenda. No decision is attached.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council will declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act at the May 10, 2023 meeting. The declarations are a standard transparency step before Council considers its agenda. No decision is attached.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council introduces the committee reports and new business from City officials for the May 10, 2023 meeting. The reports include the Executive Committee's report from May 2, the Economic and Community Development Committee's from April 25, the General Government Committee's from April 20, the Infrastructure and Environment Committee's from April 26, and the Planning and Housing Committee's from April 27. No decision is attached to this item.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes of the regular meeting held March 29, 30, and 31, 2023. Confirming the minutes makes them the official record of that meeting. No other decision is attached.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the May 10, 2023 City Council meeting opens with the call to order, the singing of O Canada, and a moment of silence. These are the standard opening formalities of a Council meeting. No decision is attached.

title: A Housing Pledge for the City of Toronto
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: City Council is asked to endorse Toronto's Municipal Housing Pledge committing to 285,000 new homes by 2031. The pledge follows the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing's October 25, 2022 request, tied to Bill 23, the More Homes Built Faster Act, and is Toronto's share of the province's 1.5 million new homes target. The Chief Planner recommends Council affirm its commitment to the 2031 Housing Target and direct staff to draft the pledge letter, with the strategies to get there set out in the Housing Action Plan 2022-2026 and HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan.

title: Housing Now Initiative - 2023 Progress Update
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: This is a progress update on the Housing Now Initiative, which has dedicated 21 of the City's prime transit-oriented sites, plus five more pipeline sites, to affordable and market rental housing in mixed-income, mixed-use communities. The City has committed over $1.3 billion in land value, capital funding, and financial incentives to the program. Council is asked to adopt the confidential staff instructions for the sites at Bloor/Kipling Block 1 (5207 Dundas Street West) and 50 Wilson Heights Boulevard. The update supports the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan and the Housing Action Plan 2022-2026.

title: 2022 Toronto Employment Survey
topics: [activities in employment and labour], employment & labour (sc), research; studies; surveys (research)
brief: This is an information item: the 2022 Toronto Employment Survey recorded 1,484,600 jobs citywide, an increase of 33,080 jobs or 2.3 percent from 2021. The bulletin reports counts of employment and business establishments, and notes Toronto's economy partially recovered in 2022 after the record job losses of 2020 and 2021 from the COVID-19 pandemic. The Chief Planner recommends the Planning and Housing Committee receive the report for information.

title: 5207 Dundas Street West - Bloor-Kipling (Six Points) Block 1 - Housing Now - Decision Report - Approval
topics: affordable housing, housing, zoning bylaws; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council is asked to approve zoning for the Housing Now development at Block 1 of the Bloor-Kipling (Six Points) site, at 5207 Dundas Street West, where KT Housing Now Six Points LP was selected as the proponent in 2022. Block 1 is one of seven publicly owned blocks created when the Six Points Interchange was decommissioned in Etobicoke Centre; earlier rezoning permits mixed-use development on Blocks 1 and 5 and a new park on Block 2. The Chief Planner recommends Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site.

title: 770 Don Mills Road, Ontario Science Centre - Heritage Request
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik recommends City Council reaffirm its interest in protecting and preserving the Ontario Science Centre at 770 Don Mills Road, whose future is in question. The Brutalist building was designed by award-winning Toronto architect Raymond Moriyama to mirror the hills and tiers of the Don Valley. Council is also asked to direct the Senior Manager of Heritage Planning to report on evaluating the Science Centre under Ontario Regulation 9/06, the criteria for municipal heritage designation.

title: Feedback on Potential Provincial Regulation(s) on Municipal Rental Replacement By-laws
topics: [activities in planning and development], by-laws; bylaws
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford recommends the Planning and Housing Committee forward the province's proposal on future regulations for municipal rental replacement by-laws to City Council without recommendation, and ask the Chief Planner and City Solicitor to report directly to the May 10-12, 2023 Council meeting with a response. The Ontario Regulatory Registry proposal, released April 6, could limit Council's ability to secure replacement rental housing and assistance for displaced tenants. Municipalities currently may regulate demolition or conversion of rental properties with six or more units.

title: Ready, Set, Midtown: Zoning Review - City Initiated Zoning By-law Amendments for Select Low-rise Areas - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Secondary Plans, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council is asked to enact City-initiated zoning by-law amendments to implement the Yonge-Eglinton Secondary Plan, also known as Official Plan Amendment 405, for select low-rise areas. The Ready, Set, Midtown initiative covers lands designated Neighbourhoods A, a portion of low-rise Apartment Neighbourhoods, and a portion of Parks and Open Space Areas. The Chief Planner recommends Council amend city-wide Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the identified areas.

title: Toronto Green Standard Update: Advancing Net Zero Emissions in New Development
topics: green standards, sustainable development; environmental sustainability; green development; sustainability; sustainable; sustainable buildings; sustainable cities; sustainable design; sustainable energy; sustainable transportation, green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards
brief: City Council is asked to adopt revised Toronto Green Standard Version 4 performance measures for 2022 embodied emissions, advancing net-zero emissions in new development through embodied emissions caps. The revision follows a July 2021 Council request for an update on the 2022 study work and is a key part of reaching zero-emissions buildings. The Chief Planner recommends Council direct that development follow the Green Standard performance measures in effect at the time of a complete site plan application, and adopt the revised measures in Attachment 1.

title: Update Downsview: Draft Secondary Plan and Draft Community Development Plan Priorities - Status Report
topics: Secondary Plans, community development; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: This is a status report on Update Downsview, bringing forward the draft Downsview Secondary Plan and draft Community Development Plan priorities. The study began in September 2021 after Bombardier announced its departure from the Downsview Airport lands, under Site and Area Specific Policy 596, which requires minimum non-residential uses and affordable housing. The Division recommends City Council direct the Chief Planner to use the draft Secondary Plan as the basis for further stakeholder and public consultation.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods: Multiplex Study - Final Report
topics: housing, multi-unit dwellings; homes; residences, multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings
brief: City Council is asked to approve the Multiplex Study's final report, which would allow more multiplex housing in Toronto's low-rise Neighbourhoods. With at least 700,000 new Torontonians expected by 2051, the report finds recent housing growth has concentrated in mid- and high-rise apartments downtown and on Avenues, while low-rise options like multiplexes have not kept pace. The Chief Planner recommends Council amend the Official Plan through Official Plan Amendment 649 and amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 to permit multiplexes more broadly.

title: 1313 Queen Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is asked to state its intention to designate 1313 Queen Street West, the former Police Station Number 6, under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. Built in 1931-32 to designs from the City Architect's Office, the building sits on the southwest corner of Queen Street West and Cowan Avenue in Parkdale and is noted for its architectural merit. The Chief Planner recommends the designation for the property's cultural heritage value.

title: 789-793 Don Mills Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is asked to state its intention to designate 789-793 Don Mills Road, known as Foresters House, under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The building was constructed in 1965-1967 as the corporate headquarters of the Independent Order of Foresters, a fraternal organization established in Canada in the 1870s, and was part of the Olympia Square complex just south of Eglinton Avenue East. The Chief Planner recommends the designation for the property's cultural heritage value.

title: 4888 Dundas Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is asked to state its intention to designate 4888 Dundas Street West, the Alexander MacPherson House, under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The 1879 brick Italianate house in the former village of Islington served as the village post office from 1887 to 1906 and the telephone exchange from 1912 to 1925. The Chief Planner recommends the designation for the property's cultural heritage value.

title: 153 and 185 Eastern Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is asked to state its intention to designate 153 and 185 Eastern Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The vernacular mid-century industrial buildings on the south side of Eastern Avenue between Cherry Street and Bayview Avenue were occupied by Dominion Wheel and Foundries. The Toronto Preservation Board considered the item on March 23, 2023. The Chief Planner recommends the designation for the properties' cultural heritage value.

title: 15 Elm Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is asked to state its intention to designate 15 Elm Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The two-storey Georgian Revival house-form building, completed by 1868, is a rare surviving Confederation-era example on the south side of Elm Street between Yonge and Bay streets, part of a row of 19th-century dwellings later adapted with commercial storefronts. The Chief Planner recommends the designation for the property's design, associative, and contextual value.

title: Technical Amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council is asked to enact technical amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013 that correct typographical errors, clarify or correct interpretations and permissions, and adjust zoning and overlay map boundaries. All the revisions reflect Council's original intentions when the by-law provisions were approved and do not change the substance of the by-laws. The Chief Planner recommends Council enact the amendments and authorize the City Solicitor to make stylistic and technical changes.

title: 22-36 Greenbriar Road - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report- Approval
topics: demolitions, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council is asked to approve redeveloping 22-36 Greenbriar Road with a 22-storey residential building (68.4 metres) containing 320 dwelling units and 24,246 square metres of gross floor area. The proposal includes 145 parking spaces in a two-level underground garage, 241 bicycle spaces, and access via Talara Drive. The companion rental housing demolition application would demolish two rental units in eight existing semi-detached houses. The Division recommends Council amend the Official Plan and the former North York zoning by-law for the site.

title: 1800 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Report for Information
topics: Official Plans, applications, public consultation, zoning bylaws; application process, community consultation; consultation; public hearing, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an information item: the report responds to a North York Community Council direction to report on a public engagement strategy for the proposed redevelopment at 1800 Sheppard Avenue East. The multi-phase proposal covers an 18.8-hectare site with 12 new buildings of 18 to 58 storeys, 7,840 square metres of parkland, a multi-use trail, new streets, and about 4,700 residential units. The Director recommends City Council receive the report for information.

title: 25 Old York Mills Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-Law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, appeals, mixed use areas, official plan amendments, permits, zoning bylaws; permit renewal, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant is appealing the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment application for a 12-storey mixed-use building at 25 Old York Mills Road (38.05 metres plus a 4.5-metre mechanical penthouse), with residential uses, a place of worship with multifunction space, a commercial community space, and a child care centre. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on January 6, 2023 after Council did not decide in time. The Director recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the tribunal in opposition while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: 131 Lyon Court and 836, 838 Roselawn Avenue  - Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, planning tribunals, zoning bylaws; omb; ontario municipal board, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant is appealing the Zoning By-law Amendment application for a 35-storey mixed-use building at 131 Lyon Court and 836, 838 Roselawn Avenue (111.40 metres), with 472 dwelling units and 397.5 square metres of retail. A companion rental housing demolition application proposes demolishing the existing 53 rental units and replacing them in the new building. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on September 14, 2022 after Council missed the Planning Act deadline. The Director recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the tribunal in opposition while continuing discussions.

title: 2451 Dufferin Street - Zoning By-Law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant is appealing the Zoning By-law Amendment application for a 20-storey mixed-use building at 2451 Dufferin Street (65.3 metres including a 5.5-metre mechanical penthouse), with 462 dwelling units and 706 square metres of ground-floor commercial space. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on November 14, 2022 after Council missed the Planning Act deadline; the first Case Management Conference was held February 22, 2023. The Director recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the tribunal in opposition while continuing discussions.

title: Elvaston Drive - Community Safety Zone
topics: community safety, school zone review, transportation; transportation services
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside recommends City Council designate a Community Safety Zone, in effect at all times, on both sides of Elvaston Drive between Sloane Avenue and a point 125 metres west of Halkin Crescent. Residents have raised concerns about speeding on the local road, which sits close to Sloane Public School. The zone would allow for safety-focused traffic measures.

title: 368-372 Briar Hill Avenue - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: condominium housing, exemptions, part lot control; condominiums; condos, exceptions
brief: City Council is asked to enact a Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for 368-372 Briar Hill Avenue to allow seven conveyable lots for three-storey townhouses. A related common element condominium application over the driveway from Briar Hill Avenue is under staff review. The Director recommends Council enact the by-law.

title: 36-46 Monclova Road - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: part lot control;
brief: City Council is asked to enact a Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for 36-46 Monclova Road (previously 195 Exbury Road) so ten conveyable lots can be created for three-storey townhouses in two blocks of five. A related common element condominium application is under staff review. The Director recommends Council enact the by-law.

title: 147 Overbrook Place - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: approval, exemptions, part lot control, planning; exceptions
brief: City Council is asked to enact a Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for 147 Overbrook Place so ten conveyable lots can be created, each for a semi-detached freehold dwelling fronting Overbrook Place. Planning staff found the proposal consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement, the Growth Plan, and the Official Plan. The Director recommends Council enact the by-law.

title: 172 - 186 Finch Avenue West, 1-33 Grantbrook Street and 305-313 Hendon Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant appealed the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for 172-186 Finch Avenue West, 1-33 Grantbrook Street, and 305-313 Hendon Avenue on November 30, 2022 after Council did not decide in time. The proposal is for mid-rise buildings, low-rise apartments, and townhouses of three to 11 storeys (12 to 38 metres) with 49 residential units, with a Case Management Conference set for March 30, 2023. The Director recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition.

title: 36, 38 and 40 Churchill Avenue - Part Lot Control Exemption Applications - Approval Report
topics: part lot control;
brief: City Council is asked to enact a Part Lot Control Exemption By-law for 36, 38 and 40 Churchill Avenue to allow 14 townhouse units to be created as conveyable lots under freehold ownership, tied to a common elements condominium. The exemption would let the owner transfer or mortgage title to individual townhouse parcels. The Director recommends Council enact the by-law.

title: Honouring Canadian Music Legend Gordon Lightfoot - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: public art; outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council ask the City Manager to report back by the third quarter of 2023 on a plan for a statue honouring folk music legend Gordon Lightfoot, including a suitable location such as Massey Hall. Lightfoot, a long-time Toronto resident, died May 1, 2023 at age 84 after a career that began in the city in 1959 and included 171 performances at Massey Hall. He rose to international fame in the 1970s with songs celebrating Canadian life.

title: Extending 2023 Application Due Dates for Property Tax and Utility Relief programs for Low-Income Seniors and Low-Income Disabled Persons  - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: taxes; levies
