brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends City Council extend the 2023 application deadline for the City's property tax, water, and solid waste relief programs for low-income seniors and low-income disabled persons from August 31 to October 31, 2023. Council extended the deadline the same way in 2020, 2021, and 2022, and the motion notes these residents may have been disproportionately affected by the pandemic and inflation. The change requires amending the Municipal Code chapters on taxation, waste collection, and water and sewage services.

title: Recommitting to Taking Action on Impaired Driving in Toronto - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Mike Colle
topics: driving;
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends City Council recommit to action on impaired driving, which police-reported data shows kills or injures more Canadians than any other crime and remains the leading factor in serious road crashes. The motion asks Council to direct the General Manager of Transportation Services, with the Toronto Police Service, to report back in the fourth quarter of 2023 with an update on Council's 2022 direction for an impaired driving report.

title: Re-Opening and Amending MM2.12 Authorization to release Section 37 funds to the Sir William Campbell Foundation for Public Realm Improvements on Queen Street West respecting Relic Linear Park - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: community improvement plans;
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council amend its December 2022 decision releasing Section 37 funds to the Sir William Campbell Foundation for the Relic Linear Park project. The funds were for the Foundation, which operates Campbell House Museum, to build Relic Linear Park as part of the Grange Green Plan, but unforeseen construction delays have occurred. The amendment would change the wording of the original funding decision to reflect the delays.

title: Delta Bingo & Gaming Proposed Relocation to 360 Evans Avenue - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends City Council approve Delta Bingo and Gaming's proposal to relocate its Class A charitable bingo hall from 1799 St. Clair Avenue to 360 Evans Avenue. The relocation proposal went to the City on March 22, 2023 with public notice and a community meeting on April 19, 2023, and the Committee of Adjustment approved a minor variance to permit the bingo hall at 360 Evans Avenue in September 2022, a decision the City Solicitor appealed the following month. Council approval is needed under the AGCO's requirements.

title: Transfer of sidewalk vending permit (York Street) - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: permits, sidewalks, street vending; boulevard vending; curb lane vending; curblane vending; food carts; food vending carts; hot dog carts; sidewalk vending; vending, permit renewal
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik asks City Council to override the moratorium on transferring street vending permits and direct staff to transfer Sidewalk Vending Permit R53-2126164 from Nanci Mantis, the longtime operator of a hotdog cart on the east side of York Street, 15 metres north of Bremner Boulevard, to a family member. The motion is urgent because the permit holder's health is failing and the cart is the family's main income; the moratorium otherwise bans new permits and transfers.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 390 to 440 Dufferin Street and 41 Alma Avenue to Transportation Services for boulevard, roadway and safety improvements on Peel Avenue and Gladstone Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: funding, transportation; financing, transportation services
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks City Council to add $300,000 to the 2023-2032 capital budget for Transportation Services, fully funded by Section 37 community benefits from the development at 390 to 440 Dufferin Street and 41 Alma Avenue, for reconstructing Peel Avenue and Gladstone Avenue north of Queen Street West. The design widens the pedestrian boulevard, narrows the roadway, and improves accessibility and road safety following the 2010 elimination of the Dufferin Jog.

title: Exploring All Options and Ensuring Multi-language Tenant Engagement In Proposed Alterations at Willowdale Manor - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: languages, tenants; renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks City Council, as shareholder, to direct the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation and Toronto Community Housing Corporation to pause accessibility renovations at Willowdale Manor (175 Cummer Avenue) in order to explore all available options and engage tenants in multiple languages. More than 100 seniors attended an April 24, 2023 meeting in English, Chinese, Mandarin and Farsi about the planned work, which includes removing the elevated stage and changing the kitchen.

title: Removal of a Commercial Loading Zone to Accommodate a CaféTO Curb Lane Café on Danforth Avenue - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: loading zones; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks City Council to rescind the commercial loading zone on the south side of Danforth Avenue, from 33.8 metres east of Chester Avenue to 10 metres further east, so a local restaurant can obtain a CafeTO curb lane cafe permit. The existing loading zone blocks the permit, and the matter is urgent so the restaurant can open its curb lane cafe alongside other local establishments.

title: 73-83 Brooklawn Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Appeal Committee of Adjustment Decision to the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillor Gary Crawford asks City Council to authorize the City Solicitor to appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of minor variances for 73-83 Brooklawn Avenue to the Toronto Local Appeal Body, and to appear there as a party opposing the decision. The appeal covers eight minor variance and consent applications, including A0315/20SC and B0050/20SC.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 1100 Sheppard Avenue West to the Transportation Services Division for the Design and Construction of Public Realm and Road Safety Improvements - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillor James Pasternak asks City Council to release $400,000 in Section 37 funds from the development at 1100 Sheppard Avenue West to Transportation Services for the design and construction of public realm and road safety improvements. The increase goes into the 2023-2032 capital budget and plan; the money was secured for local streetscape improvements.

title: 2998 Dundas Street West - Liquor Licence Application - Chiang Mai Thai Kitchen & Bar Junction Licence 2103917 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor licence for Chiang Mai Thai Kitchen and Bar at 2998 Dundas Street West is not in the public interest unless conditions are attached. The application is for an outdoor area, and residents have raised concerns about noise, litter, safety, and other disturbances near residential units. Council's position would ask the City Clerk to advise the AGCO Registrar that the licence should carry conditions addressing the community's concerns.

title: 4097 Lawrence Avenue East and 197 to 201 Galloway Road  - Technical Amendment to By-law 251-2022 - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: zoning;
brief: This is a technical fix: Councillor Paul Ainslie asks City Council to amend By-law 251-2022, which permits the redevelopment of 4097 Lawrence Avenue East and 197 to 201 Galloway Road, to correct errors and omissions in the site-specific regulations, including the maximum building height rules. The by-law was enacted in March 2022 together with a Section 37 agreement.

title: Keele Reservoir Feasibility for Heating and Cooling at York University - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: renewable energy; green energy; green power
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza asks City Council to have the General Manager of Toronto Water, in consultation with the environment and climate office, give York University the technical information it needs to study, at York's own expense, whether the City's Keele Reservoir could heat and cool the university's Keele Campus. The project would exchange thermal energy between the reservoir and the campus district energy system, cutting greenhouse gas emissions and campus electricity demand in line with the TransformTO Net Zero Strategy.

title: Street Vending Location Change - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: street vending; boulevard vending; curb lane vending; curblane vending; food carts; food vending carts; hot dog carts; sidewalk vending; vending
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik asks City Council to let hotdog cart operator Michael Wakulicz apply for a new street vending permit, despite the current moratorium on new permits. His long-held permit at the north-east corner of Queen and Spadina was revoked because of Metrolinx's Ontario Line construction, and he needs a new location in Ward 10 to keep operating and earning a living.

title: Requesting Accountability for the Destruction of the Community Garden at 133 Broadway Avenue - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: gardens, ombudsman; ombudspersons
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow asks City Council to have the Ombudsman investigate Toronto Community Housing Corporation's destruction of the community garden at 133 Broadway Avenue and to recommend ways to empower residents to animate public and private spaces. The garden was built over a decade by resident Brian Gorrell, who put in countless hours and $20,000 of his own money before officials tore it out.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Rebuild the Community Garden at 133 Broadway Avenue - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: gardens;
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow asks City Council to add $50,000 gross ($0 net) to the 2023 operating budget, fully funded by Section 37 money from the development at 75 Broadway Avenue, to rebuild the community garden at 133 Broadway Avenue. The 2,400-square-foot garden was built over a decade by resident Brian Gorrell with $20,000 of his own money before Toronto Community Housing officials destroyed it.

title: Development of Green Building Standards in Ontario Building Code - Authorizing Receipt of Funds from Municipal Affairs and Housing - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: building codes;
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford asks City Council to authorize City Planning to receive funds from the Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing as reimbursement for services, and to increase City Planning's operating budget to accept them. The money supports City staff work with the Building Development Branch to get Green Building Standards included in the Ontario Building Code by summer 2023, building on the Toronto Green Standard in place since 2006.

title: Diversifying Civic Appointees on the Toronto Transit Commission Board - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: public appointments;
brief: Councillor Jamaal Myers asks City Council to direct the Civic Appointments Committee, as part of the current Toronto Transit Commission board selection process, to recommend candidates who meet criteria for diverse and representative membership. The motion argues the Public Appointments Policy requires Council to proactively seek boards that reflect the geographic distribution and diversity of the community they serve.

title: 125 The Esplanade (Temporary North Market) Extension of Temporary Use Zoning By-law - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: zoning;
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik asks City Council to direct the Chief Planner to start a City-initiated zoning amendment extending the temporary use by-law for 125 The Esplanade, the temporary home of the St. Lawrence North Market, for another six months. The current extension expires in October 2023; the by-law was first passed in 2014 and extended in 2017 and 2020, and construction of the new North Market is now expected to finish between late 2023 and early 2024 after pandemic delays.

title: Lease Amendment Agreement for 3 Eireann Quay - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: agreements; tenancy agreements
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik recommends City Council authorize a lease amendment with the Canada Ireland Foundation, the tenant of the City-owned building at 3 Eireann Quay, changing the City's contribution for state-of-good-repair and accessibility upgrades. The building is being developed as a cultural and community hub under the Bathurst Quay Neighbourhood Plan.

title: Redirecting the Proceeds of the Sale of a Residual Portion of City-owned land at 276 Lauder Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: sale (action); selling; vending
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks City Council to redirect the proceeds from selling a residual piece of City-owned land behind 276 Lauder Avenue. The current owner unknowingly built a double-car garage on the municipal parcel in 1984 with the then-Borough of York's approval, and the error was only discovered when the property was listed for sale 38 years later. The motion would waive the policy requiring net proceeds from surplus City land sales to go to the designated land fund so the money can be redirected.

title: 3106 Dundas Street West - Liquor Licence Application - Doc's License 2052075 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor licence for Doc's at 3106 Dundas Street West is not in the public interest unless conditions are attached. The application covers indoor and outdoor areas, and residents have raised concerns about noise, litter, safety, and other disturbances near residential units. Council's position would ask the City Clerk to advise the AGCO Registrar that the licence should carry conditions addressing the community's concerns.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto District School Board for Hillcrest Community School Playground and Schoolyard Revitalization- by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Bravo
topics: playgrounds, schools; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow recommends City Council direct $280,000 in Section 37 funds, from the development at 1443, 1445 and 1451 Bathurst Street and 501 St. Clair Avenue, to the Toronto District School Board for a new playground, schoolyard and expanded turf at Hillcrest Community School. The funding raises the 2023 operating budget by $280,000 gross at no net cost to the City. The school's outdoor areas are heavily used by the school and the community, and there is no City playground nearby.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item CC5.6 regarding the Terms of Reference for the Housing Rights Advisory Committee for 2022-2026 City Council Term - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: advisory committees; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups
brief: Councillors Jamaal Myers and Josh Matlow ask City Council to re-open and amend the terms of reference for the Housing Rights Advisory Committee so that people with disabilities are explicitly included in its membership. The motion follows discussion with the Greater Toronto Area Disability Coalition, a cross-disability coalition of thirteen organizations; about 22 percent of Canadians live with disabilities, and disabled Torontonians face significant barriers to accessible, affordable housing.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to St. Clare’s Multifaith Housing Society for improvements to the landscaping at 138 Pears Avenue - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: affordable housing, funding; affordable homes; housing projects, financing
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council release $1,054.73 in Section 37 funds to the St. Clare's Multifaith Housing Society for landscaping improvements at 138 Pears Avenue. The affordable housing building is owned by the City and managed by St. Clare's, and some Section 37 money earmarked in 2012 for the building went unused. The funding would increase the 2023 Non-Program operating budget by $1,054.73 gross and $0 net, fully funded by community benefits from the development at 124 and 128 Pears Avenue.

title: A Request to Review City Partnership Programs - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: audits, reserve funds; auditors; auditors, reserves and reserve funds
brief: Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council ask the City Manager, with City divisions, agencies, and corporations, to report by the end of the first quarter of 2024 with an inventory of existing and recent sponsorship or advertising arrangements between the City and private parties. The motion cites the $46.5 billion in financial pressures over ten years reported to Council in March 2023, and says the City should look inward for savings before asking residents to pay more or accept less service. The review would examine the City's partnership programs.

title: Proclaiming November 17 as Gordon Lightfoot Day in the City of Toronto - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: public holidays; bank holidays; holidays; holidays (public)
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends City Council proclaim November 17 as Gordon Lightfoot Day in the City of Toronto. Lightfoot was a world-renowned Canadian singer-songwriter and guitarist whose hits included Sundown and If You Could Read My Mind, and who was inducted into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame in 1986 and made a Companion of the Order of Canada in 2003. The proclamation would honour the folk-rock legend who died May 1, 2023.

title: Expanding Opportunities for Recreational Sports in Toronto - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: recreational programs, sports programs; community programs; recreation programs; recreation registration
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation, with stakeholders, to explore immediate and long-term opportunities to expand Toronto's public sports facilities. Organized sports are vital for physical and mental health, and volleyball and soccer are among the most popular sports, yet the city has limited public spaces to play them year-round. The motion emphasizes beach volleyball courts and soccer fields in particular.

title: Indigenous Procurement Policy - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: First Nations; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak, recommends City Council direct the Chief Procurement Officer, with the Director of the Indigenous Affairs Office and the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture, to co-develop an Indigenous Procurement Strategy with Indigenous businesses and communities. Small and diverse businesses find it disproportionately hard to sell to the City, especially First Nations, Inuit, and Metis businesses, and Indigenous procurement is part of the City's Reconciliation Action Plan endorsed in April 2022. The strategy would improve Indigenous economic development.

title: Recognizing the Importance of Queer History and the Ongoing Two-Spirit, Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Queer (2SLGBTQ+) Community Presence at Hanlan’s Point Beach and Surrounding Area, Ward 10 - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgendered; gay community; glbt; homosexual; lgbt; queer; transexual; transgendered; two spirited
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends City Council recognize over eight decades of queer history and 2SLGBTQ+ community presence at Hanlan's Point Beach and the surrounding area, and the importance of placekeeping there. Queer people in Toronto have used the beach for eight continuous decades or longer, and the motion says this history must be actively preserved before it is lost. Council is also asked to direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation, with City Planning and others, to take steps honouring that presence.

title: 59 Merchants' Wharf - Liquor Licence Application - Simona - Licence 2087046 - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: applications, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, application process
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor licence for Simona at 59 Merchants' Wharf is not in the public interest unless conditions are attached. The application covers indoor and outdoor areas, and nearby residents have raised concerns about noise and disturbance from a licensed establishment. Council's position would ask the City Clerk to advise the AGCO Registrar that the licence should carry conditions addressing the community's concerns.

title: Launching Toronto For All Campaign 2.0 - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: discrimination, elections, racial discrimination; anti-racism; racism, polls (elections); voting
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik, recommends City Council direct staff to report to the Executive Committee by the end of the third quarter of 2023 on a plan to launch a second Toronto For All campaign. The educational initiative fights discrimination and racism through public awareness campaigns on topics like anti-Black racism, intimate partner violence, Islamophobia, and antisemitism, and past campaigns drew local and international attention. The motion cites rising reported hate crimes as the reason for a new iteration.

title: 1226 King Street West - Liquor Licence Application - Madre De Lobo Licence 1943235 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor licence for Madre De Lobo at 1226 King Street West is not in the public interest unless conditions are attached. The application is for an indoor area, and residents have raised concerns about noise, litter, safety, and other disturbances near residential units. Council's position would ask the City Clerk to advise the AGCO Registrar that the licence should carry conditions addressing the community's concerns.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Adult Exercise Equipment in Jean Sibelius Square Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: parks, physical activity; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, exercise; physical fitness
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik, recommends City Council amend the Parks, Forestry and Recreation 2023 capital budget and 2024-2032 capital plan to create a new Jean Sibelius Square Fitness Equipment sub-project. The heavily used local park has playground equipment for small children but no exercise equipment for teenagers or adults, and residents chose an adult-sized balance beam, step benches, a group fit structure, and an exercise bench at an on-site meeting. Available Section 37 funds from two developments would pay for the improvements.

title: 45 William Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, planning;
brief: Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the minor variance application for 45 William Street. The Committee of Adjustment refused the owner's variance to build a garden suite in the rear yard on March 9, 2023, the owner appealed to the appeal body on March 27, 2023, and City Planning staff opposed the application in a February 28, 2023 report. Council is asked to back the refusal at the appeal body.

title: Reducing Toronto Transit Commission Vehicle Delays for Streetcar and RapidTO Routes - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside, recommends City Council direct the General Manager of Transportation Services, with the TTC's Chief Executive Officer, to review opportunities to reduce TTC vehicle delays on streetcar and RapidTO routes. With growing traffic gridlock slowing buses and streetcars, the motion asks staff to look at introducing or extending left-turn prohibitions at appropriate intersections or alternative measures. The goal is to attract riders back to transit and reduce the number of vehicles on the road.

title: Supporting Primary Care Services in Growing Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Councillor Jaye Robinson, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends City Council direct the City Manager to review the loss of primary care providers and local medical services in high-growth neighbourhoods and report back to the appropriate standing committee in the first quarter of 2024 with strategies to protect them. Medical professionals warn primary care is disappearing across Toronto, especially in North Toronto where rising rents are pushing providers out, which can escalate health issues and strain hospital emergency departments.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Street Haven for a Healing Garden - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: gardens;
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council release $20,000 in Section 37 funds to Street Haven for a healing garden at its 144 Roxborough Avenue location. Street Haven provides emergency shelter, supportive housing, and addiction services for women, and is funded at only half the rate the City pays for shelter beds. The funding would increase the 2023 Non-Program operating budget by $20,000 gross and $0 net, fully funded by community benefits from the development at 826-834 Yonge Street and 2-8 Cumberland Street.

title: Preserving Our Industrial Heritage - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends City Council direct the Chief Planner to report on evaluating the Unilever Soap Factory at 21 Don Roadway, known as Lever Plant No. 2, under the criteria for municipal heritage designation. Cadillac Fairview's updated proposal for the East Harbour site, now under a Ministerial Zoning Order, would demolish the soap factory, a Toronto landmark since the 1890s that offers an opportunity for adaptive reuse. Preserving the building would keep a piece of the site's industrial heritage.

title: A Clean Energy Future for Toronto - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: energy, environmental programs; energy resources; energy use, environmental initiatives; green living
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends City Council oppose any new power generation proposal involving increased burning of fossil fuels, including natural gas, in Toronto. The province is moving to add natural gas-fired generation despite the emissions increase, which could mean more fossil fuel burning at the Portlands Energy Centre on the waterfront. The motion also asks Council to request the province invest instead in energy efficiency, demand management, and conservation programs.

title: Deeming Members of Council Ineligible for Jury Duty - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: elected officials; elected representatives
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends City Council ask the Premier and the Attorney General of Ontario to amend the Juries Act so City councillors are ineligible for jury duty while in office. Federal elected officials and members of Ontario's Executive Council are already ineligible, and councillors vote on police and court funding, help create community safety plans, and provide oversight on the Toronto Police Services Board, which the motion says makes jury service inappropriate. Councillors also serve on regional bodies.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 500 Sherbourne Street to Community Matters Toronto for Mural Art on Bell Utility Boxes in Toronto Centre - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: arts and culture;
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council release $19,200 in Section 37 funds to Community Matters Toronto for twelve Bell box murals in Toronto Centre, Ward 13. Since 2009, the Bell Boxes Murals Project has had local artists paint original works on Bell Canada utility boxes, replacing graffiti with art that reflects local culture and makes streets more inviting. The funding would increase the 2023 Non-Program operating budget by $19,200 gross and $0 net, fully funded by development contributions from 500 Sherbourne Street.

title: Initiating a Mayor's Roundtable to Develop a Response Plan to Reduce and End Homelessness - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: homelessness;
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, recommends City Council ask the incoming Mayor to strike a Mayor's Roundtable to End Homelessness, and ask the City Manager to engage expert representatives from the Toronto Alliance to End Homelessness and the Toronto Shelter Network. City data shows over 10,500 people experiencing homelessness, and the shelter system is strained, leaving people in parks or on the streets. The roundtable idea grew out of a January 27, 2023 meeting between the homelessness organizations and former Mayor John Tory.

title: Supporting Small Businesses: Calling on the Federal Government to Forgive a Portion of the Canada Emergency Business Account Loans - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: federal governments, loans;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council ask the Federal Government to give small businesses a multi-year, no-interest repayment plan for Canada Emergency Business Account loans, plus $20,000 in forgiveness for businesses that agree to the plan. The loans were a lifeline during the pandemic, but businesses must repay in full by December 2023 to get the $20,000 forgiveness, and a Broadview Danforth BIA survey of nearly 500 businesses found 97 percent say the deadline hurts their business and 74 percent will be pushed further into debt.

title: Pre-2008 Diesel Engine Vehicles
topics: city vehicles, motor vehicles; city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet, vehicles
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe recommends City Council ask the General Manager of Fleet Services, with other City divisions, to address the City's remaining pre-2008 diesel engine vehicles and equipment. These engines predate modern pollution standards and emit disproportionately high levels of health-harming pollutants, and the City still owns and operates more than 150 such vehicles and pieces of equipment. The recommendation asks staff to identify them all, minimize their use until decommissioned, and decommission them.

title: Cycling Network Plan: 2023 Cycling Infrastructure Installation - Second Quarter Updates and Missing Sidewalk Program - 2023 Local Road Sidewalk Installations
topics: cycling, sidewalk repairs, transportation; bicycling, roadside repair; sidewalk brick installation; sidewalk brick maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalk ramping; sidewalk replacement; sidewalks maintenance; walkway maintenance; walkway repair, transportation services
brief: This is an information item: the report asks City Council to receive correspondence dated February 17, 2023 from the Credit Valley - Toronto and Region - Central Lake Ontario Source Protection Region Program Manager. The letter gives notification of consultation under the Clean Water Act, 2006 on proposed amendments to the CTC Source Protection Plan and the Toronto and Region Source Protection Area Assessment Report, necessitated by technical work on two City infrastructure projects. The General Manager of Toronto Water recommends Council receive the correspondence.

title: High Park Movement Strategy - Final Report
topics: parks, parks and open space areas, traffic calming; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, green spaces; open spaces
brief: City Council is asked to authorize a nominal fee licence agreement with Jumblies Theatre, a registered charity, and Elder Dr. Duke Redbird to facilitate Indigenous cultural programming on a section of parkland at Toronto Island Park. The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends Council authorize the General Manager to negotiate and sign the agreement on the City's behalf. The agreement would support Indigenous cultural activities on the Island.

title: Options for Permitting Private Installation of Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure on Public Streets
topics: energy infrastructure, infrastructure; hydro property
brief: This is an information item: the report responds to Council's request for options to allow private installation of electric vehicle charging infrastructure on public streets. About five percent of Toronto residents rely on residential on-street parking permits, and without dedicated parking they also lack a place to charge an electric vehicle, a group the industry calls garage orphans. The Executive Director of Environment and Climate recommends City Council receive the report for information.

title: The Sustainable City of Toronto Fleets Plan (2023 Update and Status Report)
topics: city vehicles, green fleet; alternative fuel vehicles; green fleet vehicles; green vehicles; hybrid vehicles, city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet
brief: City Council is asked to authorize the installation of 4.0 centreline kilometres of new bikeways on Scarborough Golf Club Road from Ellesmere Road to Kingston Road in Ward 24, with cycle tracks, as part of the 2022-2024 near-term cycling network. The report also covers second-quarter updates to the 2023 cycling infrastructure installations and the Missing Sidewalk Program's 2023 local road sidewalk installations. The General Manager of Transportation Services recommends Council authorize the Road Safety Improvements Project on Scarborough Golf Club Road and amend Municipal Code Chapter 886.

title: Carbon Accountability: Institutionalizing Governance, a Carbon Budget and an Offset Credits Policy
topics: accountability, budgets, greenhouse effect; budgets and accounts, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: City Council is asked to adopt the Carbon Accountability framework that would institutionalize governance of the City's net-zero-by-2040 target through Chapter 669 of the Municipal Code on Climate Change Goals and Governance, plus an Offset Credits Policy. The framework is meant to increase transparency and accountability for reducing greenhouse gas emissions across the City government and the community, improving value for money and public engagement. The Executive Director of Environment and Climate recommends Council adopt the wording in Attachment A and the Offset Credits Policy.

title: TransformTO 2022 Annual Report: Laying the Foundation for Net Zero
topics: annual reports, climate change, greenhouse effect; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, climate protection, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: City Council is asked to approve the preferred travel network improvements for High Park, developed through the High Park Movement Strategy study launched in summer 2021. The study evaluated the weekend and holiday road closures in place since March 2020 and other mobility issues, focusing on existing paved areas. Its goal is to better serve park users and the surrounding community while improving safety, accessibility, and the park's natural environment. The General Managers of Parks and Transportation Services recommend Council approve the preferred strategy and advance detailed design and costing.

title: Authority to Enter into a Nominal Fee Licence Agreement with Jumblies Theatre and Elder Duke Redbird
topics: cultural facilities, licences, theatres (facilities); art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres, auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities, licenses; licensing
brief: City Council is asked to adopt the Sustainable City of Toronto Fleets Plan as the framework for transitioning the City's fleets to sustainable, resilient, net-zero operations by 2040. The plan covers more than 10,000 vehicles and equipment managed by Fleet Services, the TTC, Toronto Police Service, Toronto Fire Services, Toronto Paramedic Services, and Toronto Community Housing, and would supersede all previous fleet plans. Its objectives include a 45 percent emissions reduction. The General Manager of Fleet Services recommends Council adopt the plan in Attachment 1.

title: Proposed Amendments to the Credit Valley - Toronto and Region - Central Lake Ontario Source Protection Plan and the Toronto and Region Source Protection Area Assessment Report Necessitated by City Infrastructure Projects
topics: sewer and water infrastructure, water treatment; sewer and water services; water and sewer infrastructure; water management systems, water filtration; water purification
brief: City Council is asked to adopt the Corporate Policy on Submissions and Filings in Attachment 4 as part of the TransformTO 2022 Annual Report, Laying the Foundation for Net Zero. The report describes 2022 as a foundational year for the TransformTO Net Zero Strategy, ground-testing the 2021 modelling, building cross-corporate partnerships, and starting work on priority actions toward net zero. The Executive Director of Environment and Climate recommends Council adopt the corporate policy.

title: Sale of BAI Subway Telecom Infrastructure to Rogers Communications
brief: This is an administrative inquiry item: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks about the announced sale of BAI Canada, the company that owns the TTC's subway cellular and Wi-Fi networks, to Rogers Communications. The April 10 announcement was presented as the best path to expand the infrastructure and bring cellular service to all subway riders, an important step for TTC safety, but the councillor says a number of questions remain unanswered. As an administrative inquiry, the item asks questions of staff rather than proposing a decision, and no recommendation is attached.

title: Letter of Intent between the City and Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment regarding the 2026 World Cup
brief: This is an administrative inquiry item: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks about reports that the City's letter of intent with Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment for the 2026 World Cup includes conditions making the City responsible for cost overruns and requiring it to compensate MLSE for lost Toronto FC or Toronto Argonauts revenue. The inquiry notes Council approved engaging MLSE in 2022. As an administrative inquiry, the item asks questions of staff rather than proposing a decision, and no recommendation is attached.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with Grascan Construction Limited/Torbridge Construction Limited to Repair F.G. Gardiner Expressway Concrete Bents from Cherry Street to the Don Valley Parkway
brief: This is an information item: the City awarded an emergency non-competitive contract to Grascan Construction Limited and Torbridge Construction Limited to repair deteriorated concrete bents on the F.G. Gardiner Expressway from Cherry Street to the Don Valley Parkway. The contract is worth $3,678,065 excluding HST, or $3,742,799 net of HST recoveries. The work was issued urgently because the bents were significantly deteriorated and repairs were needed to keep the roadway safe. The Interim Chief Engineer and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend Council receive the report for information.

title: Customer Experience Division Annual Report - 2022
brief: This is an information item: the Executive Director of Customer Experience reports 2022 service trends for the Customer Experience Division, formerly 311 Toronto, and the City divisions it works with. City Council requested annual reporting on trending issues in September 2020 to keep members and residents informed about the services and operations. The Executive Director recommends the General Government Committee receive the report for information.

title: Request for Authority to Create a Centralized Login Platform
brief: City Council is asked to authorize the Chief Information Security Officer to create a centralized login platform for public-facing City websites, applications, and digital services. The single point of entry would replace the current multiple login platforms, strengthen cybersecurity, deliver services more efficiently, and improve the customer experience. The authorization covers collecting the necessary personal information and creating individual user digital profiles.

title: Facilities Management Services
brief: This is an information item: the report outlines the impacts of service hour changes at City Hall, Metro Hall, and the Civic Centres, as directed by City Council in March 2023. Council asked for a pause on any service reductions to review impacts on Toronto Community Housing's building requirements at Metro Hall, health and safety for staff and the public, and the effect of bundling work orders on wait times. The Deputy City Manager of Corporate Services recommends Council receive the report for information.

title: Nominal Licence Agreement with Conseil scolaire Viamonde for Non-exclusive use of Felstead Park
brief: City Council is asked to authorize a nominal licence agreement with Conseil scolaire Viamonde for non-exclusive use of about 135,650 square feet of City-owned land at 60 Felstead Avenue, known as Felstead Avenue Playground Park. The land would accommodate school activities for the board's planned secondary school at 24 Mountjoy Avenue, directly across from the park and scheduled to open in September 2023. The City would make capital improvements to the park to minimize traffic impacts. The Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management recommends Council authorize the agreement.

title: Portion of 205 Wilmington Avenue (Irving W. Chapley Park) - Licence Extension Agreement with Beth Emeth Bais Yehuda Synagogue
topics: agreements, leasing, parking facilities, research; leases, studies; surveys (research), tenancy agreements
brief: City Council is asked to authorize a licence extension agreement with Beth Emeth Bais Yehuda Synagogue for a portion of the City-owned lands at 205 Wilmington Avenue, part of Irving W. Chapley Park, for parking purposes. The agreement would amend the existing parking licence and extend its term by ten years. Parking on the licensed lands would continue to serve synagogue visitors, park visitors, and the surrounding community. The Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management recommends Council authorize the agreement.

title: Long-term Industrial Lease at 245 Bartley Drive for Toronto Transit Commission's Automatic Train Control Project and Signals Group
brief: City Council is asked to authorize the City to enter into a new ten-year offer to lease and subsequent lease agreement with 245 Bartley Incorporated for about 46,000 square feet of industrial space at 245 Bartley Drive. The space would house the TTC's Automatic Train Control project and Signals Group, as approved by the TTC Board on January 19, 2023 subject to City authorization. The Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management recommends Council authorize the lease.

title: Largest Property Tax Debtors with Tax Arrears Greater than $500,000 as at December 31, 2022
topics: property taxes; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: This is an information item: the report lists property tax accounts with outstanding balances of $500,000 or more as of December 31, 2022. There are 26 such properties, 23 owned by corporations and 3 by individuals, the same number as at December 31, 2021. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends City Council direct that Confidential Attachment 4, which names the debtors, remain confidential.

title: 800 Lansdowne Avenue, Suite 101 - Designation of a Portion of the Property Used by South Asian Women's Centre as a Municipal Capital Facility
brief: City Council is asked to pass a by-law designating about 1,880 square feet of space at 800 Lansdowne Avenue, Suite 101, used by the South Asian Women's Centre, as a Municipal Capital Facility. The City leases the space from Ridgevest Developments Limited and subleases it to the Centre, a non-profit support organization. The designation would exempt the space from municipal and education property taxes. The Controller recommends Council pass the by-law under Section 252 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006 and enter into the Municipal Capital Facility agreement.

title: 400 Rockcliffe Boulevard - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo
brief: City Council is asked not to authorize a pedestrian crossover on Rockcliffe Boulevard, about 90 metres south of Rockcliffe Court, fronting Rockcliffe Middle School. Transportation Services assessed the need for pedestrian crossing protection at 400 Rockcliffe Boulevard but found the warrant criteria were not met. Council approval is required because the TTC operates a transit service on Rockcliffe Boulevard. The Director recommends Council not authorize the installation.

title: 4174 Dundas Street West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: Dunpar Homes is appealing the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for a 15-storey residential building at 4174 Dundas Street West, with 117 units, 13,194 square metres of floor area, and a density of 6.4 times the lot area. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on December 23, 2021 after Council missed the Planning Act deadline; a hearing is scheduled for 14 days starting February 12, 2024. The Division recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the tribunal in opposition while continuing discussions.

title: 1736-1746 Weston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is an appeal report: the applicant is appealing the Zoning By-law Amendment application for 1736-1746 Weston Road, originally a 25-storey mixed-use building with 253 units and 472 square metres of non-residential space. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal on November 24, 2022 after Council missed the Planning Act deadline, and on February 8, 2023 resubmitted a 40-storey version with 446 residential units and 444 square metres of non-residential space. The Division recommends City Council direct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the tribunal in opposition to the application in its current form while continuing discussions.

title: Metrolinx Ontario Line - Temporary Lane Closures on the Don Valley Parkway and F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Temporary Delegation of Authority
topics: road closures; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: City Council is asked to amend Municipal Code Chapter 937 on temporary highway closures to delegate authority to the General Manager of Transportation Services for test pit investigation work for the Ontario Line's Don Valley Crossing. Metrolinx is building the Don Valley Crossing and Lower Don Bridge to carry the Ontario Line over the Don Valley Parkway, requiring multiple temporary lane closures on the DVP, the Gardiner Expressway, and the Don Roadway between 2023 and 2028. The General Manager recommends Council approve the delegation to keep the investigation work moving.

title: Transfer of 260 Adelaide Street West to Build Toronto Inc.
topics: development, properties (real estate); developing land; development (land); land development, property; real estate
brief: City Council is asked to authorize transferring the City-owned property at 260 Adelaide Street West to Build Toronto Inc., a CreateTO-managed corporation, or one of its affiliates. Council declared the property surplus in October 2019, and its redevelopment and sale would fund the redevelopment of 229 Richmond Street and Metro Hall. The Executive Director of Corporate Real Estate Management recommends Council authorize the Executive Director to enter into the transfer agreement.

title: Toronto Water 2022 Year End Capital Budget and 2023-2032 Capital Plan Adjustments
topics: capital budgets;
brief: City Council is asked to amend Toronto Water's 2022 capital budget and 2023-2032 capital plan to align project costs and cash flows with year-end expenditures and project progress, with zero dollar impact on either. The adjustments include reallocating $34.378 million in 2022 cash flows to accelerate and defer projects within the approved budgets, offset by matching cash flow changes. The General Manager of Toronto Water recommends Council authorize the reallocations.

title: Annual Report on City's Loan and Loan Guarantee Portfolios
topics: credit, loans, non-profit organizations; non profit; nonprofit; not-for-profit organizations, tax credit
brief: City Council is asked to approve renewing the City's lines of credit guarantees, including the $820,000 guarantee issued on behalf of Canadian Stage to its lender, for a new three-year period. The annual report on the City's loan and loan guarantee portfolios covers credit arrangements with non-profit cultural and community organizations, recreational and sports organizations, and the City's own agencies and corporations. Providing guarantees helps these groups access financing for services that benefit the community. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends the renewals.

title: Adjustments to Capital Budget, Carry Forward Funding and Future Year Commitments
topics: capital budgets;
brief: City Council is asked to approve an additional $360.6 million in carry-forward funding from unspent 2022 capital project funding, so previously approved tax- and rate-supported capital projects can continue in 2023 and beyond. The approved 2023 capital plan already included $1.322 billion in estimated carry-forward amounts; now that the 2022 fiscal year has closed, programs and agencies have finalized actual spending and their carry-forward requests. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends Council approve the adjustment detailed in the appendices.

title: 2023 Education Property Tax Levy and Clawback Rate By-Law
topics: education taxes, property taxes; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: City Council is asked to adopt the 2023 education property tax rates and the education tax levy for school purposes, as required by legislation. The City levies and collects education taxes on behalf of the Province of Ontario at rates set in Ontario Regulation 400/98, generating a total 2023 education levy of $2,140,137,916 on rateable properties. The report also continues the policy of capping allowable tax increases at 10 percent of the prior year's taxes for commercial, industrial, and multi-residential properties facing larger increases. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends adoption.

title: Toronto Hydro and City of Toronto Memorandum of Understanding for Toronto Hydro's Climate Advisory Services
topics: advisory committees, climate; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups
brief: This is an information item: the report presents the Memorandum of Understanding between the City and Toronto Hydro-Electric System Limited on coordinating Toronto Hydro's Climate Advisory Services with the City's TransformTO programs. The MOU covers joint communications and marketing to customers, aligned performance indicators, and an implementation plan with timelines and progress reporting, to ensure value for money around the Toronto Hydro dividend and climate action at scale. The Deputy City Managers recommend City Council receive the report for information.

title: Donation from Sleep Country Canada to City of Toronto
topics: donation; bequest; toy drive
brief: City Council is asked to accept an in-kind donation from Sleep Country Canada of 77 mattress sets with bedframes and posture boards, valued at $58,000, to support the Shelter, Support and Housing Administration's Rapid Rehousing Initiative. Because the estimated value exceeds the $50,000 threshold in the City's donation policy, Council approval is required. Councillor Shelley Carroll recommends Council authorize the Director of Strategic Partnerships to accept the donation.

title: The Good Roads Conference April 16-19, 2023
topics: conferences, roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), conference travel
brief: This is an information item: Councillor Paul Ainslie reports on attending the 129th annual Good Roads Association conference from April 16 to 19, 2023, as the City's appointee to the association's Board of Directors. The conference focused on transportation infrastructure developments, including new technologies and funding models. Councillor Ainslie recommends City Council receive the conference update for information.

title: Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors Meeting March 7-9, 2023
topics: [organizations in government], board members, meetings;
brief: This is an information item: Councillor Paul Ainslie reports on his attendance as one of Toronto's representatives at the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors meeting in Durham, Ontario, from March 7 to 9, 2023. The board focused on pre-budget priorities ahead of the 2023 federal budget, set out in FCM's A Better Life for All Canadians document, covering resilient, affordable, growing, and secure communities. Councillor Ainslie recommends City Council receive the report for information.

title: Transit Priority Measures to Support Scarborough SRT Bus Replacement
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: City Council is asked to authorize priority bus lanes to support the interim bus replacement for the Scarborough Rapid Transit line, which is being decommissioned in the fourth quarter of 2023 after exceeding its life expectancy. The TTC-approved plan will move the SRT's 35,000 daily customers on express buses running up to 70 per hour until the Scarborough Subway Extension opens in 2030. The lanes include northbound Kennedy Road from Eglinton Avenue East to Ellesmere Road, southbound Midland Avenue from Ellesmere Road to Lord Roberts Drive, and eastbound Ellesmere Road from Kennedy Road. The General Manager of Transportation Services recommends approval.

title: Port Lands Flood Protection - Update
topics: flooding; floods
brief: This is a project update: the report covers the next steps in completing the Port Lands Flood Protection project, with substantial completion expected by the end of 2024 and parks and public realm opening in 2025, possibly in phases. It also outlines the new City assets being created, their expected operating and maintenance costs, and issues for future reports and budget submissions. The Deputy City Manager of Infrastructure and Development Services recommends City Council approve, in principle, the updated funding strategy for the flood protection work.

title: Mirvish Village Business Improvement Area Minor Boundary Expansion
topics: business improvement areas, service boundaries; bia; business improvement associations, community council boundaries
brief: City Council is asked to expand the Mirvish Village Business Improvement Area boundary slightly to include the public right of way in front of the Bathurst Subway Station east entrance at 655 Markham Street. The General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends Council designate the expanded area under Municipal Code Chapter 19 and direct the Chief Technology Officer to prepare the designation by-law. The expansion lets the BIA cover the station frontage.

title: Junction Gardens and shoptheQueensway.com Business Improvement Areas - Name Changes
topics: business improvement areas, naming; bia; business improvement associations
brief: City Council is asked to approve renaming two Business Improvement Areas: the Junction Gardens BIA would become The Junction Business Improvement Area, and the shoptheQueensway.com BIA would become the Shop The Queensway Business Improvement Area. The Junction Gardens membership voted for the change at its November 20, 2019 annual general meeting, and the shoptheQueensway.com membership voted at its October 28, 2019 annual general meeting. The General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends Council approve both renamings.

title: Appointments to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
topics: appointments, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: City Council is asked to appoint directors to the Boards of Management of four Business Improvement Areas that fall within more than one Community Council boundary, for the new term of Council. The appointments follow the City's Public Appointments Policy, and Schedule A of Municipal Code Chapter 19 would be updated accordingly. The General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends Council make the appointments at pleasure of Council for a term expiring at the end of the Council term.

title: Business Improvement Areas - 2023 Operating Budgets - Report 3
topics: business improvement areas, operating budgets; bia; business improvement associations
brief: City Council is asked to approve the final group of 2023 Business Improvement Area operating budgets, as required by the City of Toronto Act, 2006. Council approval lets the City collect the BIA levy through a special tax on commercial and industrial properties in each BIA boundary. The budgets include the Bloor Annex at $341,193 with a $276,825 levy, and the Danforth Mosaic at $900,076 with a $365,883 levy. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends Council adopt and certify the 2023 budgets and levy requirements.

title: Employment Services Transformation: Recommendations on the City’s Role
topics: employment opportunities, social assistance; careers; employment; job applications; job boards; job openings; job opportunities; job postings; job vacancies; jobs; vacancies (jobs), financial assistance; income assistance; ontario works; ow; welfare
brief: This report recommends what role the City should play in the province's Employment Services Transformation, which is changing how employment services are delivered for Ontario Works and Ontario Disability Support Program recipients. The transformation is being implemented by the Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development. The General Manager of Toronto Employment and Social Services recommends City Council direct the City not to pursue the role of Employment Service System Manager for the Toronto service area, while taking actions to ensure the employment needs of social assistance recipients are met.

title: Follow Up Report on the UrbanHensTO Backyard Hens Pilot Program
topics: birds, livestock, pilot projects, prohibited animals; chickens; dead birds; ducks; geese (wild); gulls; pigeons; seagulls; starlings; turkeys, goats; horses; pigs, restricted animals
brief: This report recommends ending the UrbanHensTO backyard hens pilot program, which expires May 31, 2023. The pilot has had limited uptake and no significant issues since its 2018 introduction, but a city-wide program would carry considerable administration costs and there is an emerging concern about highly pathogenic avian influenza. The Executive Director of Municipal Licensing and Standards recommends Council amend the Animals chapter of the Municipal Code to remove the pilot provisions while protecting people who were lawfully keeping hens under the program.

title: Notification of Donation of Decommissioned Equipment to Province of Ontario for Humanitarian efforts in Türkiye
topics: community development, donation, fire and rescue services, international alliances; bequest; toy drive, city twinning; city-to-city relationships; friendship cities; partnership cities; sister city relationships; twin cities; twin city alliances, community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, fire fighting; fire services; fire suppression; firefighting; rescue; rescue operations; search and rescue
brief: This is an information item: the Fire Chief notifies City Council that Toronto Fire Services donated decommissioned heavy urban search and rescue equipment, including tents and heaters, to the Province of Ontario. The equipment was part of the province's February 13, 2023 emergency humanitarian effort in response to the earthquakes in Turkiye and Syria, and it had already been decommissioned as no longer suitable for Fire Services use. The Fire Chief recommends Council receive the report for information.

title: Tourist Area Exemptions for Holiday Shopping for Yorkdale Shopping Centre - Amendment to Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 510-5
topics: [rules in recreation and tourism], commercial properties, recreation & tourism (sc); office real estate; retail space
brief: The Economic and Community Development Committee recommends City Council amend the Tourist Area Exemptions chapter of the Municipal Code to let Yorkdale Shopping Centre open on holidays. Yorkdale has long sought to open on six of nine statutory holidays, putting it on equal footing with nine other Greater Toronto Area malls and recognizing its tourism role, with 4.5 million of its 18 million annual visitors coming as tourists. The City gained the authority to grant such exemptions under the City of Toronto Act, 2006. Council is asked to amend Chapter 510-5 under that authority.

title: Data on the Health of People Experiencing Homelessness
topics: [activities in community and life], community & life (sc), homelessness;
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll recommends City Council authorize the Deputy City Manager of Community and Social Services to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with Unity Health Toronto and Inner City Health Associates for a feasibility assessment of the Connecting Home Initiative. The initiative proposes a real-time, integrated platform using client data to better plan and deliver shelter and health services for people experiencing homelessness. The assessment would test the legal, privacy, and technical viability of developing the platform, building on pandemic-era collaboration between health and shelter systems.

title: Review of policies and procedures related to Warming Centres
topics: evaluation, warming centres; review; reviewing
brief: City Council is asked to consider a review of policies and procedures for Warming Centres, which are part of the Winter Services Plan for people experiencing homelessness. The report notes the City faces urgent funding gaps, including a $317 million shortfall for COVID-19 shelter response funding and a $97 million need for refugee claimant shelter, which threaten current service levels without federal, provincial, or new revenue support. The General Manager of Shelter, Support and Housing Administration recommends Council ask staff to create an inter-divisional working group to develop a long-term Warming Centre strategy.

title: New Partnership and Funding Agreements for Cultural Organizations
topics: agreements, arts and culture organizations, funding, partnerships; art councils; art organizations; arts councils; arts groups; cultural organizations, financing, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council is asked to create a new operating funding program, the Cultural Organization Operating Partnership, to replace the discontinued Major Cultural Organizations and Specialized Collections Museums grant programs. The City currently provides annual operating grants to eight organizations that were funded through those programs. The General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends Council authorize the new program in accordance with the City's Community Grants Policy and create the associated funding agreements.

title: 2023 Local Arts Service Organizations (LASOs) Grant Allocation and Renewal of Annual Contribution Agreements
topics: arts and culture, subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: City Council is asked to approve the 2023 grant allocation for the six Local Arts Service Organizations and renew their annual contribution agreements. The organizations are Arts Etobicoke, East End Arts, Lakeshore Arts, North York Arts, Scarborough Arts, and the UrbanArts Community Arts Council. These independent not-for-profit community arts organizations serve neighbourhoods across the city, with a focus on underserved communities and Neighbourhood Improvement Areas. The General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends Council authorize the annual agreements.

title: Review and Renewal of the Green Market Acceleration Program (GMAP)
topics: community benefits, green standards; green development standards; sustainable development standards; toronto green standards
brief: City Council is asked to continue the Green Market Acceleration Program until March 31, 2027, with changes set out in the report's attachments. The program supports Toronto's green sector by giving companies access to municipal infrastructure for applied research, proof-of-concept trials, and demonstrations of pre-market technologies. The review covers the program's 2018-2022 activities and finds it helps attract and retain businesses while supporting jobs and innovation. The General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends Council authorize the renewal.

title: Appointment of City of Toronto Poet Laureate
topics: arts and culture, poet laureates;
brief: City Council is asked to appoint Lillian Allen as the seventh City of Toronto Poet Laureate, for a term beginning May 10, 2023 until December 31, 2026, or until a successor is appointed. Allen is a professor of creative writing at OCAD University, a two-time JUNO Award winner, and a trailblazer in spoken word poetry. The Poet Laureate position, created in 2001, honours a Toronto poet of excellence whose work speaks to Torontonians, promotes the literary arts across the city, and includes creating a legacy project. The General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends the appointment.

title: Purchasing Policy for Adoption by the 2022-2026 Compliance Audit Committee
topics: [activities in finance], audits, compliance, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, auditors; auditors
brief: The City Clerk recommends the Compliance Audit Committee adopt the purchasing policy set out in Appendix A of the report. If the committee grants a compliance audit of a candidate's election finances for the 2022-2026 term under the Municipal Elections Act, 1996, it must appoint an auditor; the policy sets up a fair, transparent procurement process run by the City Clerk, who would negotiate and execute the auditor contract.

title: Compliance Audit Committee Role and Responsibilities
topics: [activities in finance], audits, compliance, elections; auditors; auditors, polls (elections); voting
brief: This is an information item: the Deputy Director of Legal Services will give the Compliance Audit Committee a presentation on the committee's role and responsibilities. No decision is attached.

title: Rules of Procedure for the 2022-2026 Compliance Audit Committee
topics: advisory committees, audits, compliance, council procedures; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, auditors; auditors, procedural bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Compliance Audit Committee will consider a procedure by-law to govern its meetings. Adopting the by-law would set the rules the committee follows for the 2022-2026 term.

title: Update on Alcohol in Parks Pilot - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: parks and open space areas; green spaces; open spaces
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends City Council direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to consult councillors on their interest in hosting a pilot program this summer for responsible personal alcohol consumption in parks, and to work with interested councillors to confirm an appropriate pilot. The motion notes alcohol in parks is currently illegal but largely unenforced, with no tickets issued in 2022, and that other Canadian cities are running similar pilots. The pilot would be developed with a public health and harm-reduction lens.

title: Getting the Gardiner Right: Moving Forward with a New Study on Better Options for the Gardiner East - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: construction, expressways; building, municipal highways
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends City Council ask the General Manager of Transportation Services to temporarily pause new contractual obligations for the Gardiner East of Jarvis. No construction on the Gardiner East of Cherry Street is scheduled until 2026, and staff revealed the current cost estimate excludes inflation and ongoing maintenance, implying hundreds of millions of dollars above the 2016 estimate. The pause would allow time for a comprehensive study of better options for connecting the DVP and the Gardiner.

title: Micro-mobility Couriers - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: power-assisted bicycles, transportation; e-bikes; electric bicycles; electric bikes; electric-assisted bikes; power assisted bicycles, transportation services
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends City Council request the City Solicitor, in consultation with Municipal Licensing and Standards, Transportation Services, and other divisions, to report back to the June 5, 2023 meeting. Motor-assisted micro-mobility couriers provide valuable delivery services, but a minority create safety hazards by ignoring traffic rules, riding on sidewalks, and travelling at high speeds, and enforcement is difficult because couriers and vehicles carry no clear identification.

title: Fine Equity: Balancing Toronto Transit Commission Fare Evasion and Parking Fines - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: fines, parking, transit fares;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends City Council express its support for the principle of fairness in fines for City services. The motion notes the TTC fare-evasion fine of $195, rising to $235 with fees and potentially over $400, against a $3.25 fare, while parking without paying costs $30. It asks Council to direct the City Manager to ask the TTC's Chief Executive Officer to consider immediate steps to reduce the fare-evasion fine.

title: Claim to Recover Damages - Toronto Police Service Data Centre
topics: damages, police facilities;
brief: City Council is asked to consider a claim to recover damages connected to the Toronto Police Service data centre, which sits in a City-owned building where the police service manages the data room and the City manages building operations. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential instructions in Confidential Attachment 1 and keep the attachment confidential at the City Solicitor's discretion. The details remain confidential because they concern legal proceedings.

title: 102 Berkeley Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Appeal - Request for Directions
topics: zoning;

The applicant appealed on January 24, 2022 after Council did not decide in time, a Case Management Conference was held June 6, 2022, a 10-day hearing is scheduled for May 31, 2023, and the applicant submitted a revised proposal on March 6, 2023. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release if adopted. The details are confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

topics: zoning;

The revised proposal has 414 units with a gross floor area of 32,901 square metres, including 68 replacement rental units, and a companion rental housing demolition application covers the 68 existing rental units. The applicant appealed after Council did not decide in time. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release; the details stay confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

title: 48, 50, 56, 58 and 60 Avondale Avenue, 17 and 19 Bales Avenue and 25, 35, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45, 51, 53 and 55 Glendora Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning;
