The applicant submitted revised applications on January 6 and October 31, 2022 adding more Glendora Avenue properties, and appealed after Council did not decide in time. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release. The details are confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

title: Sheppard Willowdale Secondary Plan - City-Initiated Official Plan Amendment 560 - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning;
brief: City Council is asked to give directions for the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing on Official Plan Amendment 560, the City-initiated Sheppard Willowdale Secondary Plan adopted in February 2022 to replace the Sheppard Avenue Commercial Area Secondary Plan. Four appellants appealed the amendment to the tribunal, which has scheduled a 10-day hearing starting July 24, 2023, with expert witness statements due May 23, 2023, making the item urgent. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release. The details are confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

title: 45 The Esplanade - Ontario Land Tribunal Appeal - Request for Directions
topics: zoning;
brief: City Council is asked to give directions for the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment applications for 45 The Esplanade. The proposal is for a 36- and 35-storey mixed-use development with 682 units, 8,042 square metres of hotel use, and 585 square metres of retail at grade. The applicant appealed on August 3, 2022 after Council did not decide in time, and a hearing event is scheduled for June 21, 2023. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release; the details stay confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

title: 221, 225, and 227 Sterling Road - Zoning By-law Amendment and Draft Plan of Subdivision Applications - Request for Direction Report
topics: zoning;
brief: City Council is asked to give directions for the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the zoning and subdivision applications for 221, 225, and 227 Sterling Road. The proposal is for three residential buildings of 20, 25, and 29 storeys with 892 units, plus a rental housing demolition application for 58 existing rental units, and the site was designated as having cultural heritage value in August 2022. The applicant appealed on May 30, 2022 after Council did not decide in time. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release; the details stay confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

title: Designation of the Historic Yonge Street Heritage Conservation District Under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act - Request for Directions
topics: zoning;
brief: City Council is asked to give directions for the ongoing Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of the Historic Yonge Street Heritage Conservation District Plan. Council designated the district and adopted its plan in March 2016, and the plan was appealed to the tribunal, where the next case management conference is set for July 24, 2023 and a merits hearing has not yet been scheduled. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release. The details are confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: at its April 28, 2023 meeting, the Nominating Panel - Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal considered the appointments to the tribunal and made recommendations to City Council. The City Clerk transmits the panel's decision letter, which recommends Council appoint the named candidate to serve as Chair of the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal for a term ending November 14, 2026, and until a successor is appointed. Council is asked to make the appointment.

title: 15, 19, 21 and 23 Toryork Drive - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning;

The application seeks four buildings with 97,000 square metres of gross floor area, 1,177 residential units, 870 square metres of non-residential space, an onsite park, and a privately owned public space. The applicant appealed on March 16, 2022 after Council did not decide in time, and a 15-day hearing is scheduled. The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release; the details stay confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

topics: zoning;

The City Solicitor recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations in Confidential Attachment 1 and authorize their public release if adopted. The details are confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

title: Ontario Land Tribunal Appeal of Official Plan Amendment 231 - 1235-1255 Lawrence Avenue West and 3-23 Benton Road - Request for Directions
topics: zoning;
brief: City Council is asked to give directions for the Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of Official Plan Amendment 231 as it applies to 1235-1255 Lawrence Avenue West and 3-23 Benton Road. Gagliano Properties and Benton Property Corp. appealed seeking a Mixed Use Areas designation. The City Solicitor needs further directions for an upcoming hearing and recommends Council adopt the confidential recommendations and authorize their release. The details stay confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

The details are confidential because they concern litigation strategy.

brief: The Chief Procurement Officer recommends the Bid Award Panel award a contract to Pine Valley Corporation for the construction and installation of a new wood boardwalk, site furnishings, and beach restoration for the Parks, Forestry and Recreation Division. title: 789-793 Don Mills Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is asked to state its intention to designate 789-793 Don Mills Road, known as Foresters House, under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The building was constructed in 1965-1967 as the corporate headquarters of the Independent Order of Foresters, a fraternal organization founded in Canada in the 1870s, and was part of the Olympia Square complex. Heritage Planning staff recommend the designation for the property's cultural heritage value.

title: 15 Elm Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council is asked to state its intention to designate 15 Elm Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The two-storey Georgian Revival house-form building, completed by 1868, is a rare surviving Confederation-era example on the south side of Elm Street between Yonge and Bay streets. Heritage Planning staff recommend the designation for the property's design, associative, and contextual value.

title: 1313 Queen Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is asked to state its intention to designate 1313 Queen Street West, the former Police Station Number 6, under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. Built in 1931-32 to designs from the City Architect's Office, the building sits on the southwest corner of Queen Street West and Cowan Avenue in Parkdale and is noted for its architectural merit. Heritage Planning staff recommend the designation for the property's cultural heritage value.

title: 4888 Dundas Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council is asked to state its intention to designate 4888 Dundas Street West, the Alexander MacPherson House, under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. The 1879 brick Italianate house in the former village of Islington served as the village post office from 1887 to 1906 and the telephone exchange from 1912 to 1925. Heritage Planning staff recommend the designation for the property's cultural heritage value.

title: Snow plow damage to sod along sidewalks and other landscape features within the road right of way
topics: damage, sidewalks, snow removal; snow melting; windrow clearing (snow)
brief: Councillor Holyday recommends that Etobicoke York Community Council ask the Director of Operations and Maintenance to report to its May 15, 2023 meeting on snow plow damage to sod and landscaping in the road right-of-way. Hundreds of 311 calls report damage that is worse than recent years in both number and severity. The report would cover the extent of damage, the repair plan, and the responsibilities of the City, the contractor and others.

title: Westbound Left Turn Signal at Sheppard Avenue West and Abraham Welsh Read
topics: road safety, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: Councillor Perruzza recommends that Etobicoke York Community Council ask the Director of Traffic Management to continue preparations for a westbound left-turn signal at Sheppard Avenue West and Abraham Welsh Road, operating during morning and afternoon rush periods by the third quarter of 2024. Residents report dangerous conditions and long waits turning left, with drivers rushing the turn and endangering pedestrians.

title: Safety Review of the Intersection of Torbarrie Road and Judy Sgro Avenue
topics: pedestrian infrastructure, road safety; pedestrian network
brief: Councillor Perruzza recommends that Etobicoke York Community Council ask the Director of Traffic Management to review pedestrian and traffic safety at Torbarrie Road and Judy Sgro Avenue and report back as soon as possible. Residents have raised safety concerns, and the review could recommend a crosswalk, greater limits on parked cars on Torbarrie Road, or other safety features.

title: Appointments to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
topics: business improvement areas, public appointments; bia; business improvement associations
brief: This is a procedural item: the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture recommends that Etobicoke York Community Council appoint nominees to the Boards of Management of four Business Improvement Areas within its boundaries for the new term of Council. The appointments are made at the pleasure of Community Council under the City's Public Appointments Policy.

title: Gulfstream Road - Parking Amendments
topics: on-street parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services recommends parking amendments on Gulfstream Road near Gulfstream Public School to give parents and guardians short-term parking for school drop-off and pick-up while prohibiting stopping opposite the school. The changes include a weekday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. stopping prohibition on the south side between Indrio Road and a point 85 metres west. Etobicoke York Community Council is asked to approve the amendments to improve safety and reduce congestion.

title: Thomas Fisher Drive, Edward Horton Crescent and Augustus Terrace - Heavy Truck Prohibition
topics: heavy truck prohibitions;
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services seeks approval to prohibit heavy trucks at all times on Thomas Fisher Drive between Norseman Street and Edward Horton Crescent, on all of Edward Horton Crescent, and on all of Augustus Terrace. The regulations aim to reduce heavy truck traffic infiltrating the residential neighbourhood bounded by Norseman Street and Islington Avenue.

title: Woodstream Drive - Parking Amendments and Heavy Truck Prohibition
topics: heavy truck prohibitions, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services recommends that Etobicoke York Community Council prohibit parking at all times on both sides of Woodstream Drive between Rexdale Boulevard and Humberwood Boulevard. The changes would keep a clear passage and improve visibility and safety for road and park users. Staff also seek approval for a heavy truck prohibition on the same stretch, in effect at all times.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - April 2023 (Delegated)
topics: accessible permit parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled)
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services seeks approval for the installation and removal of on-street accessible parking spaces for persons with disabilities at the locations listed in Attachment 1 of the March 16, 2023 report. Etobicoke York Community Council, acting under delegated authority, is asked to authorize the changes.

title: Richardson Avenue - Traffic Calming Poll Results
topics: polling, traffic calming;
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services reports that the traffic calming poll for Richardson Avenue between Beechborough Avenue and Lonborough Avenue did not reach the minimum 50-percent-plus-one response rate needed to proceed. Staff recommend that Etobicoke York Community Council not authorize speed humps on the street.

title: Renfield Street - Traffic Calming
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services reviewed the need for speed humps on Renfield Street between Lawrence Avenue West and Harding Avenue and found the Traffic Calming Policy warrant criteria were not satisfied. Staff recommend that Etobicoke York Community Council not authorize speed humps on the street.

title: John Best Avenue - Traffic Calming
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services reviewed the need for speed humps on John Best Avenue between Sam Frustaglio Drive and Jane Street and found the Traffic Calming Policy warrant criteria were not satisfied. Staff recommend that Etobicoke York Community Council not authorize speed humps on the street.

title: Hartismere Court - Stop Controls
topics: intersections, stop signs; all-way stop controls; technical warrants
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services recommends that Etobicoke York Community Council approve stop controls at two uncontrolled intersections. The controls would cover westbound traffic on Hartismere Court at Collingdale Road, and northbound traffic at Hartismere Court and Hartismere Court.

title: Assiniboine Road and Haynes Avenue - All-Way Stop Control
topics: stop signs; all-way stop controls; technical warrants
brief: This is a procedural item: Transportation Services recommends installing all-way stop control at the intersection of Assiniboine Road and Haynes Avenue, finding it would enhance safety for all road users. Etobicoke York Community Council is asked to authorize the all-way compulsory stop control.

title: Application for Four Variances each subject to Three Conditions Respecting One Third Party Electronic Ground Sign - 3985 Keele Street
topics: by-laws, electronic signs, minor variances, sign permits; billboard permits; permanent sign permits; sign variances; street banner permits; temporary sign permits, bylaws, changeable message signs; electronic billboard signs; electronic overhead message signs, variance
brief: Pattison Outdoor, authorized by the owner of 3985 Keele Street, seeks four variances, each subject to three conditions, to permit one third-party electronic ground sign with a single face showing electronic static copy. The sign would stand up to 7.65 metres high with a 6.10-metre-wide face directed southwest along Keele Street. The Chief Building Official recommends the Sign Variance Committee grant the variances.

title: Presentation - Overview on Area-Specific Prohibitions of Third-Party Signs
topics: signs; signage
brief: This is an information item: the Project Director of Business Transformation, Toronto Building, and the Legal Services solicitor will present an overview of area-specific prohibitions on third-party signs to the Sign Variance Committee. No decision is attached.

title: 2023 Schedule of Meetings for the Sign Variance Committee
brief: This is a procedural item: the Deputy Secretary of the Sign Variance Committee recommends the committee approve its 2023 meeting schedule. The proposed dates are March 31, May 5, June 23, September 8, October 6 and November 3, 2023, guided by Council's approved schedule and virtual meeting space availability.

title: Update on Metrolinx's Ontario Line Construction within the Toronto and East York District
topics: urban transit systems; local transit authorities; municipal transit authorities; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; transit agencies; transit operating agencies
brief: This is an information item: the report details the current status of the Ontario Line within the Toronto and East York district, including timelines, construction mitigation plans and community engagement milestones. The Ontario Line is a planned 15.6-kilometre subway with 15 stations running from Exhibition Place to the Ontario Science Centre, connecting to the Eglinton Crosstown LRT, Line 1, Line 2 and the GO network. The Executive Director, Transit Expansion recommends that the Subcommittee on Metrolinx's Ontario Line Construction receive the report for information and ask for semi-annual updates.

title: 86 Highland Avenue - Demolition of a Structure within the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District and Approval of a Replacement Structure
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning recommends that City Council approve the demolition of an 'Unrated' building at 86 Highland Avenue within the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District and approve the design of a replacement two-storey detached house under Section 42(1) of the Ontario Heritage Act. The district plan permits demolition of an unrated building where the replacement design meets the plan's guidelines for new buildings and the zoning by-laws.

title: 29-31 Prince Arthur Avenue - Alterations to Heritage Properties within the East Annex Heritage Conservation District
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning recommends that City Council approve alterations to the heritage property at 29-31 Prince Arthur Avenue under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act, for a new four-storey rear addition providing office space. The property in the East Annex Heritage Conservation District holds a three-storey semi-detached Bay-and-Gable house-form building built around 1889; the proposal retains most of the front of the existing building, with alterations following plans by Angela Tsementzis.

title: 17, 23 and 25 Lascelles Boulevard - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: dwellings, exemptions, townhouses; exceptions
brief: The City Planning Division reviews and recommends approval of the Part Lot Control Exemption application to create one block of six townhouses and another block of four townhouses, separated by a walkway, at 17, 23 and 25 Lascelles Boulevard. The part lot plan also defines 12 below-grade parking spaces and the associated common elements condominium under review, implementing the site-specific zoning by-law and site plan approval; the owner must register a Section 118 restriction under the Land Titles Act so no part of the lands can be conveyed or mortgaged without consent.

title: 975 Danforth Avenue -  Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: In April 2022 a zoning by-law amendment application was submitted to permit a 10-storey mixed-use building with ground-floor commercial uses and 57 dwelling units at 975 Danforth Avenue. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in November 2022 after Council missed the Planning Act decision timeline. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and City staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the current application while continuing discussions with the applicant to resolve outstanding issues.

title: 234-250 King Street East and 162 Princess Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Removal of Holding Symbol ("h") - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The application proposes removing the holding symbol ('h') from Zoning By-law 1151-2022 (OLT), which permits a 43-storey mixed-use building with residential and retail uses at 234-250 King Street East and 162 Princess Street. The holding symbol can only be lifted once the City receives an updated Functional Servicing Report, Stormwater Management Report and Hydrogeological Review to the satisfaction of the Chief Engineer. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council amend the by-law substantially in accordance with the draft amendment from January 31, 2023.

title: Establishing a Community Safety Zone on Greenwood Avenue
topics: community safety, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: Greenwood Avenue between Danforth Avenue and O'Connor Drive is a residential street near a school and park, carrying high traffic volumes from the Don Valley Parkway exit at Don Mills, and residents are concerned about speeding. The Toronto and East York Community Council recommends that City Council rescind the existing Community Safety Zone on Greenwood Avenue between Chatham Avenue and Springdale Boulevard and designate a new Community Safety Zone, in effect at all times on both sides of the street, covering the Danforth-to-O'Connor stretch.

title: 1235-1255 Bay Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Planning Division reviews and recommends approval of the application to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law to permit a 35-storey mixed-use building with 357 dwelling units and 90 square metres of ground-floor commercial space at 1255 Bay Street. The existing 10-storey commercial building at 1235 Bay Street would be retained.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Various Events - March 1, 2023 - August 31, 2023
topics: festivals and special events; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals
brief: The General Manager, Economic Development and Culture recommends that City Council grant exemptions from Municipal Code Chapter 636 (Public Squares) and former City of Toronto Chapter 237 (Nathan Phillips Square) for events proposed on Nathan Phillips Square from March 1 to August 31, 2023. The organizations include Celebrate Toronto, the St. Patrick's Parade, the Canadian Polish Congress, the Magellan Community Foundation, Jack.Org, City Cultural Events Production, the City of Toronto, Rugby Ontario, the Luminato Festival and the Nathan Phillips Square Farmers' Market Association.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 4B to Exclude the Development Located at 581 Bloor Street West
topics: on-street parking, permit parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Because the TTC operates transit service on Bloor Street West, City Council approval is required. Toronto and East York Community Council had asked staff to review realigning Permit Parking Area 4B to exclude the development at 581 Bloor Street West; staff found the realignment feasible and have no objection, though the address's residents and visitors would then be barred from the area's permit parking. The Director, Permits and Enforcement recommends that City Council approve the revised map of Area 4B in Municipal Code Chapter 925.

title: 820 Church Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City Planning Division reviews and recommends approval of the application to amend the Zoning By-law to permit a 38-storey commercial building containing a hotel at 820 Church Street. The building would be 124.6 metres tall including the mechanical penthouse.

title: 1 Bloor Street West (Yonge Street and Balmuto Street) - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction; building, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: Mizrahi Development Group (The One) Inc. is building an 86-storey residential tower on an eight-storey retail podium at 1 Bloor Street West, at the southwest corner of Yonge Street and Bloor Street West. Because the TTC operates transit service on Yonge Street and the request varies from City policy, City Council approval is required to extend the construction staging area, closing a five-metre-wide portion of the northbound curb lane and the east sidewalk on Balmuto Street to vehicle and pedestrian traffic.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - February 2023 (Non-Delegated)
topics: budgets, parking, transportation; budgets and accounts, transportation services
brief: This is a procedural item: because the TTC operates transit service on the subject streets, City Council approval is required for installing or removing on-street accessible parking spaces for persons with disabilities. Transportation Services requests approval for the locations in the report's Attachment 1, dated February 6, 2023.

title: 463 Vaughan Road - Non-Residential Demolition Application
topics: demolitions;
brief: This is a procedural item: the property at 463 Vaughan Road is in the former City of York, where demolition permits are decided by City Council under former York By-law 3102-95. Demolition permit application 22 240410 DEM 00 DM seeks to demolish the existing one-storey car dealership. Toronto Building recommends that City Council approve the demolition subject to conditions, including a beautification plan satisfactory to the Chief Planner and a beautification agreement before the permit is issued.

title: 95 Thorncliffe Park Drive - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 23 109197 PRS 00 IV
topics: property standards;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee (North York Panel) will hear the appeal of a property standards order issued February 1, 2023 for 95 Thorncliffe Park Drive (file 23 109197 PRS 00 IV). The committee can confirm, change, or cancel the order. The appeal is the owner's chance to challenge the city's repair or maintenance requirements.

title: 54 to 62 Glen Everest Road - Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: planning, zoning;
brief: In April 2021 a zoning by-law amendment application was submitted to redevelop 54 to 62 Glen Everest Road with a 12-storey residential building of 427 units, including 68 replacement rental units, demolishing the three existing low-rise rental buildings; a June 2022 revision increased the gross floor area to 32,901 square metres and reduced the unit count to 414. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in July 2022 after Council missed the Planning Act timeline. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and City staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the current application and continue discussions.

title: Traffic Control Signals - Morningside Avenue and Warnsworth Street
topics: intersections, traffic control systems, transportation; traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment, transportation services
brief: This is a procedural item: because the TTC operates transit service on Morningside Avenue, City Council approval is required. Transportation Services reviewed the need for traffic control signals at the intersection of Morningside Avenue and Warnsworth Street and found the warrant criteria were not met. The Director recommends that City Council not authorize the signals.

title: 4097 Lawrence Avenue East and 197 to 201 Galloway Road - Application to Lift Holding Provision Application - Final Report
topics: government symbols, planning approvals; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals
brief: The application proposes lifting the holding (H) symbol on the lands at 4097 Lawrence Avenue East and 197 to 201 Galloway Road, which would allow a 12-storey (37.8 metre) residential building with 228 dwelling units, including 15 townhouse units at the base, 230 vehicle parking spaces in a three-level underground garage and 175 bicycle parking spaces. The holding provision was added through site-specific Zoning By-law 251-2022 to ensure outstanding sanitary servicing matters were resolved. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 to remove the holding symbol.

title: Traffic Control Signals - Bellamy Road North and Banmoor Boulevard/Cedar Brae Boulevard
topics: traffic control systems, traffic signals, transportation; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment, transportation services
brief: This is a procedural item: because the TTC operates transit service on Bellamy Road North, City Council approval is required. Transportation Services reviewed the need for traffic control signals at the intersection of Bellamy Road North and Banmoor Boulevard/Cedar Brae Boulevard and found the warrant criteria were not met. The Director recommends that Scarborough Community Council not authorize the signals.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will review the Order Paper. No decision is attached.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations and announcements will be made at the City Council meeting. No decision is attached.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council may file petitions. No decision is attached.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of Council will declare interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. No decision is attached.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: committee reports and new business from City officials are introduced. The reports include the Executive Committee report from March 21, 2023, the Audit Committee report from February 13, 2023, the Civic Appointments Committee report from March 6, 2023, the Economic and Community Development Committee report from February 16, 2023, the General Government Committee report from March 3, 2023, and the Infrastructure and Environment Committee report from March 20, 2023.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from the regular meeting held February 7 and 8, 2023 and the special meeting held February 15, 2023. No decision beyond confirmation is attached.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting opens with a call to order, O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is attached.

title: Ensuring a Successful Tenant Advisory Committee at Toronto Community Housing Corporation
topics: advisory committees, tenant organizations, tenants; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: On December 14, 2022 City Council adopted Member Motion 2.16 on ensuring a successful Tenant Advisory Committee at Toronto Community Housing Corporation, directing staff through the Tenants First initiative to review the proposal covering terms of reference, member recruitment and confirmation, the role of tenant directors, and the City's role, and to report back to the February 2023 Planning and Housing Committee. The Executive Director, Housing Secretariat recommends that City Council direct the TCHC Board of Directors to ensure the Tenant Advisory Committee's terms of reference are developed in collaboration with the committee and the City.

title: Zoning By-law Amendment to Permit Laneway Suites in Yorkville - Final Report
topics: laneways, rezoning; back alleys; mews, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: In 2019, after a city-wide laneway suite study, Council amended the Official Plan and Zoning By-law 569-2013 to permit laneway suites in low-rise residential zones, but directed that the Asquith-Collier, Ramsden Park and Yorkville neighbourhoods be excluded, with staff to consider permitting them there through the review of Site and Area Specific Policy 211 (Bloor-Yorkville/North Midtown). The Chief Planner and Executive Director now recommends that City Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 to permit laneway suites in Yorkville, per the draft amendment attached to the report.

title: 835 and 839 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner and Executive Director recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the listed property at 835 and 839 Yonge Street (including entrance address 837 Yonge Street) under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property, commonly known as the Canadian Tire Store at the northeast corner of Yonge/Church Streets and Davenport Road across from the Masonic Temple, includes portions of the Grand Central Market, a two-storey commercial market building.

title: 51 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner and Executive Director recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 51 Yonge Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The four-storey commercial building on the east side of Yonge Street, north of Wellington Street East, was built around 1878-1879 (though the structure may date to 1847) in the Second Empire style and has historical and architectural links to the Bank of British North America building at 49 Yonge Street.

title: 401 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner and Executive Director recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 401 Yonge Street (including entrance addresses 403 and 405A Yonge Street) under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The mid-block property north of Yonge and Gerrard Streets holds a three-storey building constructed in 1873 for grocer and merchant Joseph Bickerstaff, a rare surviving early example of a commercial building in Toronto.

title: 3377 Bayview Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner and Executive Director recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 3377 Bayview Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. The property is the Tyndale University campus, formerly the Sisters of St. Joseph Motherhouse campus, an interconnected complex designed in 1959-1960 by Marani, Morris & Allan reflecting Neoclassical and Modernist principles, set on table lands overlooking a ravine alongside German Mills Creek, a Don River tributary.

title: 191, 193, 195, 199 College Street and 74 and 76 Henry Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner and Executive Director recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the properties at 191, 193, 195 and 199 College Street (including entrance address 197 College Street) and 74 and 76 Henry Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for their cultural heritage value. The properties on the southwest corner of College and Henry Streets are surviving late 19th-century semi-detached house-form buildings with Victorian-period detailing that maintain the historical character of College Street.

title: 239-249 Gerrard Street East (including the entrance addresses of 251 and 253 Gerrard Street East), 509 Parliament Street, 1871 and 1885 Weston Road - Inclusion of Nine Properties in Toronto and East York and Etobicoke York on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: The Chief Planner and Executive Director recommends that City Council include nine properties on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register for their cultural heritage value and interest. The nine properties are 239, 241, 243, 245, 247 and 249 Gerrard Street East (including entrance addresses 251 and 253 Gerrard Street East) and 509 Parliament Street in Toronto-Centre (Ward 13), and 1871 and 1885 Weston Road in York South-Weston (Ward 5).

title: Implementing Bill 23 - Amendments to the Heritage Act and Proposed Amendments to the Municipal Code: Chapter 103 - Heritage
topics: change, heritage conservation districts; amendments; conversion; modification, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: This report updates Council on provincial Bill 23, the More Homes Built Faster Act, 2022, which received royal assent on November 28, 2022 and extensively changed several statutes including the Ontario Heritage Act; the Heritage Act amendments took force January 1, 2023, except for the requirement that a Heritage Register be posted on a municipality's website. The Chief Planner and Executive Director proposes Phase One administrative changes to Municipal Code Chapter 103, Heritage, and recommends that City Council amend the chapter accordingly.

title: City Solicitor Opinion - Bill 23, More Homes Built Faster Act, 2022 and Section 111 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006
topics: [activities in property], [rules in planning and development], municipal officials; city officials
brief: In November 2022 City Council adopted item CC1.2 on Bill 23, the More Homes Built Faster Act, 2022, requesting a report to the Planning and Housing Committee with legal advice on a strategy for potential changes to Section 111 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006, and on alternate ways to protect rental units from demolition and conversion. The City Solicitor, with the Chief Planner, prepared this report in response. The City Solicitor recommends that City Council keep the advice in Confidential Attachment 1 confidential under solicitor-client privilege and request further work from the City Solicitor and Chief Planner.

title: Bill 109 Implementation, Phase 1 - Recommended Official Plan and Municipal Code Amendments
topics: official plan amendments, site plan control; site plan approvals
brief: The recommended Official Plan Amendment 641 and municipal by-law bring the City's Official Plan and Municipal Code into conformity with provincial Bill 109, the More Homes for Everyone Act, 2022. Under the legislation, changes to pre-application consultation, complete application requirements, delegated authority and appeal timelines for Site Plan Control applications took effect July 1, 2022. The Chief Planner and Executive Director recommends that City Council adopt Official Plan Amendment 641 and amend Municipal Code Chapter 415, Development of Land.

title: 6167 Yonge Street, 10 Newton Drive, 9 Madawaska Avenue and City-owned Public Lane - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, applications, laneways, mixed use areas, official plan amendments, permits, planning tribunals; application process, back alleys; mews, omb; ontario municipal board, permit renewal
brief: On February 11, 2022 an application was submitted to amend the Official Plan and zoning by-laws to permit two 14-storey (47.8 to 48.36 metres) mixed-use buildings at 6167 Yonge Street, 10 Newton Drive, 9 Madawaska Avenue and the City-owned public lane, with 549 residential units, 998 square metres of at-grade retail, a gross floor area of 38,810 square metres and density of 5.98 times the lot area. The Director, Community Planning, North York District recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the application (File 22 108032 NNY 18 OZ).

title: 943 - 963 Eglinton Avenue East and 23 Brentcliffe Road - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Plan of Subdivision Applications - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: In November 2021 applications were submitted to permit four new mixed-use residential buildings with 1,279 units, ranging from 16 to 28 storeys (57.5 to 93 metres), with a total gross floor area of 103,743 square metres at 943-963 Eglinton Avenue East and 23 Brentcliffe Road. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in September 2022 after Council missed the Planning Act timeline. The Director, Community Planning, North York District recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and City staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the current Official Plan, zoning and subdivision appeals.

title: 1466 and 1500 Bayview Ave - Zoning By-law Amendment and Site Plan Control Applications - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, applications, planning & development (sc), planning tribunals, site plan control, zoning bylaws; application process, omb; ontario municipal board, site plan approvals, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: In October 2020 applications were submitted for a 9-storey (26.35 metres) mixed-use building with 156 residential units and 1,659.5 square metres of at-grade retail at 1466 and 1500 Bayview Avenue; the applicant later revised it to an 8-storey building with 153 units and 1,545.6 square metres of retail. The Director, Community Planning, North York District recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and City staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the current zoning by-law amendment and site plan control appeals, while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: Federal Electoral Districts Redistribution affecting North York
topics: municipal elections, wards;
brief: Toronto is one of North America's fastest-growing cities, yet the latest Federal Electoral Districts Redistribution removes one riding, Don Valley East, which would mean less representation for Toronto residents. Councillor Lily Cheng, who represents Ward 18 Willowdale in North York, recommends that City Council strongly express its objection to the boundary changes that could eventually reduce Toronto City Council by one seat.

title: 37 Rochester Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Appeal and Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body
topics: appeals, applications, hearings, planning tribunals; application process, omb; ontario municipal board
brief: On December 7, 2022 the North York Panel of the Committee of Adjustment denied the owner of 37 Rochester Avenue ten minor variances, including building length, building depth and floor space index, to build a new detached dwelling; Community Planning staff had recommended refusing two of the variances. Councillor Jaye Robinson recommends that City Council instruct the City Solicitor and City staff to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing to oppose application A0489/22NY and authorize the City Solicitor to negotiate a settlement of the appeal.

title: 2 - 20 Glazebrook Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: planning approvals, planning tribunals, services; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, omb; ontario municipal board
brief: In July 2022 a zoning by-law amendment application was submitted to permit a 34-storey (109.9 metres) mixed-use building with 434 dwelling units and a total gross floor area of 29,600 square metres at 2-20 Glazebrook Avenue. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in December 2022 after Council missed the Planning Act decision timeline. The Director, Community Planning, North York District recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and City staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the current application while continuing discussions with the applicant.

title: Traffic Control Signals at Wilson Avenue and Champlain Boulevard
topics: approval, infrastructure, mixed use areas, planning & development (sc), traffic management, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: A new development is under construction on the north side of Wilson Avenue east of Wilson Heights Boulevard (470-530 Wilson Avenue), replacing 110 rental units with 161 rental units, 394 condo units, 387 parking spaces, and office and retail space at grade. Councillor James Pasternak recommends that City Council authorize a signalized traffic control at the intersection of Wilson Avenue and Champlain Boulevard to handle the future pedestrian and vehicle traffic, with the developer paying for and installing the signal so there is no financial impact on the City.

title: 1141 Roselawn Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning Amendment Application - Request for Direction Report
topics: applications, hearings, official plan amendments, planning tribunals, residential properties, zoning bylaws; application process, omb; ontario municipal board, residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: In December 2021 an Official Plan and zoning by-law amendment application was submitted to permit an 11-storey residential building with 133 units, 9,689 square metres of residential floor area, 94 vehicle parking spaces and 163 bicycle parking spaces at 1141 Roselawn Avenue. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in July 2022 after Council missed the 120-day Planning Act timeline. The Director, Community Planning, North York District recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and City staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the current application while continuing discussions.

title: 699 - 711 Lawrence Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, applications, hearings, planning tribunals, zoning bylaws; application process, omb; ontario municipal board, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: In February 2022 a zoning by-law amendment application was submitted to permit a 40-storey (131.6 metres) residential building with 360 dwelling units and 162.8 square metres of ground-floor retail at 699-711 Lawrence Avenue West. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal in July 2022 after Council missed the 90-day Planning Act timeline; the first case management conference was scheduled for February 9, 2023. The Director, Community Planning, North York District recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and City staff to attend the Tribunal in opposition to the current application while continuing discussions.

title: Supporting Locally-Based Community Health and Well-Being Projects: The Rhema Foundation Canada's Mobile Community Learning Kitchen - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: community outreach; awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach
brief: The Rhema Foundation Canada has served York Centre and Greater Toronto Area residents for many years, and its Mobile Community Learning Kitchen project would bring people across socio-economic and cultural backgrounds together for food skills training, food and nutrition literacy and community health, addressing Toronto's urgent food scarcity challenge. Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, recommends that City Council direct the Executive Director, Social Development, Finance and Administration to explore funding opportunities for the mobile kitchen and report to the Economic and Community Development Committee.

title: Authority to Amend the 2023 City Council Approved Operating Budget for Parks, Forestry and Recreation for Morse Street Playground Water Service - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: ice rinks, playgrounds, water; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, airs (rinks); civic centre ice rinks; hockey rinks; ice pads; ice surfaces; natural ice rinks; nirs; rinks; skating rinks
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends that City Council amend the 2023 approved operating budget for Parks, Forestry and Recreation by $8,000 gross ($0 net) to install water service in Morse Street Playground, enabling a natural ice rink over the winter seasons. The work is fully funded by Section 42 cash-in-lieu funds above five percent generated by the development at 462 Eastern Avenue, which have been received and are eligible for this purpose.

title: Micro-mobility Couriers - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: power-assisted bicycles, transportation; e-bikes; electric bicycles; electric bikes; electric-assisted bikes; power assisted bicycles, transportation services
brief: Couriers on motor-assisted micro-mobility vehicles, including electric-assist bicycles, provide valuable delivery services without air pollution or congestion, but a minority create safety hazards for pedestrians and vulnerable road users by ignoring traffic rules, speeding and riding on sidewalks. Enforcement has been ineffective partly because neither the couriers nor their vehicles carry clear identification. Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends that City Council ask the City Solicitor, with Municipal Licensing and Standards, Transportation Services and other divisions, to report back to the June 5, 2023 meeting on options.

title: Fine Equity: Balancing Toronto Transit Commission Fare Evasion and Parking Fines - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: fines, parking, transit fares;
brief: The fine for Toronto Transit Commission fare evasion is $195 ($235 with other fees, rising above $400) for a $3.25 loss, while parking in a pay-and-display space without paying or exceeding the time limit carries a $30 fine. Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends that City Council support the principle of fairness in fines for City services and direct the City Manager to ask the TTC Chief Executive Officer to consider immediate steps to reduce the fare evasion ticket amount.

title: High Hope Cider - Limited Liquor Sales Licence - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, moves to support High Hope Cider's application for a manufacturer's limited liquor sales licence for sales by the glass at 130 Ossington Avenue (rear). A municipal council resolution is required before the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario can process the application. City Council is asked to advise the AGCO of its support.

title: Support for the City of Montreal's Motion regarding a High-speed Train in the Quebec-Toronto Corridor - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: trains;
brief: On February 27, 2023 Oshawa City Council adopted a motion supporting Montreal's February 20, 2023 motion for a high-speed train in the Quebec-Toronto corridor rather than the high-frequency train the federal government is pursuing, which would only slightly cut travel times and be less attractive to the public. Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that City Council express its support for Montreal's motion for a high-speed train program and join Oshawa in endorsing it.

title: 55 - 65 Broadway Avenue - Off-site Parkland Conveyance - Amendment to Item 2017.CC34. 7 by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, moves to amend Council's 2017 decision on the 55-65 Broadway Avenue zoning appeal settlement by deleting Part 3 of the confidential instructions to staff. Those instructions had approved a 530 square metre off-site park at 70 to 76 Soudan Avenue, to be conveyed to the City free of encumbrances. City Council is asked to adopt the amendment.

title: Approval to demolish and rebuild 5 Whitehall Road - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: demolitions;
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, moves to approve demolishing and rebuilding the unrated heritage property at 5 Whitehall Road in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District. The Toronto Preservation Board already recommended approval, and the motion seeks urgency so construction can start before frost rather than waiting six weeks for the normal committee cycle. City Council is asked to approve the demolition and replacement.

title: Supporting Employers in the Tapscott Employment Area (Middlefield Road) - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: employment areas, land; employment districts; employment zones, property
brief: Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, moves to support employers in the Tapscott Employment Area after Surati Sweet Mart, a Ward 23 food manufacturer providing low-barrier jobs, faced repeated noise and odour complaints despite always being found in compliance. Ongoing complaints to the Ministry of the Environment trigger costly investigations and threaten a planned third shift. City Council is asked to classify lands around McCowan Road, Placentia Boulevard, Middlefield Road and Finch Avenue East as a Class 4 Noise Area.

title: Update on Alcohol in Parks Pilot - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: parks and open space areas; green spaces; open spaces
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, moves to launch an opt-in pilot this summer allowing responsible personal alcohol consumption in select parks. Noting that alcohol in parks is currently illegal but largely unenforced, with no tickets issued in 2022, the motion asks Council to direct the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to consult Councillors on hosting a pilot in their wards, following other Canadian cities' best practices.

title: Protecting Access to Healthcare for all Ontarians - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: accessibility, health (sc); barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, moves to ask the Province to reverse its decision to end the Physician and Hospital Services for Uninsured Persons Program on March 31, 2023. The motion argues ending the program removes care from over a million Ontarians, many of them the most vulnerable. City Council is asked to request the Government of Ontario reverse the decision.

title: Provincial/Municipal Bill 23 Audit - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: audits, charges, development; auditors; auditors, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, moves to adopt the Terms of Reference for a third-party audit of costs the City bears from Bill 23's changes to development charges. In November 2022 the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing promised to compensate Toronto for lost revenues, and the audit's terms were developed jointly by provincial and municipal staff. City Council is asked to adopt the Terms of Reference and direct the Chief Financial Officer to provide needed information.

title: Authorization to Approve a Development Charge Credit for the Design and Construction of the Future Park at 55 Lake Shore Boulevard East - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: construction, development charges, parks; building, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, moves to approve a development charge credit against the Parks and Recreation component of development charges for the owner's design and construction of Above Base Park Improvements to a new one-hectare park at 53, 55 and 95 Lake Shore Boulevard East. The park was secured through a tri-party parkland agreement after Council approved the area's planning applications in 2018.

title: Accepting an in-kind donation to convert the outdoor basketball courts into fully accessible courts at Confederation Park Ward 24 - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: basketball, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, moves to accept an in-kind donation of up to $500,000 from Canadian Tire Jumpstart Charities to upgrade the basketball courts at Confederation Park, 250 Dolly Varden Boulevard in Ward 24. The donation would fund accessibility improvements and enhancements including new posts and backboards, lighting, fencing, accessible seating, a shade structure and sport court surfacing. City Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept the donation.

title: Workplace Health and Safety in the Ward 13 Office - by 	Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: health (sc), safety; public safety
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, moves to address crowding in the Ward 13 City Hall office, where 10 staff plus the Councillor work in space that does not allow a safe and healthy working environment. City staff recommended bringing the matter to Council. City Council is asked to approve assigning Suite A7 to the Ward 13 Councillor at the same fee charged for civic centre offices.

title: Authority to Amend the 2023-2032 Council Approved Capital Budget and Plan for Parks, Forestry and Recreation for Topham Park Clubhouse Improvements - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: budgets, parks; budgets and accounts, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, moves to add $1,477,000 to the Parks, Forestry and Recreation capital budget for Topham Park Clubhouse improvements, raising the project total from $306,000 to $1,783,000 so a construction contract can be awarded. The increase would be funded by $1,037,173 from the South District Parkland Development Reserve Fund and $439,827 from Section 42 cash-in-lieu from nearby developments, with cash flow split between 2023 and 2024.

title: Securing a Long-Term Future for Seniors at the Beech Hall Housing Co-operative - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
brief: The Beech Hall Housing Co-operative in Mount Dennis has for over forty years operated 127 affordable non-profit rental homes for seniors in sixteen City-owned low-rise buildings; the intentional community was built in 1950 by the Borough of York Housing Company, and the co-op entered a 45-year lease with the former Borough of York Housing Company on January 4, 1980. Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends that City Council ask the Housing Secretariat, with Corporate Real Estate Management and CreateTO, to bring a policy framework to the April 27, 2023 Planning and Housing Committee to secure the co-op's long-term future.

title: 1311 St. Clair Avenue West - Liquor Licence Application - Tre Mari Bakery (Licence 2086931) - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, moves to tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor licence for Tre Mari Bakery at 1311 St. Clair Avenue West is not in the public interest unless conditions are attached. The indoor premises sits close to homes, with community concerns about noise, litter, safety and other disturbances. City Council is asked to direct the City Clerk to advise the AGCO Registrar accordingly.

title: Request to Accept an In-kind Donation for Upgrades to Outdoor Basketball Court in Joel Weeks Park - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: basketball, donation, parks; bequest; toy drive, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, moves to accept an in-kind donation of up to $125,000 from Buckets and Borders Incorporated to upgrade the Don Mount basketball court in Joel Weeks Park. The charitable non-profit's inaugural Toronto project is funded in partnership with NBA Canada and the WNBA. City Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to accept the donation.

title: Donation of Vehicles to Support the Ukrainian Government's Humanitarian Effort - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: donation, motor vehicles; bequest; toy drive, vehicles
brief: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, moves to donate three end-of-life City vehicles to the Ukrainian government for humanitarian purposes, more than a year after Russia's invasion. The vehicles are a 2012 Ford Escape Hybrid and a 2001 Ford Ranger from Fleet Services, plus a 2014 Chevrolet Tahoe from Paramedic Services equipped with lights, sirens and first aid supplies. City Council is asked to authorize the General Manager of Fleet Services to donate them at no cost.

title: 1733 Bloor St. West - Liquor Licence Application - WingsUp! (License 2010028) - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, moves to tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor licence for WingsUp! at 1733 Bloor Street West is not in the public interest unless conditions are attached. The application covers indoor and outdoor areas near homes, with community concerns about noise, litter, safety and other disturbances. City Council is asked to direct the City Clerk to advise the AGCO Registrar accordingly.

title: Advancing grant funding at Paul Martel Park - Authority for staff to amend existing license agreement with Aki Wiidookaagewin (Earth Helpers) and The Neighbourhood Group - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: agreements, licences, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, licenses; licensing, tenancy agreements
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, moves to authorize the General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation to amend the existing agreement with The Neighbourhood Group Community Services and Aki Wiidookaagewin - Earth Helpers for Paul Martel Park. The amendment would let the General Manager extend the arrangement to advance grant funding for the small native-plant park in the Bloor-Spadina neighbourhood.

title: Completion of City-owned site at 5200 Yonge Street to allow for successful launch of City-initiated Food Incubator Program - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: food, rent; menus, rents
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, moves to give the entrepreneurs in the City-initiated Food Incubator Program at 5200 Yonge Street a rent break while a not-for-profit operator is selected. The motion asks Council to authorize a 75 percent rent abatement from January 1 to March 30, 2023 and a 50 percent abatement after that. The pandemic-era incubator supports entrepreneurs from equity-seeking groups building food businesses.

title: Getting the Gardiner Right: Moving Forward with a New Study on Better Options for the Gardiner East - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: construction, expressways; building, municipal highways
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, moves to pause new contractual obligations for the Gardiner Expressway east of Jarvis Street and study better options, noting no construction is scheduled until 2026 and the cost estimate excludes inflation and ongoing maintenance. The motion asks Council to request the General Manager of Transportation Services to temporarily pause new contracts to allow a comprehensive review of alternatives to rebuilding the elevated expressway.

title: Restoring Majority Rule to City Council - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: provincial legislation;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, moves to defend majority rule, arguing Bill 39 (Better Municipal Governance Act) lets the Mayor pass bylaws with only a third of Council's support. The motion asks Council to call on the new head of Council to publicly commit to never advocating for or implementing provincially initiated changes to Council operations without Council's full prior support and consent.

title: Limiting Provincial Influence in Council Decision-Making - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: legislation, provincial legislation; acts
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, moves to limit provincial influence over Council, arguing Bill 3 (Strong Mayors, Building Homes Act, 2022) concentrates power in the Mayor, including a veto over Council decisions tied to provincial priorities. The motion asks Council to call on the incoming Mayor to reject the veto authority and enshrine that commitment in formal procedures.

title: Save Don’t Pave - The Duffins-Rouge Agricultural Reserve, the Rouge National Park, the federally owned former airport lands or the Greenbelt - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: conservation, natural habitat; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie, moves to affirm Council's support for protecting the Greenbelt, Rouge National Urban Park, Duffins Rouge Agricultural Preserve and the federally owned Pickering lands. The motion cites the City's 50-year history of defending these ecologically and agriculturally important lands, dating to 1974. Council is also asked to support Pickering's unanimous December decision on the lands.

title: Place Names in the Port Lands - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: naming, waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: The Port Lands Flood Protection project will be complete in 2024, creating a new island that will become a mixed-use waterfront community with new streets, parks and community infrastructure. City staff have already engaged the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation on renaming the segment of Cherry Street between Villiers and Commissioners Streets ahead of the new Cherry Street alignment opening in 2023. Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik, recommends that City Council direct the Waterfront Secretariat and the Indigenous Affairs Office to consult Treaty partners and urban Indigenous communities and report back to the Executive Committee in the first quarter of 2024 with proposed naming.

title: Exploring an Iranian Cultural District in Willowdale - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: culture (sc), urban planning districts;
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, moves to explore designating Yonge Street between Steeles Avenue and Drewry Avenue in Willowdale as an Iranian Cultural District. The motion asks Council to request the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture, with the local Councillor's office, to engage community organizations on the idea as part of the City's new Cultural Districts Program.

title: Moving Fast on the Housing Accelerator Fund - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: funding, housing; financing, homes; residences
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng, moves to have Toronto apply at the earliest opportunity to the federal Housing Accelerator Fund. The motion asks Council to direct the Executive Director of the Housing Secretariat and the Chief Planner to prepare a submission to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation. Federal support would help unlock affordable homes and infrastructure for complete communities under the City's Housing Action Plan.

title: City Council Supporting Bill 56, Fewer Floods, Safer Ontario Act, 2022 - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by 	Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: flooding; floods
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, moves to express City Council's support for provincial private member's Bill 56, the Fewer Floods, Safer Ontario Act, 2022, which commits to flood public awareness and education and measures to mitigate flooding risks. The motion also asks Council to forward its support to the Premier and the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing.

title: Don't Block the Box - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: congestion, intersections, traffic; gridlock, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, moves to fight gridlock by asking the Province to stiffen penalties for blocking intersections. The motion asks Council to direct the City Manager to request the Province review the fine structure and consider raising the current $85 fine for an improper stop at an intersection to $450. It comes as Ontario Line construction is expected to worsen congestion.

title: Improving Road Safety by Expanding the Number of Automated Speed Enforcement Cameras and Operational Hours - by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: road safety, speed limits;
brief: Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, moves to expand Automated Speed Enforcement, citing the Vision Zero 2.0 Road Safety Plan's finding that higher speeds raise the risk of severe injury and death. The motion asks Council to direct Transportation Services, Court Services and the City Solicitor to investigate procurement options to add 75 cameras as soon as possible, for 150 city-wide, and to report on feasibility. Cameras have already helped change driver behaviour where installed.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 200 Queens Quay West to the Bentway Conservancy for the Waterfront Reconnect Project to be constructed under the Gardiner Expressway at Lower Simcoe Street - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: development, funding; developing land; development (land); land development, financing
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, moves to release $92,179.93 in Section 37 funds from the 200 Queens Quay West development to the Bentway Conservancy for the Waterfront Reconnect Project under the Gardiner Expressway at Lower Simcoe Street. The contribution was secured when Council approved the site's zoning amendment in July 2022. City Council is asked to add the amount to the Non-Program operating budget on a one-time basis.

title: 1425 Bloor Street West - Liquor Licence Application - Keys Comedy Club (Licence 1967072) - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: licences; licenses; licensing
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, moves to tell the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that a liquor licence for Keys Comedy Club at 1425 Bloor Street West is not in the public interest unless conditions are attached. The premises sits close to homes, and residents have raised concerns about noise, litter, safety and other disturbances. City Council is asked to direct the City Clerk to advise the AGCO Registrar accordingly.

title: The Need for More Openness at Metrolinx Board of Director Meetings - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: public meetings, regional transportation agencies; commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, moves to press for more openness at Metrolinx board meetings, arguing the agency routinely discusses regular matters behind closed doors that municipalities handle in public. The motion asks Council to request the Minister of Transportation and the Province to amend the Metrolinx Act (2006) so Metrolinx and its board operate in a more open, transparent and accountable manner.

title: City Licence to 2249487 Ontario Limited and Fifth Social Club Inc. for the use of the property at 229 Richmond Street West - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: licences; licenses; licensing
brief: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, moves to authorize the Director of Transaction Services to extend and amend the City's licence agreements with 2249487 Ontario Limited (operating as The Ballroom) and Fifth Social Club Inc. for the vacant lot at 229 Richmond Street West. The lot has been used intermittently under the CafeTO program since 2020 to give nearby restaurants patio space during the pandemic. City Council is asked to approve the licence extensions.

title: Toronto is Calling: Supporting the Tourism and Hospitality Sector in Pursuit of a Strong Economic Recovery - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
topics: accommodation providers, tourism; accommodation services; bed and breakfasts; hotel rooms; hotels; lodging (short term); motels; resorts; student hostels; tourist accommodation; traveller accommodation
brief: Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, moves to support the tourism and hospitality sector's economic recovery. The motion asks Council to direct the General Manager of Economic Development and Culture to report back with recommendations for the Mayor to consider in the 2024 budget, on a long-term plan that could allocate Municipal Accommodation Tax revenue to tourism recovery. It builds on programs like CafeTO and the Amplified Live Music on Patios pilot.

title: 1151 Davenport Road - Liquor Licence Application - Lambretta Pizzeria (Licence Number 1984043) - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: An application has been made to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for a liquor licence for the indoor area of Lambretta Pizzeria at 1151 Davenport Road (licence 1984043). Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends that City Council tell the AGCO Registrar that issuing the licence is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns about noise, litter, safety and the premises' closeness to residential units are attached.

title: 60 Brant Street - Authorization to Release Section 37 (Planning Act) Funds for Public Realm and Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: funding; financing
