brief: Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, moves to release $500,000 in Section 37 community benefits from the 489-539 King Street West development for public realm and streetscape improvements around 60 Brant Street. The funds would support the area around the former City Waterworks building, now home to Eva's Phoenix transitional housing for at-risk youth. City Council is asked to add the $500,000 to Transportation Services' 2023 capital budget on a one-time basis.

title: Bolstering the Toronto Police Services Hate Crime Unit - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jaye Robinson
topics: crime, police services; illegal activity, police; policing
brief: Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jaye Robinson, argues that no one in Toronto should face harassment or hate based on national origin, race, culture, language, religion, sex or gender, age, disability or sexual orientation, and that hate crimes are growing in number and investigative complexity. They recommend that City Council ask the Toronto Police Services Board, as part of its 2023 budget and human resources decisions, to consider putting additional personnel, technology and other resources into the Toronto Police Service's Hate Crime Unit to address the growing caseload.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 funds to help fund the provision of new construction of a residential building for affordable rental housing at 6 Shipman Avenue - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: affordable housing, housing; affordable homes; housing projects, homes; residences
brief: Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher, recommends that City Council authorize a one-time transfer of $185,370 to the Housing Secretariat's operating budget, funded by Section 37 community benefits from the development at 2706-2730 Dundas Street West in Ward 4, to support the Neighbourhood Land Trust in building two self-contained affordable rental homes at 6 Shipman Avenue. The funding would flow from the Capital Revolving Reserve Fund for Affordable Housing under the HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan's goal of protecting the affordable rental supply.

title: Adjustments to Toronto Public Health's 2023 Budget to Fund Construction of a New Dental Clinic at 160 Borough Drive - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: dental clinics, health; dentist, health coverage
brief: Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, moves to shift $426,610 from Toronto Public Health's 2023 operating budget to its capital budget to cover higher construction costs for a new dental clinic at 160 Borough Drive. The clinic, next to the busy Scarborough Civic Centre clinic at 150 Borough Drive which has a constant wait list, faces inflation-driven cost increases. City Council is asked to approve the budget reallocation.

title: Authorization to release Section 37 funds to Dixon Hall for the Dixon Hall Community Hub - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: Dixon Hall has served people in need in the Downtown East for almost a century from its single-storey building at 58 Sumach Street; public and private investment will revitalize it into an open, inclusive community hub for housing, food security, settlement services and employment assistance. Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends that City Council increase the 2023 approved operating budget for Non-Program by $500,000 gross ($0 net) on a one-time basis, fully funded by Section 37 community benefits from the developments at 59 Richmond Street East and 114 and 120 Church Street, for the Dixon Hall Community Hub.

title: Waiving Permit Fee Charges for the 2023 Bum Run in Support of Colon Cancer Awareness - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: fees, recreational subsidies; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, financial assistance for recreation programs; welcome policy
brief: The Bum Run began eight years ago to raise awareness that 90 percent of colon cancer deaths are preventable through early diagnosis, raising funds for early diagnosis clinics and prevention; it is Toronto's only 100 percent non-profit registered event, run by unpaid volunteers with all funds going to the cause. Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends that City Council direct the General Manager, Transportation Services to waive the permit fee for the 2023 Bum Run event (Fee Ref. 61.07 under Municipal Code Chapter 441).

title: Implementation of the Fully-Funded Pedestrian Safety Enhancements along Allen Road - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: A fully-funded pedestrian safety project, supported by City staff, would connect the east and west sides of Allen Road with new crosswalks and open the east side to pedestrians with a new sidewalk from Sheppard Avenue West to Rimrock Road. In July 2022 Council directed staff to report detailed design and construction plans to the first 2023 North York Community Council meeting, but the report did not arrive. Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends that City Council ask the General Manager, Transportation Services to report to the May 16, 2023 North York Community Council meeting with a design and implementation plan for the sidewalk and crosswalks.

title: Accessing Justice and Courthouse Safety - Pausing the Closure of the Neighbourhood Courthouses in North York and Scarborough - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford
brief: In 2021 Council adopted a motion on new Toronto courthouses; the new Ontario Court of Justice courthouse at 11 Centre Street will consolidate smaller neighbourhood court locations under one roof. Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Gary Crawford, warns that closing local courthouses will marginalize people accessing justice, hurt small businesses nearby and worsen security concerns at the centralized site. They recommend that City Council reiterate its objections to closing the North York and Scarborough neighbourhood courthouses and send the decision to the Attorney General of Ontario.

title: 411 Victoria Park Avenue - Authorizing an Option to Purchase Agreement with Habitat for Humanity - By Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends that City Council authorize the City to enter into an Option to Purchase Agreement with Habitat for Humanity for the affordable home ownership development at 411 Victoria Park Avenue in Scarborough Southwest. Owner-developer Diamond Kilmer plans to transfer a parcel of land to Habitat to build 58 affordable homeownership townhomes; the City-Habitat option agreement is urgently needed as a prerequisite for Diamond Kilmer to transfer the lands, register its plan of subdivision and issue permits.

title: Supporting Locally-Based Community Health and Well-Being Projects: Toronto Black Farmers Collective's Community Kitchen - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: community outreach; awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach
brief: The Toronto Black Farmers Collective works to bring fresh, locally grown food to communities and families in need and runs workshops on healthy eating and sustainability; a community learning kitchen would give families access to nutritious produce and teach local eco-friendly diets, aligning with City strategies on food scarcity and nutrition. Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends that City Council direct the Executive Director, Social Development, Finance and Administration to explore funding opportunities for the Collective's Community Learning Kitchen and report to the Economic and Community Development Committee.

title: Climate and fiduciary duties of OMERS - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: climate, pensions;
brief: City councillors and employees are among the many Torontonians who rely on the Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System (OMERS) to invest their retirement savings and pay future pensions; how OMERS invests affects both pension values and the liveability of the climate, especially for young people. Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers, recommends that City Council invite OMERS, in 2023, to present a climate strategy to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee that is consistent with OMERS' net-zero commitment and with limiting global heating to 1.5 degrees.

title: College Street Bikeways Extension
topics: bike paths, pedestrian walkways, projects; bicycle paths; bicycle trails; bike trails; cycling paths; cycling trails; off-road paths (cycling), footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways
brief: College Street is one of Toronto's busiest cycling corridors, and 25 vulnerable road users were seriously injured there between 2010 and 2020; in April 2022 Council authorized separated cycle tracks from Manning Avenue to Bay Street. Councillor Dianne Saxe and Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommend that City Council ask the General Manager, Transportation Services to include a study and near-term cycling and pedestrian project on College Street between Lansdowne Avenue and Manning Avenue in the next Near Term Cycling Network Plan (2025-2027) and report back.

title: Modernizing Bike Share Toronto Rate Structure
topics: bicycle sharing, parking authorities, programs; bicycle lending; bike sharing; bikeshare, parking authority
brief: On March 3, 2023 the Toronto Parking Authority Board recommended that City Council approve adjustments to the Bike Share Toronto rate structure. Bike Share Toronto has grown since 2011 from 80 stations and 400,000 annual rides to over 680 stations, 7,100 bikes (including 525 e-bikes) and 4.6 million rides in 2022. The TPA Board recommends that Council approve the rate adjustments (excluding HST) under Municipal Code Chapter 441 to take effect April 3, 2023.

title: Southwest Agincourt Transportation Connections Study
topics: environmental assessments, official plan amendments, road transportation; ea; ecological assessment; environmental assessment; environmental evaluation
brief: Southwest Agincourt is intensifying from low-rise residential and employment uses to higher-density mixed-use buildings, with planned and proposed developments between Highway 401 and Sheppard Avenue East, from Kennedy Road to West Highland Creek, expected to bring about 12,000 new residents plus retail and office space. Without new routes, the added traffic will worsen congestion, and the area lacks safe active transportation routes. The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends that City Council endorse the preferred design for a new north-south complete street and the realignment of Cowdray Court, and authorize the General Manager to proceed.

title: Home Energy Loan Program - Review of Eligibility Requirements
topics: energy, environment (sc); energy resources; energy use
brief: Launched in 2014, the Home Energy Loan Program helps Toronto homeowners make their homes more comfortable, healthier and energy efficient while cutting greenhouse gas emissions, a key TransformTO net-zero program, offering low-interest loans for measures such as air-source heat pumps, window and door replacements, rooftop solar panels and electric vehicle chargers. The Deputy City Manager, Corporate Services recommends that City Council approve changes to the Residential Energy Retrofit Program and amend By-law 1105-2013 to reflect them.

title: Entering into an Agreement with Fred Victor Centre at Regent Park
topics: agreements, infrastructure; tenancy agreements
brief: The General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends that City Council authorize a five-year management agreement with Fred Victor Centre, a registered charity, with a renewal term of up to five years, letting Fred Victor manage the greenhouse, bake oven and community garden complex at Regent Park on the City's behalf. The community partnership is intended to help these park amenities reach their full potential serving the community.

title: Senior Safety Zones - Increasing Speeding Fines
topics: safety, seniors, traffic speed; elderly; geriatric; older adults; senior citizens, public safety
brief: Councillor Crisanti, the City's Seniors Advocate, asks for support in calling on the Province of Ontario to double speeding fines in Senior Safety Zones to better protect seniors. The share of Toronto's population over 65 is projected to reach 21.2 percent by 2041, and Council has established 64 Senior Safety Zones as a first step. Councillor Crisanti recommends that City Council ask the General Manager, Transportation Services, with the City Solicitor, to report to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee on enhanced safety options for Senior Safety Zones, including the feasibility of doubling speeding fines.

title: Parking Regulation Amendments - to temporarily authorize Permit Parking on the east side of Blackthorn Avenue between Rogers Road and Kenora Crescent
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Construction of the Fairbank Silverthorn storm trunk tunnel requires an 18-month road closure on Silverthorn Avenue between Dunraven Drive and Aileen Avenue and between Kenora Crescent and Rogers Road, blocking driveway access for several residents who have been given temporary parking permits. Councillor Nunziata recommends that City Council amend the existing permit parking regulation on Blackthorn Avenue to temporarily authorize permit parking on the east side between Rogers Road and Kenora Crescent, adjusting the existing west-side regulation from house #308 to #424.

title: Entering into an Agreement with Artscape at Spectrum Park (Regent Park Boulevard Park)
topics: agreements, charities, community benefits; charitable organizations; charity, tenancy agreements
brief: The General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends that City Council authorize a non-exclusive nominal fee licence agreement with Toronto Artscape Inc., a registered charity, for community programming at Spectrum Park (Regent Park Boulevard Park) and the adjacent road allowance. The outdoor spaces were built as part of the Regent Park redevelopment for public programming and events, and the agreement would support enhanced community programming through collaboration with Artscape.

title: Regarding an Update on Enforcement and Implementation of the City of Toronto Hate Sponsored Rallies Policy
topics: government (sc), public inquiries; judicial inquries
brief: This is an information item: an administrative inquiry under Municipal Code Section 27-7.11 asks staff for details of enforcement and actions planned by City staff and police in response to ongoing harassment and intimidation of the Jewish community in Toronto, and for an update on implementing the City's Hate Sponsored Rallies Policy. Council adopted the policy (item EX5.3) in May 2019 to give the public service and police tools to discourage and respond to rallies and actions of harassment that demonize and threaten communities. No decision is attached.

title: Determining Impact of Service Hours Changes at City Hall, Metro Hall and Civic Centres
topics: hours of operation; business hours; holiday closures; hours; open hours; operating hours
brief: The Mayor's budget passed February 15 includes significant changes to custodial service levels and public access hours at City Hall, Metro Hall and the Civic Centres. At the same time, the ModernTO office consolidation will relocate the Toronto Community Housing Corporation head office and operations to Metro Hall from 931 Yonge Street, requiring building standards and public access there not be compromised. The motion asks City Council to direct the City Manager and Deputy City Manager, Corporate Services to immediately pause the service reductions at City Hall, Metro Hall and all Civic Centres while the impact on TCHC's requirements is reviewed.

title: Update on the Confirmation Program's Remediation Plans for City IT Divisions, Agencies, and Corporations
brief: This is an information item: City Council had directed the Chief Information Security Officer to periodically report to the General Government Committee on any City agency, corporation or other entity in the cybersecurity Confirmation Program that deviates from the program's objectives (item GL30.12). The report gives updates on agencies' and corporations' adherence to the confirmation program, with details in a confidential attachment. The Chief Information Security Officer recommends that City Council keep Confidential Attachment 1 confidential because it involves the security of City agencies' and corporations' property.

title: Extension of Agreement for the Provision of Electrical and Mechanical Show Services for Events and Exhibitions at Exhibition Place Due to COVID-19 Pandemic
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements; tenancy agreements
brief: In September 2015 the Exhibition Place Board entered a five-year agreement with ShowTech Power and Lighting for the exclusive provision of electrical and mechanical services to shows and events, ending September 14, 2020 with an extension option. The Board of Governors of Exhibition Place recommends that City Council approve a two-year extension of the ShowTech agreement from September 15, 2022 to September 14, 2024, on the same terms and conditions.

title: Request for Authority to Enter into a Non-Competitive Agreement with OpenText Corporation leveraging the Provincial Volume Licensing Agreement
brief: The Chief Technology Officer and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend that City Council authorize the Chief Technology Officer to execute a non-competitive agreement with OpenText Corporation under the provincial Volume Licensing Agreement for Enterprise Information Management products and services, at $965,000 net of taxes ($981,984 net of HST recoveries). More than 90 percent of City information is created electronically, and the City needs the supporting infrastructure to manage the full lifecycle of its paper and electronic records.

title: Below Market Rent Lease Agreement with Toronto Cat Rescue at 705 Progress Avenue, Unit 15, and Designation of the Premises as a Municipal Capital Facility
brief: The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management and the Executive Director, Municipal Licensing and Standards recommend that City Council authorize the City to enter into a below-market basic rent lease and a service agreement with Toronto Cat Rescue for about 2,031 square feet at 705 Progress Avenue, Unit 15. Council is also asked to pass the by-law designating the premises, owned by the City and the Toronto District School Board, as a Municipal Capital Facility, which provides an exemption from municipal and education taxes.

title: The Disposition of 13 Barberry Place
brief: The Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management seeks City Council authority to dispose of a small remnant portion of the property at 13 Barberry Place, shown as Part 1 on the report's Attachment 1, without giving the previous owner the first chance to repurchase it on the terms of the best offer, as section 42 of the Expropriations Act would otherwise require. The surplus lands are a small leftover from the original expropriation, and the previous owner owns no abutting property.

title: Proposed Governance Change in respect of the Retirement Compensation Arrangement for certain members of the Metropolitan Toronto Police Benefit Fund
brief: The Controller recommends amending By-law 18-97 so the City of Toronto assumes the responsibilities of the Board of Trustees of the legacy Metropolitan Toronto Police Benefit Fund in relation to the Police Retirement Compensation Arrangement (RCA), discharging the trustees of further responsibility. The Benefit Fund was rolled into OMERS in 2019, the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario has approved closing it, and the remaining step is repealing the Benefit Fund By-law 181-81; the Police RCA itself cannot be rolled into OMERS.

title: 240 Alton Towers Circle - Designation of a Portion of the Property as a Municipal Capital Facility
brief: The Controller recommends that City Council pass a by-law under Section 252 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006 to designate space leased by Toronto Public Health as a Municipal Capital Facility, with an exemption from municipal and education taxes. The space is about 1,700 square feet at 240 Alton Towers Circle, suite 300, leased from Cedar City Paradise (Milliken) Inc.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Traffic Logix Corporation for Watch Your Speed Signs for the Vision Zero Road Safety Plan - School Safety Zone Program
topics: contracts, purchasing, road safety, transportation; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, transportation services
brief: The General Manager of Transportation Services and the Acting Chief Procurement Officer recommend that City Council authorize a non-competitive agreement with Traffic Logix Corporation for the supply and delivery of 'Watch Your Speed' signs for the Vision Zero Road Safety Plan's School Safety Zone Program. The two-year term runs from the award date to December 31, 2024 with an option to renew for three additional one-year periods, totalling $4,067,273 net of HST ($4,138,857 net of HST recoveries); a 2017 blanket contract with the same company came from a competitive quotation process.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Orange Traffic Inc. for the Supply and Delivery of Traffic Signal Controllers
topics: contracts, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations
brief: The General Manager of Transportation Services and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend that City Council authorize a non-competitive five-year agreement with Orange Traffic Inc. for the supply and delivery of traffic signal controllers, at $3,046,590 net of HST ($3,100,210 net of HST recoveries). A recent request for quotations for traffic control equipment split the work into five parts to be awarded separately, but Part C covering the controllers did not yield an award through that process.

title: Non-competitive Contract with Midome Construction Services Limited for the New Streetcar Tracks on Adelaide Street
brief: The Interim Chief Engineer, the General Manager of Transportation Services and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend that City Council authorize a non-competitive contract with Midome Construction Services Limited to install new streetcar tracks and related infrastructure on Adelaide Street between York Street and Victoria Street, at $39,545,000 net of taxes ($40,240,992 net of HST recoveries). Metrolinx intends to fund $39,235,000 of the track installation and the City would fund $310,000 for road resurfacing on Adelaide Street.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with Clearway Construction Limited to Rescue a Micro-Tunneling Boring Machine on Old Mill Drive for Assignment 5-01 Under the Basement Flooding Protection Program Phase 4
brief: This is an information item: the report advises Council of an emergency non-competitive contract with Clearway Construction Limited to rescue a micro-tunnelling boring machine on Old Mill Drive, north of Bloor Street, for Assignment 5-01 under the Basement Flooding Protection Program Phase 4. The contract totals $8,997,161 excluding HST ($9,155,511 net of HST recoveries); it was issued as a matter of extreme urgency because the stuck machine posed a significant public health and safety hazard. The Chief Engineer and the Chief Procurement Officer recommend that City Council receive the report for information.

title: Award to Multiple Suppliers for Collection Services for Provincial Offences Act Fines for Court Services Division
brief: The Chief Procurement Officer and the Director, Court Services report the results of the request for proposals for collection agency services for defaulted Provincial Offences Act fines; existing contracts expire March 31, 2023 and new contracts are needed. They recommend that City Council authorize awarding the contract to nine recommended suppliers and approve their commission rates under the City of Toronto Act, 2006, with the services segmented into three categories.

title: Award of Ariba Document Number 3448368603 to CH2M Hill Canada Limited and Stantec Consulting Limited for Professional Engineering Services for Phase 5 of the Basement Flooding Protection Program
brief: The Chief Engineer and the Chief Procurement Officer report the results of the request for proposals for professional engineering services for Phase 5 of the Basement Flooding Protection Program, covering program management, design, construction administration and post-construction services. They recommend that the General Government Committee authorize agreements with CH2M Hill Canada Limited at $41,348,551 net of taxes ($42,076,285 net of HST recoveries) and Stantec Consulting Limited at $43,768,591 net of taxes ($44,538,918 net of HST recoveries).

title: Evans Avenue and Ourland Avenue - Traffic Control Signals
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, road safety, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: because the TTC operates transit service on Evans Avenue, City Council approval is required. Transportation Services assessed the intersection of Evans Avenue and Ourland Avenue and recommends installing traffic control signals to enhance safety for all road users, finding the installation justified.

title: Islington Avenue and Prince George Drive/Ridgevalley Crescent - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, pedestrian crossovers, traffic signals; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: because the TTC operates transit service on Islington Avenue, City Council approval is required. Transportation Services reviewed the need for pedestrian crossing protection at Islington Avenue and Prince George Drive/Ridgevalley Crescent and recommends installing traffic control signals to enhance safety for vulnerable road users.

title: Fenmar Drive - Parking Amendments
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, standing prohibitions; no standing, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: because the TTC operates transit service on Fenmar Drive, City Council approval is required. Transportation Services recommends prohibiting standing at all times on the north side of Fenmar Drive between Signet Drive and a point 165 metres east, to deter parking there and improve vehicle movements for loading and transit operations.

title: 4195, 4219, 4221 Dundas Street West and 556, 558, 560, 562 and 564 Prince Edward Drive North - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, municipal officials, official plan amendments, rezoning; city officials, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A 2016 zoning by-law amendment application for an eight-storey mixed-use building with 166 units at 4195 Dundas Street West was revised in May 2022 to cover 4195, 4219 and 4221 Dundas Street West and 556-564 Prince Edward Drive North, proposing three 18-storey towers (61.4 metres excluding mechanical penthouse) with mixed uses. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and City staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the current Official Plan and zoning amendment appeals.

title: 5415-5481, 5485 and 5487 Dundas Street West and 15 and 25 Shorncliffe Road - Application to Lift the Holding Provision - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, municipal officials, planning & development (sc); city officials
brief: The application proposes lifting the holding symbol on the site at 5415-5481, 5485 and 5487 Dundas Street West and 15 and 25 Shorncliffe Road, where the site-specific by-law permits a comprehensive multi-phase mixed-use development of four buildings and eight towers ranging from 26 to 44 storeys, with 2,875 residential units, over 15,000 square metres of non-residential floor area and a 4,144 square metre public park. The holding provision relates to specified off-site servicing upgrades. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council amend Zoning By-law 206-2022 to remove the holding symbol.

title: 5251 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [buildings by height], rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: The City Planning Division reviews and recommends approval of the application to amend the Zoning By-law to permit a 50-storey (153 metres) mixed-use development at 5251 Dundas Street West with 544 dwelling units and 200 square metres of ground-floor retail, for a total gross floor area of 35,247 square metres. A privately-owned publicly-accessible space is proposed at the northeast corner to improve pedestrian access to the Kipling Mobility Hub south of the site. The proposal conforms with the Official Plan and the Etobicoke Centre Secondary Plan.

title: 20 Brow Drive (Long Branch GO Station) - City-Initiated Zoning By-Law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: land use, regional transportation agencies, rezoning, transit networks; commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: This City-initiated zoning by-law amendment would allow a transit station use at 20 Brow Drive by applying a Commercial-Residential (CR) zoning category to the site. The Long Branch GO station already occupies the site although the current zoning does not permit a transit station; the rezoning supports Metrolinx's planned improvements of two new station entrance buildings, a reconfigured surface parking lot and pick-up/drop-off area, new bicycle parking and landscaping. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council approve the amendment.

title: SmartTrack Stations Program - Update
topics: budgets, programs; budgets and accounts
brief: In February 2021 Council approved terms with the Province to advance the SmartTrack Stations Program to construction, delivered by the Province and its agencies with a scope of five stations: Finch-Kennedy, East Harbour, King-Liberty, St. Clair-Old Weston and Bloor-Lansdowne. The City's capital contribution was reconfirmed at $1.463 billion, including $585 million from the federal government. The Deputy City Manager, Infrastructure and Development Services recommends that City Council direct the City Manager to negotiate with the Province for it to pay all costs above the original $1.463 billion budget needed to deliver the program.

title: Amendment to Delegation of Authority for the Endorsement of Temporary Liquor Licences
topics: legislation, licences; acts, licenses; licensing
brief: Because of provincial legislation changes, the permanent CaféTO program and the need to streamline temporary liquor licensing administration, the City Clerk recommends that City Council update the delegation of authority to the City Clerk's Office. The update would cover designating an event of municipal significance and issuing letters of non-objection to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for Special Occasion Permits and temporary liquor extensions of hours (4 a.m. extensions).

title: Making Electronic Participation for Council and its Local Boards Permanent
topics: meetings, municipal codes;
brief: The City Clerk recommends that City Council amend Municipal Code Chapter 27, Council Procedures, to make electronic participation a permanent option for meetings of City Council and its committees, and to let local boards amend their own rules of procedure. Members participating electronically would be deemed present for determining quorum and for other meeting purposes.

title: Deferred Revenue Report at September 30, 2022 and Administrative Amendments to Obligatory Reserve Fund
topics: budgets, development; budgets and accounts, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: The City collects monies it must set aside for specific purposes, such as development charges collected at building permit issuance to fund growth-related infrastructure; these are recorded as deferred revenue liabilities. The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommends that City Council establish a new obligatory reserve fund called the 'Development Charges Reserve Fund - Transit (EELRT)' under Municipal Code Chapter 227 to fund the Eglinton East Light Rail Transit, and receive the deferred revenue report at September 30, 2022.

title: City of Toronto Relationship Framework for the Toronto Parking Authority
topics: organizational structure, port authorities; administrative structure; divisions; reporting relationship; reporting structure
brief: The City Manager recommends that City Council adopt the City's Relationship Framework for the Toronto Parking Authority, the governing instrument setting out the agency's mandate, delegations of authority, legislative framework, policy directions, accountability and relationship to the City. The framework reflects the Authority's mandate in Municipal Code Chapter 179, subsequent Council decisions and applicable policies and legislation. Council is also asked to authorize the City Manager, with the City Solicitor, to make technical changes to the framework.

title: Amended and Restated Master Agreement with the Canadian National Exhibition Association, Exhibition Place and City of Toronto
topics: Canadian National Exhibition, Exhibition Place; cne; the ex
brief: Since 2013 the City has been party to a Master Agreement with the Canadian National Exhibition Association and the Exhibition Place Board governing the CNEA's use of Exhibition Place grounds for the 18-day Canadian National Exhibition. The existing agreement expires March 31, 2023. The City Manager recommends that City Council authorize an Amended and Restated Master Agreement for five years from April 1, 2023 to March 31, 2028, with a possible further five-year renewal, requiring the CNEA to pay licence fees at discounted rates for the grounds and for services.

title: 2023 Financial Update and Outlook
topics: budgets, finance (sc), funding; budgets and accounts, financing
brief: This is an information item: the report gives a financial update and outlook to inform the City's long-term financial planning and a forthcoming updated Long-Term Financial Plan. After the 2023 budget, the City updated its financial model with an independent third party to assess long-term fiscal risks over the next ten years, highlighting significant challenges ahead; an updated Long-Term Financial Plan will come to Council later in 2023. The City Manager and the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer recommend that City Council receive the report for information.

title: Community Safety Issues and Response
topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: The Toronto Transit Commission asks City Council to authorize withdrawing up to $15 million from the TTC Stabilization Reserve. The funds would implement any unbudgeted measures to address the health, safety and security of TTC employees, customers and the public across the transit network.

title: Ontario Good Road Association Board Quarterly Committee meetings and Board meeting update on Thursday March 2 and Friday March 3, 2023
topics: conferences, exhibits; conference travel, exhibitions; exhibitors
brief: This is an information item: Councillor Paul Ainslie, the City's appointee to the Ontario Good Roads Association Board of Directors, reports on the quarterly committee and board meetings held March 2 and 3, 2023, covering road safety auditing guidelines, a reduced load period calculator, the Skills Development Fund Round III application, education program performance and pre-trip inspection training for municipal drivers. Councillor Ainslie recommends that City Council receive the update for information.

title: Business Improvement Areas (BIAs) - 2023 Operating Budgets - Report 2
topics: business improvement areas, operating budgets; bia; business improvement associations
brief: The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer brings forward Business Improvement Area annual operating budgets for City Council approval, as required by the City of Toronto Act, 2006; Council approval lets the City collect funds through a special tax levy on commercial and industrial properties in each BIA. The recommendation is that Council adopt and certify the 2023 operating budgets and levy requirements for the BIAs in this second report, including Bloorcourt Village ($322,645 budget, $203,488 levy) and Church-Wellesley Village ($584,294 budget).

title: Appointment of City of Toronto Photo Laureate
topics: [people in culture], appointments, culture (sc), photography; cameras; images; photographers; photographs; photos
brief: The General Manager, Economic Development and Culture recommends that City Council appoint Nadya Kwandibens as the third City of Toronto Photo Laureate for a term from April 1, 2023 to December 31, 2026, or until a successor is appointed. The Photo Laureate honours a photographer recognized by peers for artistic excellence and major contributions to photography, serving as an advocate for visual culture, art photography and photojournalism; Kwandibens is Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) from Animakee Wa Zhing #37 First Nation in northwestern Ontario, an award-winning portrait and events photographer and a Canon Ambassador.

title: Claim to Recover Damages - Toronto Police Service Data Centre
topics: damages, police facilities;
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Solicitor seeks direction from City Council on a claim to recover damages related to the Toronto Police Service data centre, which sits in a City-owned building. Responsibilities are shared: the Police Service handles the data room and systems, while the City's Corporate Real Estate Division handles building operations including mechanical and electrical systems. Council is asked to adopt the confidential instructions to staff in Confidential Attachment 1.

title: Review and Consideration for a Housing Commissioner Role or Function at Ombudsman Toronto
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: In July 2022 Council asked Ombudsman Toronto to consider reports on a possible housing commissioner role, including the May 2022 Maytree consultant report and the June 2022 City Manager's report, and to recommend the resources and structure needed for the office to investigate systemic housing discrimination and systemic barriers in the City's housing planning and service delivery. The Ombudsman recommends that City Council authorize a dedicated unit within the office, reporting to the Ombudsman, to focus on those investigations and reports.

title: 51 Panorama Court - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Chief Planner and Executive Director recommends that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 51 Panorama Court under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value, and grant authority to enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement. The property, on the south side of Panorama Court northeast of Kipling Avenue and Finch Avenue West near the Humber River, was the former County Branch of the Hospital for Sick Children (1928-1957) and later the provincially-owned Thistletown Regional Centre for Children and Adolescents (1957-2014).

title: Appointment of Public Member to the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board
topics: appointments, public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel - Corporations recommends that City Council appoint Mike York as a public member of the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board, at the pleasure of Council, for a term ending July 20, 2025 and until a successor is appointed. The recommendation follows the panel's March 20, 2023 meeting.

title: Appointment of Public Member to the Toronto Hydro Board
topics: appointments, public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel - Corporations recommends that City Council appoint Earl Davis as a public member of the Toronto Hydro Board, at the pleasure of Council, for a term ending March 31, 2025 and until a successor is appointed. title: Intergovernmental Advocacy Efforts on Toronto's Refugee Claimant Shelter Response
topics: housing services, intergovernmental relations, refugees; federal-municipal relations; governmental relations; inter-governmental relations; intergovernmental cooperation; provincial-municipal relations
brief: This is an information item: Toronto's shelter system faces ongoing occupancy challenges, and the City has exhausted its resources to sustain a dedicated response to refugee claimant (asylum seeker) arrivals without widening its operating budget gap or cutting capital spending. The City is advocating for tri-level government collaboration on the current surge and a formal intergovernmental strategy for sudden large-scale asylum seeker arrivals; a supplementary report with updated information is planned. The City Manager recommends that City Council receive the report for information.

title: Modernizing Bike Share Toronto Rate Structure
topics: bicycle sharing, boards of management, parking authorities, power-assisted bicycles; bicycle lending; bike sharing; bikeshare, boards of directors; boards of governors, e-bikes; electric bicycles; electric bikes; electric-assisted bikes; power assisted bicycles, parking authority
brief: Bike Share Toronto has grown since 2011 from 80 stations and 400,000 annual rides to one of North America's largest bike share systems, with over 680 stations, 7,100 bikes (including 525 e-bikes) and 4.6 million rides in 2022. Management's growth strategy would expand the system to all 25 wards and electrify over 20 percent of the fleet. The President recommends that the Toronto Parking Authority Board recommend that City Council approve adjustments to the Bike Share Toronto rate structure (excluding HST), as required by Municipal Code Chapter 441.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - Financial Performance for the Year Ended December 31, 2022 (Unaudited)
topics: boards of management, budgets, financial reports, parking authorities; annual financial reports; financial statements, boards of directors; boards of governors, budgets and accounts, parking authority
brief: This is an information item: Toronto Parking Authority's unaudited 2022 results show net income of $31.4 million, $17.0 million above plan. Total revenue was $129.2 million, $8.9 million above plan, as parking revenues recovered to 76.2 percent of pre-pandemic 2019 levels; costs were $97.7 million, $8.2 million below plan, largely from deliberate spending conservation amid recovery uncertainty. Audited statements come to the May 2023 board meeting. The President recommends the Board receive the report for information.

The change responds to Council's direction through recommendation 8 of the Auditor General's report AU4.5 on safeguarding rent-geared-to-income assistance, and builds on the City's existing technology for service continuity and system integration.

title: Cancellation, Reduction or Refund of Property Taxes - March 3, 2023 Hearing
brief: This is a procedural item: the report covers tax appeal applications made to the Treasurer under Sections 323 and 325 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006. Section 323 lets Council cancel, reduce or refund taxes when a property is destroyed, demolished, becomes exempt or changes use; Section 325 covers overcharges from assessment roll errors. The legislation requires a decision after a public meeting where applicants may appear. The Controller recommends that the General Government Committee approve the individual applications and tax reductions listed in Appendix A.

On November 10, 2021, Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment, and Draft Plan of Subdivision applications were submitted to permit a 24-storey (76 metres high) mixed-use building and a 9-storey residential building (30 metres high) at 2402-2418 Dufferin Street and 4-10 Ramsden Road. Also proposed are a northerly extension to the existing municipal laneway within the site, and an on-site parkland dedication of 509.66 square metres at the southwest corner of the site. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate City staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the current Applications regarding the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment.

title: Recipient of the 2023 Agnes Macphail Award
topics: awards, commendations, letters, volunteering; volunteer groups; volunteers
brief: This is a procedural item: the Agnes Macphail Award, established by the former Borough of East York, annually recognizes an outstanding volunteer who upheld the values and causes of Agnes Macphail and lives within the former borough's boundaries. The recognition committee met on January 9 and 23, 2023 and unanimously chose Thorncliffe Park community leader Shakhlo Sharipova; North York Community Council recommends that City Council approve her as the 2023 recipient.

title: 529-543 Marlee Avenue and 805-819 Glencairn Avenue Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The applicant has appealed the planning application for 529-543 Marlee Avenue and 805-819 Glencairn Avenue Official Plan Amendment and Zoning Amendment Application to the Ontario Land Tribunal. On November 29, 2021, a complete application to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-laws (21 221282 NNY 08 OZ) were submitted to permit a 28 storey (89.35 metres excluding mechanical penthouse) mixed-use building with 306 residential dwelling units and retail uses at grade (224.50 square metres). The proposal also includes a road widening of Marlee Avenue and an on-site parkland dedication. The City Planning Division recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and appropriate City staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal in opposition to the current Application regarding the Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment appeal for the lands at 529-543 Marlee Avenue and 805-819 Glencairn Avenue.

title: Senlac Road, South of the York Cemetery and Funeral Centre Access - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, pedestrians; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, pedestrianization
brief: As the Toronto Transit Commission operates a transit service on Senlac Road, City Council approval of this report is required. Transportation Services has reviewed the need for pedestrian crossing protection on Senlac Road at the York Cemetery and Funeral Centre access. The Director, Traffic Management, Transportation Services recommends that City Council authorize the installation of a pedestrian crossover on Senlac Road at a point approximately 210 metres north of Burnett Avenue.

title: 699 Sheppard Ave East Application to Lift the Holding Provisions (H) - Decision Report- Approval
topics: zoning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Planning staff recommend approving the planning application for 699 Sheppard Ave East Application to Lift the Holding Provisions (H). This application proposes to lift the Holding symbol (H) for the site at 699 Sheppard Avenue East and subject to site specific Zoning By-laws 468-2022 and 469-2022. These by-laws permit a 12-storey mixed use building, containing 169 residential units at 699 Sheppard Avenue East subject to a Holding provision. The Holding provisions of Zoning by-law 468-2022 and 469-2022 requires that prior to lifting the Holding symbol (H) upgrades to the sanitary sewer must be completed to the satisfaction of the Chief Engineer and Executive Director, Engineering and Construction Services and the General Manager, Toronto Water. City Council is asked to approve the application.

title: 11 Polson Street - Maya Corp Application to Remove Conditions from their Liquor Licence - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: applications, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, application process
brief: In 2017, after the City, the Toronto Island Noise Committee and the York Quay Residents' Association objected, the Licence Appeal Tribunal approved a liquor licence for 11 Polson Street with nine conditions, including a ban on amplified sound on or directed at the outdoor licensed area. The licence holder, Maya Corp, has now applied to remove or amend those conditions, and the AGCO has issued a Notice of Proposal to refuse that application. Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor to retain party status in the appeal.

title: Expressing Support for Bill 5, Stopping Harassment and Abuse by Local Leaders Act - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: elected officials, harassment; elected representatives
brief: A private member's bill, Bill 5, the Stopping Harassment and Abuse by Local Leaders Act, was introduced in the Legislative Assembly in March 2021 and was at First Reading as of August 10, 2022; it would amend the Municipal Act, 2001 and the City of Toronto Act, 2006 to require municipal codes of conduct to include compliance with workplace violence and harassment policies. Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that City Council express its support for Bill 5 and forward the item to Premier Doug Ford, the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, Toronto MPPs and others.

title: 63 and 73 Widdicombe Hill Boulevard - Technical Amendment to By-laws 976-2022 and 977-2022 - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: apartments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: in July 2022 Council adopted amendments and enacted By-laws 976-2022 and 977-2022 to permit redevelopment of 63 and 73 Widdicombe Hill Boulevard with two new apartment buildings of seven and 18 storeys, keeping the two existing 17-storey apartment buildings. City Planning found a minor error in the height map: the southernmost part of Building B is shown as permitting three storeys. Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley, recommends that Council amend both by-laws with corrected schedules.

title: 4097 Lawrence Avenue East and 197 to 201 Galloway Road  - Technical Amendment to By-law 251-2022 - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: in March 2022 Council adopted Scarborough Community Council item SC30.2 and enacted By-law 251-2022 to permit redevelopment of 4097 Lawrence Avenue East and 197 to 201 Galloway Road at greater height and density than Zoning By-law 569-2013 allows, in exchange for community benefits and a Section 37 agreement. City Planning found a technical error needing correction. Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that Council amend Diagram 4 of the by-law and replace Site Specific Regulation (M) of Exception CR 463.

title: Reviewing Revenue Tool Options for Toronto - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: finance (sc), revenue generation; revenue tools
brief: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise, recommends that City Council direct the City Manager, the Deputy City Manager and the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer to report in the third quarter of 2023 with an updated assessment of revenue-generating options available under the City of Toronto Act, 2006. The motion argues the discussion of a new fiscal deal with the federal and provincial governments needs current information, noting a 2016 review led to expressway tolls (later rejected by the province), the hotel tax and harmonized land transfer tax rates.

title: Street Vending Permit Transfer - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: street vending, vendor permits; boulevard vending; curb lane vending; curblane vending; food carts; food vending carts; hot dog carts; sidewalk vending; vending
brief: David Roland Schooley has operated a hot dog cart under a Sidewalk Vending Permit on the north side of Lake Shore Boulevard, 30 metres east of Bay Street, for many years, and the family relies on it as their main income. A moratorium blocks new sidewalk vending permits and prohibits transferring them, so Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends that City Council allow the permit to be transferred anyway, describing the request as urgent because the cart cannot keep operating without the transfer.

title: 341 Jane Street - Liquor Licence Application - Salsa Venezuelan Street Food - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: An application has been made to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for a liquor sales licence for the indoor area of Salsa Venezuelan Street Food at 341 Jane Street. Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends that City Council tell the AGCO Registrar that issuing the licence is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns about noise, litter, safety and the premises' closeness to residential units are attached.

title: 73 Bainbridge Avenue - Request for Representation at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: municipal officials, zoning bylaws; city officials, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The owner of 73 Bainbridge Avenue applied to the Committee of Adjustment (Application A0553/22NY) for minor variances to build a new dwelling; Planning staff opposed the variances for building length, building depth and lot coverage, but the Committee approved the application on January 19, 2023. Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor to appeal the decision to the Toronto Local Appeal Body and attend with City staff in support of staff's position; the appeal deadline is February 8, 2023.

title: Metrolinx's Community Participation and Actions Regarding Osgoode Station and the Ontario Line - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: community outreach, public transit; awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: On February 1, 2023 the City's Transit Expansion Office shared an independent consultant's review of potential locations for the Osgoode Hall station entrance for the Ontario Line, but Metrolinx said at the community presentation that evening it would start construction immediately without giving the community time to receive the report; on February 5 the Law Society of Ontario was granted an interim injunction. Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe, recommends that City Council ask Metrolinx to halt removal of the Osgoode Garden's trees until the Construction Liaison Committee can reconvene to discuss siting options, and to create a structure for participatory engagement with community stakeholders.

title: 43 Tank House Lane - Liquor Licence Application Old Flame Brewing Co. - License 1987901 - by Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: An application has been made to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for a liquor licence covering indoor and outdoor areas for Old Flame Brewing Co. at 43 Tank House Lane (licence 1987901), in close proximity to residential units. Councillor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor to seek party status at the Licence Appeal Tribunal at the earliest opportunity if the matter is appealed, and to attend all proceedings.

title: 139 Poyntz Avenue - Request for Representation at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: municipal officials, zoning bylaws; city officials, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The owner of 139 Poyntz Avenue applied to the Committee of Adjustment (Application A0714/22NY) for minor variances to build a new second-storey addition over the existing foundation, a new garage and a new one-storey addition. Planning staff recommended a modification to the lot coverage, but the Committee approved the application on January 19, 2023 with a condition from Urban Forestry to submit a complete permit application for injuring or removing City-owned trees. Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor to appeal the decision to the Toronto Local Appeal Body and attend with City staff in support of staff's position.

title: 68 Alcorn Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Appeal and Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, municipal officials; city officials
brief: On January 18, 2023 the Toronto and East York Panel of the Committee of Adjustment approved three minor variances, including soft landscaping and setbacks, for an existing rear deck at 68 Alcorn Avenue (Application A0787/22TEY), even though Community Planning staff recommended refusal, saying a reduced density would better match the zoning by-law's intent. Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle, recommends that City Council have the City Solicitor and City staff appeal the decision to the Toronto Local Appeal Body.

title: Casting a wider net: Updating the eligibility requirements for property tax, water and solid waste relief programs - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: property taxes, tax reduction; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts, tax assistance; tax decrease; tax rebate; tax refunds; tax relief
brief: The City gives financial relief to eligible low-income seniors and people with disabilities through its property tax, water and solid waste relief programs, applied for once a year through a single application. With a 5.5 percent property tax increase in the current budget proposal, Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, recommends that City Council ask the Chief Financial Officer to report back at the February 15, 2023 Council meeting on the programs' current status and the costs and implications of widening eligibility.

title: 319 Roncesvalles Avenue - Liquor Licence Application Roncevalles Convenience Plus T.B.K.A Alimentari Italian Grocery - License 1937452 - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: applications, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, application process
brief: An application has been made to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for a liquor licence for the indoor area of Roncesvalles Convenience Plus T.B.K.A Alimentari Italian Grocery at 319 Roncesvalles Avenue (licence 1937452). Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends that City Council tell the AGCO Registrar that issuing the licence is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns about noise, litter, safety and the premises' closeness to residential units are attached.

title: 3051-3079 Pharmacy Avenue Item  - Minor Amendments to Zoning By-Laws - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: in February 2022 Scarborough Community Council required the applicant for 3051-3079 Pharmacy Avenue to submit a revised Functional Servicing Report showing that groundwater discharge to the City's sewers meets Municipal Code Chapter 681 before zoning bills could be introduced. The Chief Engineer confirmed satisfaction on January 31, 2023. Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Deputy Mayor Jennifer McKelvie, recommends that City Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the lands in line with the draft by-law attached to the February 8, 2022 planning report.

title: 818 Eastern Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Retain Outside Consultant at Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: zoning;
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll, recommends that City Council authorize the City Solicitor to retain outside consultants as needed to assess any settlement proposal and to continue opposing the appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of a minor variance for 818 Eastern Avenue (Application A0706/21TEY; TLAB file 21 250427 S45 14). Council had already directed the City Solicitor in February 2022 to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose the application and try to negotiate a resolution.

title: Extending the Vacant Homes Tax Declaration Due Date and Adding Additional Instalment Due Dates for Making VHT Payments - by Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Mayor John Tory
topics: taxes; levies
brief: Toronto implemented the Vacant Home Tax in 2022, requiring all property owners to declare their property's occupancy status each year; the first declaration was due February 2, 2023. Councillor Gary Crawford, seconded by Mayor John Tory, recommends that City Council extend the declaration due date to give owners a grace period in the tax's first year, and amend Municipal Code Chapter 778 to replace the single May 1 payment date with three equal yearly instalment dates to moderate the financial impact.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds to Toronto District School Board for Winona/McMurrich Senior and Junior Public School Playground and Schoolyard Revitalization - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, recommends that City Council contribute $150,000 of Section 45 development funds toward a new playground and schoolyard at Winona/McMurrich Senior and Junior Public School, used by the school and the broader community. The funding would help revitalize the playground, field, basketball courts and other outdoor areas, and the motion asks Council to increase the 2023 Operating Budget for Non-Program by $150,000 gross ($0 net), fully funded by Section 45 funds from the development at 834-840 St Clair Avenue West.

title: 400 Euclid Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: municipal officials, zoning; city officials
brief: In April 2022 the owner of 400 Euclid Avenue applied to the Committee of Adjustment for variances to legalize and keep a two-storey semi-detached house converted into 22 self-contained rental units built without a building permit, plus a reconstructed front basement walkout. City staff first thought 21 of the units were rooming-house dwelling rooms but confirmed by site visit that all 22 are self-contained units. Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford, recommends that City Council authorize the City Solicitor to seek party status at the Toronto Local Appeal Body and attend the hearing with City staff.

title: 970 College Street - Liquor Licence Application - Lardo (Licence Number 2015037) - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: An application has been made to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for a liquor licence for the indoor area of Lardo at 970 College Street (licence 2015037). Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks, recommends that City Council tell the AGCO Registrar that issuing the licence is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns about noise, litter, safety and the premises' closeness to residential units are attached.

title: 1165 Bloor Street West - Liquor Licence Application - Island Oysters (Licence Number 2003373) - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: An application has been made to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for a liquor licence for the indoor area of Island Oysters at 1165 Bloor Street West (licence 2003373).
