title: Moving by One Day the Special Council Meeting on Budget - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: This is a procedural item: following the death of former Mississauga Mayor Hazel McCallion, whose state funeral is scheduled for February 14, 2023 (what would have been her 102nd birthday). Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata, recommends that City Council move its special meeting on the Mayor's proposed budget from February 14 to February 15, 2023, and adjust the shortened 30-day period for Council amendments to the budget accordingly.

title: Support for Bill 47, Protecting Human Rights in an Emergency Act (Emergency Power Generators) - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: human rights, residential landlords;
brief: In November 2022, MPPs moved to amend the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 and the Condominium Act, 1998 through Bill 47, the Protecting Human Rights in an Emergency Act (Emergency Power Generators), 2022, so that landlords and condo corporations must provide emergency power protections for residents, such as working elevators for people with mobility issues, hallway lighting and access to clean water. Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik, recommends that City Council express its support for the bill and forward it to several Toronto-area MPPs.

title: Joint Appointment of Waterfront Toronto Chair - by Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: boards of management, waterfronts; boards of directors; boards of governors, lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: This is a procedural item: Mayor John Tory, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik, recommends that City Council, together with the provincial and federal governments, reappoint Stephen Diamond as a Director and Chair of Waterfront Toronto for a three-month term from March 21, 2023 to June 30, 2023. Diamond has chaired the board for four years, and the extension would provide continuity while the board searches for and transitions to a new Chair.

title: Conveyance of Parkland - 35, 41, 63, 65 and 95 High Park Avenue and 66 and 102-116 Pacific Avenue - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik
topics: parkland dedication;
brief: As approved, the owner of the development at 35, 41, 63, 65 and 95 High Park Avenue and 66 and 102-116 Pacific Avenue must convey 1,832 square metres of on-site parkland to the City before any above-grade building permit is issued, but the owner is not yet ready to do so because of the waste management method currently serving the site's nearly one thousand rental units, even though an above-grade permit for Tower A is expected early in 2023. Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Ausma Malik, recommends that City Council amend its 2019 approval (item 2019.CC13.10) to change the parkland dedication requirement.

title: Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant Effluent Disinfection System - Construction Delay Claims
topics: construction, wastewater treatment, water treatment plants; building, filtration plants; water filtration plants; water treatment and supply plants; water treatment facilities, sewage treatment; waste water treatment; wastewater management
brief: The City awarded Contract No. 17ECS-MI-03AB to Graham Construction and Engineering LP ("Graham") on January 19, 2018 to upgrade the effluent disinfection system at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant ("ABTP") and to refurbish the water pumping station and seawall substation. The City Solicitor recommends that City Council adopt the confidential instructions to staff.

title: Update on the Transition of Toronto's Blue Bin Recycling Program to Extended Producer Responsibility
topics: blue bins, city initiatives, recycling; blue boxes; recycling boxes, city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives
brief: This report provides an update on the outcome of negotiations with a Producer Responsibility Organization (Circular Materials Ontario) on the City of Toronto's role as a recycling service provider from July 1, 2023 to December 31, 2025. The City of Toronto entered into a contract with Circular Materials Ontario to provide recycling collection, transfer and haulage, promotion and education, and 311 customer services to municipally-serviced residential households, schools, and long-term care facilities for financial remuneration. The General Manager of Solid Waste Management Services recommends that City Council authorize the General Manager, Solid Waste Management Services to participate in processes established by Producer Responsibility Organization(s) registered with the Resource Productivity Recovery Authority, and/or their designate.

title: Standard of Care Training Course for Members of City Council
topics: councillors, drinking water standards, workplace training and development; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, continuous learning; corporate learning; employee development; employee training; job training and development; learning maps; learning plan; occupational training; on the job training; professional development; retraining at work; skills development in the workplace; staff development; staff training; training and development at work; work-based learning, maximum acceptable concentration; potable water standards
brief: The purpose of this report is to provide information concerning the responsibilities of members of City Council under the Province of Ontario's Safe Drinking Water Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Safe Drinking Water Act"), in particular the statutory Standard of Care provision, which came into force on December 31, 2012. This report also provides additional information regarding the City of Toronto Drinking Water Licence, Permit and Accreditation requirements and their historical context. The General Manager, Toronto Water recommends that City Council authorize the General Manager, Toronto Water to hire the Walkerton Clean Water Centre to provide the Standard of Care training course for all members of Toronto City Council at a cost of approximately $2,050.00 net of all taxes and charges ($2.

title: Park People 2023 National Urban Parks Conference - Host City Partner
topics: [environmental events], conferences, urban forestry; conference travel, forestry; tree health
brief: Park People, a Toronto-based national registered charity focused on urban parks, would like to collaborate with the City of Toronto as Host City Partner in order to deliver the National Urban Parks Conference in June 2023. This report outlines anticipated host city obligations and seeks authority to work with Park People as Host City Partner. The General Manager of Parks, Forestry and Recreation recommends that City Council authorize the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to negotiate and sign on behalf of the City an agreement with Park People, a Toronto-based registered charity.

title: F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Don Valley Parkway Closure - Bike for Brain Health
topics: cycling, highways, road closures; bicycling, freeways; motorways; parkways, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: The purpose of this report is to request City Council approval to close the F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Don Valley Parkway on the Sundays of June 4, 2023, June 2, 2024 and June 1, 2025 for the purpose of the Bike for Brain Health event in support of the Baycrest Foundation. The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends that City Council authorize the closure of the F.G. Gardiner Expressway, from the Humber River to the Don Valley Parkway, including all ramps, and the Don Valley Parkway, from the F.G. Gardiner Expressway to York Mills Road, including all ramps, on the Sundays of June 4, 2023, June 2.

title: Cycling Network Plan: 2021 ActiveTO Cycling Network Expansion Project Updates
topics: cycling, projects; bicycling
brief: In December 2021, City Council adopted the Cycling Network Plan and the associated 2022-2024 Near-Term Implementation Plan, which seeks to build on the existing network of cycling routes to Connect gaps in the current network, Grow the network into new parts of the city, and Renew existing parts of the network to improve safety. This report provides an update on the progress of the Cycling Network Near-Term Implementation Program (2022 to 2024) including an outline of three major projects planned for 2023. The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends that City Council approve the ActiveTO Yonge Street Cycling Network Expansion project installed in 2021 currently in place as permanent and in doing so, authorize the necessary by-law amendments to retain the following locations as a permanent installation.

title: Construction Staging Area Time Extension - 75 Broadway Avenue
topics: construction, transportation; building, transportation services
brief: This report is submitted to Infrastructure and Environment Committee as Broadway Avenue forms a shared boundary between the Toronto and East York Community Council and the North York Community Council. Hazelview Investments is constructing one 38-storey residential rental tower at 73 Broadway Avenue that will be connected to the remaining portion of 75 Broadway Avenue through the common first-floor and underground parking. The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends that City Council authorize the continuation of the closure south sidewalk and a 2.7 metre-wide portion of the westbound south-side curb lane on Broadway Avenue, between a point 71.5 metres west of Redpath Avenue and a point 40.5 metres further west, from March 1, 2023 to June 30, 2025.

title: Construction Staging Area Time Extension - 100-120 Broadway Avenue
topics: construction, transportation; building, transportation services
brief: This report is submitted to Infrastructure and Environment Committee as Broadway Avenue forms a shared boundary between the Toronto and East York Community Council and the North York Community Council. Reserve Properties Limited is constructing 33 and 21 level condominium towers, and a 36 level rental tower on the north side of Broadway Avenue, between Redpath Avenue and Mount Pleasant Road. The General Manager, Transportation Services recommends that City Council authorize the continuation of the closure of the east sidewalk and a 1.6 metre-wide portion of the northbound lane on Redpath Avenue, between Broadway Avenue and a point 74 metres north, from February 8, 2023 to August 31, 2024.

title: Feasibility Report on a Pilot Project to Demonstrate Solar Powered Smart Compacting Garbage and Recycling Bins
topics: recycling containers, renewable energy; green energy; green power, recycling bins
brief: Councillor Colle recommends that City Council ask the General Manager of Solid Waste Management Services, with the Economic Development and Culture Division, to report back to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee by the third quarter of 2023 on the feasibility of a pilot project using solar powered smart compacting garbage and recycling bins. The motion responds to long-standing complaints that the City's public bins are poorly maintained and often overflowing.

title: Regarding the Gardiner East Project
brief: This is an information item: an administrative inquiry submitted under Municipal Code Section 27-7.11 asks staff for the current status and updated cost estimate of the Gardiner East 'hybrid' rebuild. A 2016 staff report estimated the Hybrid 3 option, which Council chose, at $1.053 billion in 2013 dollars ($1.31 billion in 2022 dollars), and a City spokesperson confirmed in October 2022 that only $500 million in contracts had been committed. No decision is attached; the item seeks updated figures.

title: Cold weather and the effects on those experiencing homelessness
topics: emergency housing, extreme cold alerts, persons who are homeless, warming centres; cold alerts; extreme cold weather alerts, emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless), homeless; homeless individuals
brief: The City of Toronto is facing a sharp increase in the number of people experiencing homelessness. Toronto's shelter system is unable to support the number of residents in need, placing extra pressures on the city's drop-in and warming centres. Councillor Ausma Malik, Councillor Alejandra Bravo, and Councillor Gord Perks recommends that City Council direct the Medical Officer of Health to establish a working table, including physicians, medical experts who work with people experiencing homelessness, and people with lived experience.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract to Repair a Sanitary Sewer within an Easement Between Ridge Drive and Carstowe Road
topics: budgets, repairs, wastewater; budgets and accounts, sanitary sewage; sewage; waste water
brief: This is an information item: The purpose of this report is to advise Toronto City Council, pursuant to Chapter 195 of the Toronto Municipal Code (Purchasing By-Law, Section 195-7.4), of a non-competitive contract with 614128 Ontario Ltd. o/a Trisan Construction. Emergency general contracting and construction services were required to replace a collapsed sewer main by directional drill method within an easement located between Ridge Drive and Carstowe Road in the amount of $2,095,723 net of all applicable taxes and charges ($2,132,608 net of HST recoveries). City Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract to Repair a Sanitary Sewer and Storm Sewer in the North Park Creek Crossing
topics: sanitary sewers, storm sewers; stormwater sewers
brief: This is an information item: The purpose of this report is to advise Toronto City Council, pursuant to Chapter 195 of the Toronto Municipal Code (Purchasing By-law, Section 195-7.4), of a non-competitive contract with Aqua Tech Solutions Inc. brief: Toronto is home to a number of world-class, publicly-funded post-secondary institutions and plays host to over 100,000 students from around the world. brief: City Council on July 19, 20, 21 and 22, 2022, referred Motion MM47.55 to the Economic and Community Development Committee.
